articleTitle: Characterization of Isotactic-Polypropylene-Based Compounds for HVDC Cable Insulation
abstract: This paper aims at a preliminary characterization of isotactic-polypropylene-based blends as a candidate to be used for High-Voltage Direct Current HVDC cable insulation in the framework of the European project NEWGEN (New GENeration of HVDC insulating materials, cables and systems). Isotactic-polypropylene (i-PP) is blended with various propylene-based elastomers (PBEs) and heterophasic PP random copolymers (HECO) with different percentages. Results show that, compared to XLPE, i-PP blends have a comparable breakdown strength, but higher DC conductivity. Noticeable space charge accumulation is observed in the i-PP blends. TSDC measurements show that i-PP blends are characterized by two great peaks (that attribute shallow and deep traps) compared to only one deep-trap peak in the XLPE.

articleTitle: Screening of Suitable Random Copolymer Polypropylene Blends for HVDC Cable Insulation
abstract: Polypropylene (PP) based thermoplastics offer an interesting alternative over cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) for extruded HVDC cable insulation. In this study, a set of PP random copolymer-based blends are screened by dielectric characterizations (dielectric breakdown strength, space charge, thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC), polarization/conductivity) in order to find the most promising blend systems for HVDC cable insulation. Moreover, thermomechanical properties of the PP blends are evaluated to ensure suitability for cable insulation applications. The blends show similar or slightly improved breakdown strength but clearly lower field enhancement factor in space charge measurements when compared to a fully degassed XLPE reference material. The TSDC measurements reveal the possibility to optimize the trapping behavior by varying the blend composition. Thus, the best blend formulations offer promising performance for further HVDC insulation development. After this screening phase, the best blend alternatives will be taken to pilot-scale production level with sample extrusion and for further HVDC insulation material development and optimization.

articleTitle: Effect of Temperature on Charge Mobility in Oil-Paper Insulation
abstract: Oil-paper insulation serves as the primary insulation material for converter transformers. In the converter transformer, intricate electrical stresses and complex temperature distribution coexist. To achieve accurate calculation of the electric field distribution of insulation structures under various conditions, it is crucial to comprehend the effect of temperature on the charge transport. In this work, the charge mobility in oil-immersed paper at different temperatures is measured using a newly proposed method based on pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method. Utilizing epoxy as the blocking material, a double-layer structure with one blocking layer is constructed to establish a unipolar injection condition. The mobility of negative and positive charges in oil-immersed paper is calculated based on the charge distributions of the double-layer sample under various applied voltages. For the oil-immersed samples composed of mineral insulating oil and cellulose insulating paper used in our work, the charge mobility increases with increasing electric field and increasing temperature. The relationship between charge mobility and temperature conforms to the Arrhenius equation, and the mobility activation energy of negative charge is higher than that of positive charge, indicating that the negative charge mobility is more dependent on temperature.

articleTitle: Influence of Support Insulators on the AC Electrical Strength of Parallel-Cylindrical Conductors in Liquid Nitrogen
abstract: In order to make superconducting high-voltage power cables more compact and easier to manufacture, it may be possible to dispense with solid electrical insulation and use liquid nitrogen (LN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) instead. LN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> has very good electrical properties. However, each phase conductor of a three-phase, LN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-insulated arrangement of such a cable must be kept at a distance from each other and from the surrounding earthed cryostat by means of a support insulator. In this work it is therefore investigated what influence different insulating materials have on the electrical strength. For this purpose, a simple straight model insulator of a support insulator was developed and manufactured from the materials PTFE, PP, PE, POM-C, and twice GRP and tested for their electrical flashover properties. In comparison to the breakdown properties of LN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the same test arrangement, most materials surprisingly showed the same or only slightly reduced electrical flashover strength. PE shows the best properties on average, followed by POM-C, PP, GRP EGS 102 and PTFE. The highest average reduction in electrical strength, at almost 26%, is caused by GRP G11.

articleTitle: Characterization of Structural and Dielectric Properties of Silicon Nitride Thin Films Deposited by PECVD
abstract: The structural and electrical properties of silicon nitride (SiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) are influenced by its composition ratio, x. In this study, we examine the characteristics of SiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> films, deposited by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), electron microprobe microscopy (EMP), ellipsometry, and high-voltage broadband dielectric spectroscopy (HVBDS). The film composition ranged from N-rich to Si-rich. The dependence of refractive index, permittivity, loss factor and AC conductivity on the SiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> ratio is presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement Limitations in Identifying Partial Discharges in Turn-Turn Insulation of Low-Voltage Induction Motors
abstract: This work aims to highlight limitations of measurement techniques when identifying partial discharges (PDs) in the turn-turn insulation of low-voltage induction motors. It has been observed in previous studies that different types of PDs exist. While the nomenclature of the authors varies, these types can be broadly classified into so-called “Townsend-like” and “streamer-like” PDs. The former are low amplitude slow rise time PD pulses and may thus be undetectable by common PD instruments. The present study extends previous investigations by identifying conditions which favor the formation of such Townsend-like PDs, illustrating the challenges associated with detecting such PDs, and showing that a prolonged exposure of an organic insulation material's surface to such PDs causes surface erosion. This emphasizes the potential importance of being able to detect this PD type between the thin turn-turn insulation of low-voltage induction motors.

articleTitle: Space Charge Deflection Behavior under Strong Magnetic Fields
abstract: In this paper, an experimental device is designed to characterize the asymmetric distribution of charges caused by the charge deflection under a magnetic field in the polypropylene (PP) dielectric. Under the magnetic field, the electric potential difference caused by the asymmetric distribution of charges appears on both sides of the sample. The potential difference increases with the enhancement of the magnetic field. The stronger electric field also promotes the accumulation of the asymmetric charges. In addition, the charge packet phenomenon is observed in this experiment. Increasing the magnetic field can accelerate the charge packets to reach the dynamic equilibrium, and the enhanced electric field drives the charge packet to move faster towards the opposite electrode.

articleTitle: Study on Breakdown of Dielectric Elastomer Generators during Energy Harvesting Process
abstract: The continuous development and application of dielectric elastomer materials has shown that they have great potential in the mutual conversion of electrical and mechanical energy. However, in the process of energy harvesting, electrical breakdown is one of the main failure modes that limit the lifespan of the dielectric elastomer generator (DEG). To clarify the effect of mechanical stretching on the dielectric strength of dielectric elastomer materials and the relationship between breakdown and tensile displacement during energy harvesting, in this paper, the energy harvesting process of DEG is studied and electrical breakdown events are observed under different conditions. It was found that the dielectric strength of the tested elastomers is greatly affected by their tensile state and the breakdown field strength increases with increasing strain. During the energy harvesting process, under constant charge conditions, the actual electric field strength in the material varies with strain. Furthermore, discharge phenomena are observed during strain relaxation, which greatly affects the dielectric properties of the dielectric elastomer.

articleTitle: Identification of Defect Type in an Aged 22 kV Cast Resin Transformer from Phase-Resolved PD Patterns
abstract: This paper presents identification of defect type in the insulation system of an aged 22 kV cast resin transformer (CRTr) from comparing phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) patterns with those in different electrode systems simulating various kinds of defects. Quantitative analysis of the PRPD patterns was performed using a measure of the difference between the two probability distributions, called the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence. Comparison of PRPD patterns using KL divergence value (KL-D) suggested the possibility that a defect type in the aged 22 kV CRTr was attributed to inter-layer voids. Furthermore, even for the PRPD pattern of CRTr, which had little apparent change over time, the value of KL-D increased with increasing cumulative application time tc. As a result, it can be said that KL divergence is a useful index in comparing PRPD patterns quantitatively.

articleTitle: Dependence of Self-Healing Arc on Metal Vaporization Contributions for Metallized Film Capacitor
abstract: Metallized film capacitor (MFC) bears high operation-reliability under high electric field, owing to the unique property of self-healing (SH). The SH process is always accompanied by the growth and extinction of arc, together with the evaporation of metal electrode. This paper established the three equivalent circuit models to visualize the abstract SH process. Moreover, a theoretical model based on charge quantity was constructed to study the dependence of SH arc on metal vaporization contributions for MFC under low electric field. The consequence of model and experiment shows that the aluminum vapor is ionized in the SH process that constantly provides charge to the arc. Moreover, the demetallized zone area is proportional to the voltage drop in the condition of breakdown of 1 layer of biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) and evaporation of two layers of metal electrodes above and below it.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of the DC Breakdown of a Sphere Gap due to a Weakly Nonuniform Electric Field
abstract: Understanding the breakdown (BD) characteristics of air gaps in different electrode systems is essential for insulation coordination. Modeling of the BD mechanism using drift-diffusion equations is proposed as an alternative to expensive and time-consuming experimental procedures to determine the BD strength. The 2D model of sphere gap (SG) with a diameter of 100 mm is modeled in COMSOL Multiphysics, and the plasma hydrodynamic equations are solved for different gap spacings. The formation of electron avalanches and transition of the avalanche to the streamer are analyzed. The variation in electron density from the initial avalanche to the final streamer and the variation in the electric field due to space charges are also discussed. The predicted breakdown voltages (BDV s) are validated using experimental results.

articleTitle: Effect of Elastomer Blend on High Temperature Dielectric Properties of Polypropylene
abstract: This paper presents investigation on dielectric properties of polypropylene (PP), binary blend (iPP/EOC=4.4:5.6), and ternary blend 1 (iPP/EOC/PPC=4:5:1), and ternary blend2 (iPP/EOC/PPC=3.6/4.6/1.8) at high temperatures up to 150°C. EOC and PPC stand for ethylene-octene copolymers and EPR dispersed in PP, respectively. The relative complex permittivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{\bm{\varepsilon }}}_{\bm{r}}}^{\bm{*}} = \varepsilon_{r}^{\prime} - {\bm{j}}\varepsilon_{r}^{\prime\prime}$</tex> and AC conductivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{\bm{\sigma }}}_{{\bm{ac}}}}$</tex> were measured in a temperature range from 30°C to 150°C at frequencies from 1 Hz to 10 kHz. Experimental results revealed that the real part <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{r}^{\prime}$</tex>of the relative permittivity of all kinds of material decreased with increasing temperature, though pristine PP exhibited a smallest decrease in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{r}^{\prime}$</tex>with temperature. While the imaginary part <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{r}^{\prime\prime}$</tex> exhibited a linear decrease with the frequency in the log vs log plot below 1 kHz and above 100°C for binary blend, ternary blend1 and 2. The results indicate that the EOC addition to PP is contributed to the increase in the complex permittivity. It was also found that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{\bm{\sigma }}}_{{\bm{ac}}}}$</tex> of binary blend, ternary blend1, and 2 remained constant below 1 kHz and above 110°C, while <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{{\bm{\sigma }}}_{{\bm{ac}}}}$</tex> of all the samples increased proportionally with frequency above 1 kHz. The calculated activation energies derived from the temperature dependence of the DC conductivity of binary blend, ternary blend 1, and ternary blend 2 were 0.602, 0.849, and 0.791 eV, respectively, with ternary blend 1 having the largest activation energy. Ternary blend 1 with the largest value was considered the most likely to inhibit carrier transport.

articleTitle: Surface Discharges Inception & Flashover of Solid Insulating Materials with Homogeneous and Inhomogeneous Electrical Fields for Aeronautical Applications
abstract: High voltage (> 1 kV) requirements in aerospace applications have raised concerns over the insulation and safety of the interconnected systems. With short gaps, the compact-sized connectors will experience higher electric field stress, resulting in increased discharge activities. Although surface discharges on insulators in dry/contaminated states have been studied for a long time, but this subject has not been comprehensively covered in existing research works in the aerospace domain. The aim is therefore to investigate the surface discharge behavior of a solid dielectric at varying pressures considering the aircraft flying altitudes. An experimental study was conducted by considering the effect of both air pressure and electrode geometry on surface partial discharge inception and flashover voltage. The experimental data were compared with Paschen's curve of air breakdown and IEC 60664-1 recommended values.

articleTitle: Multi-Point Vibration Monitoring of Power Transformer Based on Optical Fiber Sensing System
abstract: Vibration signal analysis is an effective method to diagnose mechanical condition of transformers online. A multi-point vibration sensing system phase-sensitive optical time domain reflectometer (φ-OTDR) is proposed for transformer tank vibration monitoring. Compared with piezoelectric accelerometers commonly used in the field, the proposed system has high electromagnetic interference immunity and complexing ability. In this paper, the vibration sensing principle based on φ-OTDR is first introduced. Then, an optical fiber sensor for transformer tank vibration is proposed. Next, the vibration sensing performance of the system is calibrated experimentally. Finally, vibration monitoring tests are carried out online on a 500 kV transformer, verifying the accuracy and comprehensiveness of the proposed system for transformer vibration monitoring.

articleTitle: Humidity Impact on Streamer Inception Parameters for Turn-to-Turn Insulation of Inverter-Fed Motors
abstract: This study explores the impact of varying relative humidity (RH) levels (30%-90%) at 90°C on streamer inception parameters (SIPs) compared to those at 25°C. Schumann's streamer inception criterion (SCSIC) is used to assess the vulnerability of turn-to-turn insulation in inverter-fed motors with rising humidity at 90°C. The analysis includes SIPs such as effective ionization coefficient of air (α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>), partial discharge (PD) inception field (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">inc</inf>), critical field line length (CFLL), and firing voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">firing</inf>). Furthermore, this study emphasizes the humidity-dependent shift in the Schumann constant (i.e., the natural logarithm of the critical electron number that determines the Townsend-to-streamer discharge transition, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>) from 25°C to 90°C and advises caution when using the derived <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> at room temperature (e.g., 25°C) to predict PDIV at higher temperatures (e.g., 90°C), especially when RH≥50%.

articleTitle: Dielectric Model of Polarization Mechanisms in Time Domain Field Simulation Including Temperature Dependence
abstract: The voltage distribution in an insulating system depends on the geometry and the permittivity of the applied dielectrics. The permittivity is frequency and temperature dependent. Understanding this dependence is important for the design of renewable energy sources and electric vehicles, in whose application both large temperature fluctuations and pulsed voltages occur. This work proposes a macroscopic approach to model dielectric materials in time domain FEM simulations based on broadband dielectric spectroscopy. The model is used to investigate the effect of voltage shape and temperature on the electric field strength in polymer dielectrics.

articleTitle: Increase in Electrical Resistance of Rubber-Containing Epoxy Resin by Heat and Radiation
abstract: Rubber-containing soft epoxy resin, used as potting material in nuclear power plants, must exhibit good electrical insulation performance. Various simultaneous treatments with heat and gamma-ray irradiation were given to this resin, and leakage current, space charge distribution, glass transition temperature, elongation-at-break, and tensile strength were measured. It has become clear that the simultaneous treatment remarkably reduces the leakage current of the resin. This is because exposure to heat and radiation hardens the resin, inhibiting electrical conduction. Therefore, there is no need to worry excessively about resin aging.

articleTitle: Trap Spectroscopy from the Dielectric Isothermal Step Response: Theory and Simulations
abstract: The isothermal response of a dielectric subjected to a DC field or to an initial charge deposit is in a large part governed by charge trapping in progressively deeper levels. The distribution of the traps in energy may therefore be deduced from the absorption current, or from the potential decay. The general theoretical problem is described here in the frame of multiple trapping theory, illustrated by simple simulations. The limits of a commonly used simplification using the demarcation energy are underlined, and suggestions are made to apply more sophisticated techniques.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Partial Discharge Measurements for Artificial Defects under HVAC and HVDC Voltage Stresses for Cable Insulating Materials
abstract: In the last decade there has been a growing adoption of HVDC cable systems especially for power transmission over long distances. However, during the manufacturing and commissioning processes, HVDC cables are usually subjected to quality control testing using Partial Discharge (PD) measurements under AC voltage stress. The main challenge in DC PD measurement, compared to AC, lies in the absence of a phase reference, which complicates noise rejection and PD source identification. In this paper, to deepen the knowledge of PD characteristics under DC stresses, a comparative analysis of test results under AC and DC conditions will be presented. The tests have been performed on different PD defects (i.e. internal, surface, and corona), using various solid insulating materials and test conditions. The test procedure, the manufacturing of PD samples, and the obtained results will be discussed. Additionally, the analysis of statistical parameters and peculiarity behaviors derived from Time-Resolved PD (TRPD) patterns will be proposed.

articleTitle: Study on Partial Discharge Characteristics of Dielectric Films for Metallized Film Capacitors
abstract: This paper investigates the partial discharge (PD) characteristics of biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films and metallized films based on the actual structure of metallized film capacitors. The PD inception voltage of metallized films is 30.2% lower than that of BOPP films due to the uneven voltage distribution along the films. Under the low electric field, the internal discharge occurs in the gaps between films. Under the high electric field, the surface discharge is more intensive. And the equivalent frequency of PD in metallized films can reach 15 MHz, surpassing that of BOPP films. Additionally, as the voltage increases, the phase distribution of PD in metallized films is more extensive with a lower phase correlation of the PD repetition rate. However, the average PD amplitude decreases. The complex nature of the PD is facilitated by the migration and accumulation of surface charge generated by previous PDs at the margin of metallized films, leading to distortion of the electric field. This is an essential element of metal electrodes loss near the margin leading to the reduction in capacitance. This paper aims to provide a theoretical basis for refining the capacitance loss mechanism of metallized film capacitors.

articleTitle: Effects of Low Temperature on the Thermal Stress Distribution of GIS Cable Termination
abstract: In recent years, there are many GIS termination failures occur at low temperature. The breakdown of epoxy bushing is one of the main features. It is inferred that the operation condition of epoxy bushing has changed at low temperature, but its evolution process is unclear. In order to explore the evolution process, simulation model of a 110kV GIS cable terminal based on COMSOL is established, and the thermal stress distribution in epoxy bushing at different temperatures is simulated. It is found that, with temperature decreases, the difference in thermal expansion coefficients of the materials results in stress concentration at the metal insert/epoxy interface, as well as increased tensile stress along the direction of the electric field in the epoxy bushing. At -40 °C, the thermal stress is concentrated at the metal insert, where defects are easy to occur. Moreover, due to the assembly constraints of GIS terminations, there is a transition from compression stress to tensile stress in the epoxy bushing at low temperatures. This transition further distorts the stress distribution, resulting in defects and further leading to insulation deterioration.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Measurement During Interfacial Tracking Degradation Under 50 Hz Voltage Excitation
abstract: Modern high-voltage solid insulation is a system of multiple dielectric layers of different properties brought together to provide the best stress relief. Thus, understanding the degradation in interfaces of these layers, is essential for assessing the dielectric performance of the insulation system. This paper focuses on the interfacial degradation of SiR-SiR under AC stress using Partial Discharge (PD) measurement to assess the mechanism and its visual characterisation. Results from this work will aid in understanding the propagation of interfacial tracks, especially around stress grading in HV assets. This study used coplanar needle-plane geometry to analyse the degradation of solid dielectric interfaces. SiR sheets were pressed together using transparent acrylic plates and nylon bolts, which were tightened using a torque wrench to control the contact pressure. After five hours of testing at 12 kV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</inf> 50 Hz, the tests showed electrical degradation in the material's surface (tracking) and the bulk (treeing) with extensions between 444 µm and 817 µm, depending on the sample and its pressure. These results suggested that the contact pressure affects how the degradation develops at the interface.

articleTitle: Application of a Reference Method for the Training and Evaluation of PD Analysts
abstract: Currently, electrical company users of PD measuring systems face the difficulty of the lack of procedures, for the training and evaluation of their technicians' analytical capabilities. This same difficulty must be also afforded by companies developers of PD measuring systems technology. In this paper a benchmark method, useful for the comprehensive training and evaluation of PD analysts in a technically and economically feasible way, is presented. This method is focused on the issues faced by technicians of this field in real-life PD measurements and analysis. Various evaluation tests are proposed in the method, with which the technicians are challenged with practical cases of analysis. The measurements to be analyzed are related to real experiences when HFCT sensors are used. A practical example of the method application is presented, showing its effectiveness for the training and evaluation of PD analysts' capabilities.

articleTitle: Methodology for MD Simulation and Estimation of Material Properties of Cross-Linked Epoxy Resin
abstract: Dielectric materials play a crucial role in various technological applications ranging from electronic devices to insulation of power apparatus. Understanding the dielectricity of materials at a molecular level is essential in tailoring novel materials for new applications. In this context, computational tools like Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations are useful. This study aims to study and outline an effective methodology for MD based estimation of the dielectric constant (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\varepsilon _r}$</tex>) of cross-linked epoxy resin, along with the estimation of density and glass transition temperature (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${T_g}$</tex>). Two different approaches for computation of the dielectric constant viz. the External Field (EF) method and Fluctuation Dipole (FD) method are used and compared in terms of their effectiveness. Issues in MD simulations that affect the accuracy of the estimates are discussed. Simulation results are validated against experimental data from the authors’ laboratory. The outcome of this study enables modeling of a dielectric at the nano-metric level and opens up the possibility of understanding and modifying nanodielectric properties.

articleTitle: Impact of Particle Thermal Treatment on Dielectric Properties of Core-Shell Filled Epoxy Nano-composites
abstract: This paper presents the effect of Silica-Titania <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{SiO}_{2}{@}\mathbf{TiO}_{2})$</tex> core-shell nano-particles added into amine-cured epoxy composites, under three different particle treatment conditions: untreated, calcined at 250 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$</tex> and 450 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\circ}{\mathbf{C}}$</tex>, on the dielectric and structural properties of the bulk composite. Characterization was conducted using a range of methods Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Fourier}$</tex> Transform Infra-Red Spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman Spectroscopy, Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and Broadband Dielectric Spectroscopy (BDS). TEM confirmed the synthesis of the core-shell architecture with denser shells at higher calcination temperatures. Raman spectroscopy showed an increase in the Ti-O-Ti network formation and orderliness with elevated temperature treatment. Incorporating untreated filler into epoxy reduces the bulk real permittivity, while the inclusion of calcined fillers leads to an increase. An additional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega$</tex> relaxation was observed in imaginary permittivity spectra of nano-composites pointing towards altered molecular dynamics within the epoxy due to nano-particle addition. These findings highlight the role of core-shell nano-particles in modifying the dielectric properties of epoxy composites, whilst differentiating them from conventional nano-particles.

articleTitle: Effect of Stretching Temperature on the Breakdown Performance of Long-chain Branched Polypropylene Films for HVDC Capacitors
abstract: The purpose of this article is to study the effect of stretching temperature on the microstructure as well as dielectric breakdown property of long chain branched polypropylene (LCBPP) film and facilitate the industrial application of polypropylene-based dielectric materials. With the increase of stretching temperature, the stress-induced crystallization effect is strengthened, which increases the crystallinity of the stretched sample and helps to limit the movement of carriers. However, as the stretching temperature rises, the trap density and energy level decreases. During biaxial stretching, the appropriate stretching temperature is pivotal to achieve the best breakdown property of LCBPP film. The results show that under the test temperature of 115 °C, the breakdown strength and conductivity of LCBPP film stretched at 165 °C are significantly higher than those of pure polypropylene (PP), which increases by 27.5% and 87.6% respectively.

articleTitle: Effect of the Bending Radius on the Breakdown Strength of Rectangular PAI/PEEK Insulated Winding Wire of Electric Motors
abstract: The high efficiency and mass production of electric motors for e-mobility solutions raised the hairpin technology in motor manufacturing. The reliability of these machines depends on the insulation quality of the windings, which can be investigated by the breakdown test of winding wires according to existing standards. In this study, two groups of U-shaped samples prepared from rectangular wire covered with double-layer polyamide-imide (PAI) and polyetheretherketone (PEEK) insulation were prepared with 25 mm and 50 mm bending diameters. The samples were tested by 50 Hz A.C. progressive stress. The results show that the breakdown voltage of the sample group with a smaller bending diameter is significantly lower than that of samples with a greater bending diameter. The result of the study shows that the breakdown voltage of rectangular cross-section conductors with layered insulation is very sensitive to the bending radius. This affects the long-term reliability of rotating machines wounded with hairpin technology.

articleTitle: Cable Defects Location Method Based on M-sequence with Broadband Impedance Spectroscopy
abstract: This paper suggests a method for locating cable defects using M-sequence with Broadband Impedance Spectroscopy (BIS). In this paper, the principles of M-sequence signal generation and noise reduction by cross-correlation algorithm are introduced. A platform has been constructed for the thermal aging and BIS measurement of 10 kV cable samples. Local thermal aging defects with different aging temperatures and times were introduced in the cable samples. The measured BIS data were analyzed using M-sequence and IFFT methods. Results indicate a notable decrease in noise levels in the positioning waveforms generated using the M-sequence method, with a more pronounced reflection peak at the defective point. The peak reflection of a defect caused by local thermal aging in the positioning waveform is bimodal, indicating variations in the distributed capacitance at the specific thermal aging point of the cable. The defect is located at the midpoint of the reflection peak. The reflection peak's amplitude rises with longer aging time and higher temperature.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Tree Growth under Electrical and Mechanical Stresses
abstract: Epoxy insulators in gas-insulated power apparatus are subjected to the combined effects of electrical and mechanical loads. In this study, a simulation model is built based on the energy theory to explore the electrical tree growth of epoxy resin under tensile and compressive stresses. With increasing AC voltage, the electrical tree growth is promoted, exhibiting a morphology with more branches. Tensile stress accelerates the electrical tree growth, while proper compressive stress has the opposite effect. However, when the compressive stress exceeds a certain value, electrical tree growth is promoted again. When the mechanical stress is vertical to the needle electrode, these effects primarily impact the length of the trees. Conversely, in parallel cases, mechanical stress mainly affects the width of the electrical trees. The electrical tree morphologies of simulation and experiment are in good consistency, proving the reasonability of the simulation model.

articleTitle: A Portable, Non-Invasive and Non-Destructive Technique for Condition Assessment of Liquid Insulation
abstract: Liquid insulation plays a vital role as an insulant and coolant in transformers. It provides detailed information about the condition of the transformers. Numerous testing methodologies and equipment are available to evaluate the physiochemical and electrical properties of the liquid insulation. In their previous work, the authors presented a non-invasive and non-destructive technique for condition assessment of mineral oil. This work focuses on making the technique portable and extending it to alternate insulating oils such as nanofluids, ester, and blended oils. It also discusses the limitations of its application to nanofluids. The average errors in the prediction of moisture and acid number for blended oils are found to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$11.53{\rm{\% }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.26{\rm{\% }}$</tex>, respectively. This handy, portable and fast condition assessment module for insulating oils will be helpful for utilities in on-site testing.

articleTitle: Development Process of Electrical Arc Movement on Ice-covered HVDC Outdoor Insulators
abstract: This study concentrates on the dynamics of electrical arcs on ice-accreted outdoor insulators under DC voltage, essential for ensuring the reliability of electrical grids in extreme icy conditions. Employing a comprehensive methodology that combines ice accretion experiments, theoretical analysis, and simulation modeling, the research aims to explore the characteristics and attenuation mechanisms of arc formation and development. Key findings include the effective characterization of arc formation, development, and pre-flashover dynamics under DC voltage, particularly noting intensified discharge activities under negative DC voltage. Furthermore, the study establishes a quantitative relationship between arc burning time, leakage current, and arc parameters, identifying distinct contact-type and non-contact-type arc attenuation mechanisms. These insights not only enhance the understanding of flashover mechanisms on iced insulators but also contribute significantly to improving their operational reliability in harsh environments.

articleTitle: Effect of Gamma-ray Irradiation on Ageing of LDPE Micro/Nanocomposites Estimated by DCIC Method
abstract: With the rapid development of nuclear power technology, the safety of electrical equipment in nuclear power plants (NPP) has received widespread attention. NPPs are exposed to extreme environments with gamma-ray irradiation for long periods, which can lead to the deterioration of insulation. In order to ensure the safe and stable operation of NPPs, it is necessary to accurately evaluate the ageing status of cable insulation. The direct current integral charge (DCIC-Q(t)) method is a non-destructive detection method that can evaluate the degree of charge accumulation in materials. In this paper, the LDPE and LDPE/BN/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> composites were prepared and irradiated with gamma-ray at different total doses. The charge characteristics of LDPE and composites were investigated based on the DCIC-Q(t) method. The ratio of charges was proposed as a basis for judging the irradiation ageing state of the materials. The changes in the microstructure of the materials before and after ageing were analyzed using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), and the correlation between Q(t) and microstructure was established. The results showed that with the increase of irradiation dose, the charge ratio of LDPE showed a trend of slight increase and then rapid increase; the composites with added micro-nanoparticles can inhibit the injection and accumulation of charge.

articleTitle: Dielectric Performance of Sustainable Fluids
abstract: Early studies discovered that the streamer breakdown voltage and breakdown acceleration voltage in selected ester fluids were lower than those in mineral oil (MO) in a nonuniform electric field under lightning impulse voltage [1]. In the present work, the dielectric performance of sustainable fluids (e.g., synthetic esters, natural esters, and isoparaffinic oils) was systematically investigated and compared with MO. Five types of electrode configurations (viz., needleplane, needle-sphere, plate-plate, a U-type geometry, and a turnturn-turn model) were introduced to understand further the features of streamers and breakdown. The permittivity, dissipation factor, and resistivity of fluids were measured and compared at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${90^ \circ }\mathrm{C}$</tex> from 0.001 to 10000 Hz . Cole-Cole plots were drawn at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20{\;^ \circ }\mathrm{C}$</tex> from 0.00001 to 10000 Hz for the first time in seeking the possible mechanisms of polarization. Breakdown voltage and the locations of breakdown in a transformer-like turn-to-turn geometry were recorded and analyzed under AC voltage and a chopped-impulse voltage. The investigations enable us to achieve a sustainable insulating system for the potential application in the next generation of HV transformers.

articleTitle: Breakdown Characteristics of Insulating Oil in Uniform to Non-uniform Electric Field under AC Voltage
abstract: It is imperative that insulation designers understand breakdown voltage (BDV). BDV of transformer oil are generally understood to follow stressed oil volume (SOV) theory. However, estimating more than 90% stressed oil volume in non-uniform electric fields in a transformer is extremely time consuming. Therefore, we propose a prediction formula that can estimate the BDV of insulating oil easily. In this study, the breakdown characteristics of insulating oil were investigated in a non-uniform electric field under AC voltage application. Experimental results were obtained with those several bare electrodes and oil gap lengths. As a result, it was derived that a prediction formula represented by √UE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> =25.3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">•0.28</sup> in the mineral oil and ester oil. It was also confirmed that experimental results matched to the prediction curve and could easily estimate the breakdown voltage.

articleTitle: Electret Charge Stability and Thermomechanical Properties of Polypropylene Blends with Ethylene-Methyl Acrylate Copolymer
abstract: Electret charge stability has been studied by means of thermally stimulated surface potential decay (TSSPD) for a series of polypropylene homopolymer blends with an ethylene methyl acrylate random copolymer. Charge decay has been investigated in heat-pressed thin films for both positive and negative polarities. It has been found that the electret charge stability was quite sensitive to the copolymer content in the blend ratios investigated. However, above 2 wt% polar copolymer content the charge decay pattern does not substantially change any further. Charge polarity only has a limited effect on the surface potential decay. Flexural modulus has been determined via three-point bending tests at ambient temperature while the evolution of the flexural modulus with temperature has been determined by dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). Charpy impact tests confirm the increased impact resistance with increasing ethylene copolymer content. Calorimetric measurements have been performed with dynamic scanning calorimetry (DSC) to support the interpretation of charge decay measurements and to assess the sample morphology in pressed thin films.

articleTitle: PDIV and AC Breakdown Behavior of Magnet Wire in Different Embedded Media
abstract: Growing electrification and advancements in technology are driving the demand for electric motors. As a result, more research and development is required in many areas, including testing techniques. The purpose of this work is to examine the breakdown voltage and PDIV of magnet wire in order to determine if it may be utilized as winding insulation in electric motors. Another aim is to investigate the influence of the two embedded media on the PDIV and breakdown voltage, and to determine whether the measurement method using the medium of water is a simple method for investigation. As a result, measurements according to the standard and those made in ambient medium water were compared.

articleTitle: Electric Field-assisted Preparation of Anisotropic BNNw/SiR Composites for Thermal Management
abstract: Enhancing the thermal conductivity of insulation materials in high-capacity electrical equipment and highly integrated circuits can significantly improve the operational efficiency and lifespan of the devices. Establishing a phonon propagation pathway is a critical factor in enhancing the thermal conductivity of composite insulation materials. Traditionally, the reliance on random filler dispersion presents challenges related to a high percolation threshold and potential detrimental effects on mechanical and insulating properties. This work investigates the dielectric and thermal properties of BN nano whiskers / silicone rubber (BNNWs/SiR) composites prepared with electric field assistance. The dielectric spectrum data demonstrate the oriented self-assembly of BNNWs under the electric field. The thermal conductivity of the composites in the direction of the assisted electric field is enhanced with the filler content and assisted electric field strength. Compared to pure SiR, the out-plane thermal conductivity increased from 0.16 W/m·K to 0.37 W/m·K with only 8wt% filler and 24 V/mm/10 kHz assisted electric field lasting for 0.5h. The out-of-plane orientation of BNNWs would reduce the in-plane thermal conductivity. Therefore, for different thermal management scenarios, the degree of anisotropy of the thermal conductivity of the material should be modulated, thus optimizing the heat dissipation effect of the target device.

articleTitle: Effect of Mechanical Pressure on Interface Charges of Double-Layer Cross-Linked Polyethylene
abstract: Space charges exist at the interface between high voltage direct current (HVDC) cables and factory joints, both made of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE). The interface condition is closely related to the mechanical stress during the manufacture process of factory joints. In this paper, the space charge distributions in double-layer XLPE samples made at different pressures were measured using the pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method. Subsequently, the electric field distortions caused by these interface charges are analyzed. Experimental results indicate that increasing the pressure applied to the double-layer sample can reduce the accumulation of interface charges and mitigate the associated electric field distortion. Furthermore, the transport mechanism of interface charges under different pressure conditions is elucidated. This paper provides valauble guidance for the design and application of factory joints in HVDC systems.

articleTitle: Effects of Chemical Grafting on the Dielectric Properties of Aramid Fiber Reinforced Composites
abstract: In this paper, polyethyleneimine (PEI) with abundant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\text{NH}_{2}$</tex> groups is grafted onto the surface of aramid fibers after surface activation by plasma pretreatment, and aramid fiber reinforced epoxy composite (AFRC) samples are prepared to research their dielectric properties. The results indicate that PEI is successfully grafted onto the aramid fiber surface. The interfacial shear strength increased from 29.5 MPa to 63.7 MPa, demonstrate ng an enhancement in interfacial bonding strength. The dielectric properties of the composite material, including DC conductivity, dielectric constant, and breakdown strength, are improved, attributed to the reduced interface polarization and increased interface bonding strength. This research provides a scientific basis for improving the performance of AFRC for insulation rods used in gas insulated switchgear (GIS).

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Pressure on Breakdown and Electrode Loss Behavior of Metallized Polypropylene Films
abstract: Owing to the property of self-healing, metalized film capacitors can be reliably used under high electric field. However, self-healing is at the expense of capacitance loss. High interlayer pressure is often promoted to reduce the capacitance loss. Research has shown that an increase in interlayer pressure can lead to a decrease in the breakdown field and self-healing area of the metallized film, and the impact of the two on capacitor performance is opposite. Therefore, further analysis is necessary. a metallized film breakdown platform was established. The breakdown probability distribution of the metallized film under different pressures were studied. Based on the experimental results of breakdown field and self-healing area, the loss area of capacitor electrode under different electrical field and pressure was calculated. The breakdown characteristics of metallized polypropylene film under the pressure of 20kPa - 1MPa were studied. The breakdown field of the metallized film decreases significantly with the increase of pressure. When the pressure exceeds 200kPa, the influence of pressure on the breakdown electrical field shows a saturation trend. There are two opposite effects of pressure on the capacitance loss of metallized film capacitors. Through theoretical calculation, it is found that the electrode loss increases with the increase of pressure under low electric field. But the electrode loss is very small at this time. The great electrode loss under high electric field can be inhibited by increasing the pressure. Therefore, increasing the interlayer pressure to a certain extent is beneficial to the reliability of the capacitor.

articleTitle: Effect of Gamma-Ray Irradiation on Dielectric Properties of PP/Elastomer/TiO2 Nanocomposite
abstract: This article focuses on electrical properties and microstructure of polypropylene (PP)/elastomer/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanocomposites for cable insulation in nuclear power plants (NPPs). The nanocomposite comprising isotactic PP, 30 wt% propylene-based elastomer (PBE) and 3 wt% nano-TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, undergoes <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co gamma-ray irradiation with doses ranging from 0 to 250 kGy. Electrical conductivities at different temperatures and trap distributions are measured. The obtained results indicate that the addition of nano-TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> can significantly improve the electrical properties of the PP/PBE composite, characterized by reduced conductivities and increased trap depths, and these improvements persist with irradiation. As the irradiation dose increases to 250 kGy, the electrical conductivities at all temperatures increase, while trap depth and deep trap density decrease. The deterioration in electrical properties is more obvious for the sample with nano-TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, possibly attributed to the emergence of defects in microstructure induced by irradiation.

articleTitle: AC Breakdown Voltages of PEEK Insulation Used in Subsea Cable Connections
abstract: Subsea cable connectors are crucial components in offshore power delivery systems, commonly using a solid-liquid composite insulation system. Unfortunately, limited literature exists on the electrical characterisation of the insulation material polyether ether ketone (PEEK), despite extensive research on liquid and solid insulation materials in high voltage applications. This paper investigates the AC breakdown strength of PEEK immersed in a mineral oil at 20 °C. The results are statistically analysed using both 2-parameter and 3-parameter Weibull distributions, resulting in characteristic breakdown strenghts of 30.79 kV/mm and 30.40 kV/mm, respectively. Additionally, the location of each breakdown event was identified using a self-developed image processing procedure.

articleTitle: Influencing Factors and Potential Early Warning for Wind-Biased Transmission Line Discharges
abstract: Transmission lines are susceptible to external environmental factors such as strong winds and ice cover. In recent years, severe weather has occurred frequently, and wind bias faults on transmission lines have occurred from time to time, causing huge economic losses and affecting normal production and life. In this paper, ANSYS Workbench finite element analysis platform is used to establish the transmission line-hanging insulator string system model. Calculations were carried out for transmission lines under different stall spacing, height difference, wind speed and wind attack angle, analyzing the influence of different factors on the wind bias of insulators, and obtaining the rule of change of wind bias angle with stall spacing, height difference, wind speed and wind attack angle. Combining the effects of wind speed and wind attack angle on the wind bias angle of insulator strings, a wind bias early warning model for transmission lines was established based on PSO-SVM, and the practical effect of the model was evaluated. The study results can serve as a guide for designing and erecting of UHV and EHV transmission lines, as well as for the early warning of wind bias.

articleTitle: Study on Space Charge Properties of Different Nano/Epoxy Composites
abstract: Under high temperature and high electric field, space charge is easily accumulated in polymer dielectrics, leading to electric field distortion and material deterioration. The addition of nano particles can effectively inhibit space charge accumulation. Here, the different doping ratios (1 wt%, 3 wt%, 5 wt% and 10 wt%) and different types (MgO and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) epoxy resin (EP) based nano composites are prepared and the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) experiments are carried out under 30 kV/mm at 60°C and 80°C. It is found that EP-3 wt% MgO and EP-3 wt% Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> show the best ability to inhibit space charge accumulation, which respectively decrease 76.34% and 58.06% of average space charge density at 3600 sunder 80°C compared with neat EP. Nano MgO particles have better capability to suppress space charge in comparison with nano Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> particles. Furthermore, the different type of added nano particle leads to the different interface zone thickness.

articleTitle: Investigation on Resistance to Corona Erosion of Different Epoxy-amine Combinations
abstract: Insulating materials may be subjected to corona erosion when Partial Discharges are incepted and maintained, creating an additional stress that affects lifetime of these materials. A common material used in insulation systems consists in a polymer made of epoxy resin and amine hardener; depending on the type of hardener used, properties of the matrix differ, impacting also on the resistance to corona erosion. In this study, the same epoxy backbone reacted with three different amines was tested for corona erosion resistance at high temperature, measuring Mean Time To Failure (MTTF) and looking for a correlation with some properties of these materials, like glass transition temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>), coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE), relative permittivity, dissipation factor and cross-linking density.

articleTitle: Dielectric and Structural Insight Into an Innovative Self-healing Copolymer
abstract: Polymer-based electrical insulations are an indispensable part of modern electrical devices. Unfortunately, the insulation systems are exposed to high mechanical and electrical stresses. Self-healing polymers have recently attracted attention in electrical engineering because of their ability to partially recover from mechanical and electrical damage to material in some cases. This paper presents a study of self-healing ethylene-anisylpropylene copolymers without and with the tert-butyl substituent in the phenyl ring, emphasising comparing the two materials regarding dielectric and structural properties. The study covers the full range of analytical techniques, including broadband dielectric spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, thermo-mechanical analysis and differential scanning calorimetry. This comprehensive approach has allowed in-depth investigation of their dielectric and structural properties, providing valuable insights into their performance and potential applications. Two tested copolymers exhibit exceptional dielectric properties, making them promising materials for various applications. The dielectric constant, loss factor and dissipation factor were evaluated, and the results showed that both materials met the requirements for practical use as either a rigid or stretchable insulator. However, the practical use of both materials is limited mainly by the glass transition temperature, around 8 °C for one material and 28 °C for the other. The dielectric and mechanical properties change rapidly when the glass transition temperature is exceeded.

articleTitle: Radiation Resistance of PET and PEN as Probed by Luminescence and Conductivity Measurements
abstract: Thermoplastic polyesters as Poly(ethylene terephthalate) –PET- and Poly(ethylene naphthalate) –PEN- are commonly used as capacitors but can find other high end applications such as scintillators. Among other properties, the radiation resistance of such materials have often been compared, pointing notably to the evolution of physicochemical and optical properties. In this work, the evolution of the luminescence and dielectric properties with irradiation are investigated. We show a much greater sensitivity to radiation of PET in photoluminescence. This greater sensitivity is confirmed considering conduction properties.

articleTitle: Study on Insulation Relaxation Current Characteristics of Transformer with Different Operating Time
abstract: In order to study the effect of operation time on the insulation state of transformer, four kinds of transformer insulating oils with different operation time and fresh insulating paper are selected to make oil-paper insulation specimens. Isothermal relaxation current (IRC) experiments are conducted to study the trap distribution characteristics of the above four specimens. In addition, high-field conductivity tests are carried out to obtain the threshold electric field of the specimens. Characteristic values that represent the trap density and depth are derived from IRC test results. It is found that trap density and depth inside oil-impregnated-paper insulation show an increasing trend with the increase of transformer oil operatingtime. And it is found that the decreasing trend of the threshold electric field could also reflect the prolongation of the operation time of the transformer insulating oil, indicating that the specimen is easier to be injected with charge under low electric field below 10kV/mm.

articleTitle: Aging Characteristics and Lifespan Prediction of Composite Insulator SIR Under Multi-Haze Environment in Coastal Area
abstract: Composite insulators are currently widely used in power grids around the world due to their excellent performance. However, the insulation performance of composite insulators is greatly affected by exposure time and environment. At present, the existing discrimination methods for the aging of composite insulators are often based on the data of composite insulators in normal environment, so the aging discrimination of composite insulators under special climatic conditions is often not universal. In this paper, the running composite insulators in a coastal city in China hit by haze are tested and analyzed, and the sample insulators are tested by FTIR test, Water Diffusion test, and TGA test respectively. In this paper, the discrimination conditions of silicone rubber aging of composite insulators under multi-haze environment in coastal areas are determined, and the corresponding discriminant parameters are obtained, which provides a reference for the intelligent detection method of aging state of composite insulators under multi-haze environment. At the end of the paper, the BP neural network is used to predict the service life of composite insulators in coastal areas under multi-haze environment. It is proved that the prediction error is less than 5%, which is in line with the actual standard of the project.

articleTitle: Investigation of Effect of Nano-filler Concentration on the Life Estimation of Polyamide-6 Nanocomposites
abstract: This paper presents an investigation to estimate the life of polyamide-6/Barium Titanate (PA6/BTO) nanocomposite insulation under high-voltage DC fields. The influence of nanofiller concentration on the breakdown process was analysed. The tests were conducted at different electric fields under constant controlled thermal stress conditions. These tests were carried out above the glass transition temperature. The time to breakdown was analysed in terms of a two-parameter Weibull distribution. There is a drastic reduction in sample life as the electric field increases, particularly at 90kV/mm. Nanofiller concentrations between 1% and 10% have little effect upon lifetime but when the concentration reaches 20% there is a drastic reduction of the insulation life in the experimental field range of 90 kV/mm to 70 kV/mm.

articleTitle: An Aging Evaluation Method of Composite Insulators Based on Deep Learning and Decision Tree Model
abstract: Composite insulators have attracted more and more attention all over the world because of their excellent insulation performance. With the increase of operating life, long-term exposure to the daily environment will often lead to the gradual decline of its insulation performance. In this paper, the samples of composite insulators with service life of 0-35 years were tested by FTIR, shore hardness and hydrophobicity classification. The results of FTIR show that the peak of Si-O-Si and Si-CH3 are negatively correlated with the aging degree, and the peak of -OH is positively correlated with the aging degree. It can be seen that the three peaks of Si-O-Si, Si-CH3 and -OH can be used as the basis for judging the degree of aging. The shore hardness test results show that the difference between the actual and the standard hardness can be used as the basis for judging aging. In addition, a hydrophobicity classification evaluation method of composite insulators based on deep learning is proposed in this paper. The recognition accuracy can reach 97.6%. Finally, a decision tree model for aging evaluation of composite insulation sheds is established in this paper. The model can evaluate insulators into three grades: A, B, C and the accuracy of the evaluation is 99.8% and 95.6%, which is of great engineering value.

articleTitle: Dynamic Characteristics of Electric Field and Mechanical Stress Distribution of GIS Insulation Rod During Operation
abstract: In this paper, a gas insulated switchgear (GIS) insulation rod model is built by the finite element software, to research the electric field and mechanical stress distribution of the rod during the closing process. The electric field strength near the contact end (high voltage part) gradually decreases to 0, while simultaneously, the field strength at the operating end (grounding part) sees a corresponding increase. The maximum field strength along the surface remains relatively stable. The distribution of mechanical stress across the rod's surface is not uniform before the impact, and at the moment of the impact, the rod experiences large alternating tensile and compressive stresses. Significantly, the surface electric field and mechanical stress distribution of the insulation rod do not maintain the same distribution characteristics at different displacements during operation. Dynamic characteristics of the insulation rod is vital for optimizing the circuit breaker design and improving its operational performance and safety.

articleTitle: The Homogenizing Effects of Dielectric Functionally Graded Material on the Cylindrical Spacers with Insulating Defects
abstract: This paper provides an exploration about how dielectric functionally graded material (d-FGM) homogenize electric field on the cylindrical spacers with some general defects. The simulation models of cylindrical spacers with 3 kinds of defects, internal pore, surface pore and surface metal particle are simulated by COMSOL. Furthermore, the corresponding real models are prepared by thermal curing and their partial discharge properties are tested under 50Hz AC voltage. The results indicate that d-FGM has a good effect on homogenizing electric field in these 3 cases. The maximum electric field strength is reduced by about 62<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 53 % for internal pore and surface pore defects, respectively. For the surface metal defect, the area of electric field concentration is significantly reduced. The partial discharge inception voltages (PDIV) are increased by about 19.0% and 31.1 % for internal pore and surface pore defects, respectively. While for surface metal particles, the PDIV is increased by 3.6%. This research verifies that even though the insulating defects exist, the d-FGM still have good effect in homogenizing the electric field distribution.

articleTitle: Study on the Catalytic Degradation of Strong Greenhouse Gas SF6 Using a Two-Dimensional Metal Organic Framework
abstract: With the continuous development of sustainable and renewable energy sources, the catalytic degradation of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, a strong greenhouse gas, is receiving increasing attention. In this article, we provide a reference for the selection of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> thermal catalysts by simulating the adsorption and decomposition processes of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> on two-dimensional metals with different metal modifications. Based on DFT (density functional theory), simulate energy changes and charge transfer during adsorption and decomposition processes. The absence of band gaps in the energy band structure of Cu-CN, Mo-CN and Tc-CN implies their metallic character, which can be attributed to the effective orbital interaction between the benzene ring and MN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>. In addition, there is a strong chemisorption between the CN structures of Cr, Mn and Ru and SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> with significant bond length changes, charge transfer. The CN structures of these three metals have better potential to catalyze SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>

articleTitle: Effects of Thermal Properties on Insulation Breakdown Behaviors of Epoxy/Al2O3 Composite with Boron Nitride Doping
abstract: Epoxy resin/alumina composites are widely used in power equipment due to its superior electrical and mechanical properties. As the insulating support material for high voltage conductor and grounding electrode in GIL/GIS equipment, epoxy resin/Al2O3 composites are subjected to large temperature gradient field generated by high current. The epoxy resin/Al2O3 composites are prone to breakdown under the electric field superimposed on the temperature gradient field, reducing the operational stability of the equipment. In this paper, the influence of hexagonal boron nitride with high thermal conductivity on the thermal conductivity of epoxy resin /Al2O3 composites is investigated. The influence of different doping ratios on the breakdown field strength of the composites is investigated. It also verifies the effectiveness of the high thermal conductivity material to enhance the thermal conductivity and insulation properties of epoxy resin/Al2O3 composites by simulation.

articleTitle: New Model for Acetophenone Ions in XLPE Insulation –Space Charge and Electric Field Characteristics Using Bipolar Charge Transport Theory
abstract: Bipolar charge transport (BCT) models have been used for the past few decades to simulate and analyze charge transport and its associated phenomena in polymeric insulation materials. Whilst in this method primarily, electronic charge carriers are used, recent studies show that there has been a high interest in the addition of ionic charge carriers and their physical processes in the model. Among the byproducts in the crosslinked XLPE, acetophenone is speculated to have deep electron traps and therefore can contribute to the electrical conduction processes in XLPE insulation, leading to charge and field dynamics in XLPE insulation. In this paper, a new model is attempted considering acetophenone for modelling the ions originating from acetophenone molecules, which demonstrates the charge and field dynamics in the insulation. Using the BCT model, combining with the electronic species, the impact of the presence of the ions is discussed. The ionic charge carrier and the neutral molecule are modelled based on Marcus theory. The results reported in this paper draw attention to the charge and field distribution for different ionic concentrations, the effect of thermal gradient and mobilities of the ions. A comparison between the experimental conductivity values from various literature and the proposed model has been done.

articleTitle: Breakdown Testing of Pressure- and Cure-bonded Silicone Rubber Interfaces
abstract: Dielectric interfaces are critical in determining the reliability of high voltage insulation systems. By considering new experimental results and data from electrical treeing in the literature it is shown that not only is the nature of the interface being studied important, but so is the electrode configuration. In particular, voids around the electrodes are critical to inception and development of a track. Unlike in electrical treeing tests where homogeneity is often sought in a laboratory sample, it is concluded that understanding the nature of the interface being modelled is essential and that experimentation must replicate service materials and systems. Comparison of silicone rubber interfaces formed purely by pressure and those which are bonded must be differentiated by whether the source of partial discharges (here a needle tip) is vented, and whether a void is present at the point of discharge initiation.

articleTitle: Identification of the Defect Type in Epoxy Resin Using the Differences in Reflected THz Wave Characteristics
abstract: A non-destructive inspection method by using Terahertz wave is effective for detecting defects in epoxy resin, which is widely used for insulating materials. To identity the type of defect such as metal fragment, void and resin burr is important to improve the electrical insulation property of the resin. In this study, we investigated the good method to identify the defect type by using THz time domain spectroscopy. As the results, we focused on the three feature properties of reflected wave: amplitude difference, frequency dependence and distribution of time interval. It is concluded that the combination of these feature quantities provides a useful way to distinguish the defect types.

articleTitle: An Engineering Model for Predicting Probabilities of Dielectric Breakdown in Gas-insulated Systems
abstract: In high-voltage engineering the so-called “streamer integral” is used widely to predict dielectric breakdown voltages of gas-insulated systems. The simple, deterministic nature of the model facilitates application to complex system geometries but comes at a price: most notably, the physical relation between the predicted “inception voltage” for breakdown and the experimentally-observable, statistical behavior of a system is lost. Consequently, the inception voltage is typically associated ad hoc with the voltage, at which breakdown occurs with two percent probability. This complicates the determination of the model parameters and limits their applicability across diverse system geometries. In this work, we introduce a probabilistic extension of the streamer integral model, which permits predicting how the probability of breakdown depends on the applied voltage. An initial validation is performed based on breakdown experiments in air with lighting-impulse voltages.

articleTitle: Defect Location and Identification Method for Long-Distance Cable Based on Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave
abstract: Conventional frequency domain reflectometry faces challenges in detecting local defects for long-distance cables, such as weak anti-interference capability, large shielding zone, and inability to identify defect types. To address these issues, a method for defect location and identification based on frequency modulated continuous wave is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the principle of defect location is introduced, where the wave is injected into the cable head, and the beat signal carrying the information of defect location and characteristics is obtained. Secondly, the diagnostic function for local defects is constructed utilizing the generalized orthogonal integration algorithm, and the identification criterion for defect types is proposed based on the diagnostic waveforms. The position of the diagnostic peak is used for defect location, and the polarity of that is used for type recognition. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation and experimentation. The results indicate that the method can accurately locate the local defect, with a relative location error of less than 0.3%, and the criterion can efficiently identify the defect types.

articleTitle: Effect of Moisture and Oil-Immersion on Dielectric Properties of Paper Insulation
abstract: To further explore the dielectric mechanism of oil-paper insulation and the effect of moisture action, the dielectric spectra of oil, non-impregnated paper (NIP), and oil-impregnated paper (OIP) in oil-paper systems with different moisture contents are obtained and comparatively analyzed. The results show that the dielectric response of NIP is composed of hopping conductivity, low-frequency relaxation polarization and high-frequency relaxation polarization. As the moisture content increases, the first two dielectric processes move towards high frequencies with the dielectric curve shape remaining unchanged, while the high-frequency polarization is almost unaffected. Oil-immersion only has a considerable effect when the oil conductivity is greater than that of paper insulation. The influence of moisture on paper insulation is much greater than that of oil. Only at a low moisture condition does the conductivity of oil and NIP intersect, so that the low-frequency dielectric response of OIP, such as the hopping conductivity and low-frequency relaxation polarization, may be covered by the high dielectric loss of oil. When the moisture content is high, the dielectric properties of OIP is the same as that of NIP.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of the Moisture Effect on the Dielectric Properties of Thermally Upgraded Kraft Paper Impregnated with Mineral Oil and Natural Ester
abstract: An essential component of power transformers is the electrical insulation system, composed of cellulose-based materials and usually mineral oil. Currently, this fluid is being replaced by alternative dielectric fluids derived from plants, such as soybean, sunflower, etc. The dielectric system must be kept in prime condition. Moisture affects the dielectric strength and the rate of insulation ageing. Frequency Domain Spectroscopy (FDS) is a promising method to analyze the moisture effect in oil-paper insulation system of the transformer. This study investigates the influence of moisture on the dielectric behavior of Thermally Upgraded Kraft (TUK) paper, both non-impregnated and impregnated with mineral oil and soybean ester. The samples were prepared in the laboratory with different moisture content within 1% to 5%. Measurements were performed over a wide frequency range from 16.62 mHz to 5 kHz. It was found that the impregnation of the paper samples helps to reduce the variation of tan δ with the incrementation of moisture and that the dielectric response is sensitive to moisture content regardless of the impregnation and the type of impregnation liquid.

articleTitle: Preliminary Characterization of Dielectrics for Insulated Metal Substrates (IMS) of Power Modules
abstract: The study investigates organic dielectric materials for use on insulated metal substrates in 1200V power modules with enhanced power density. Six materials are examined for their electrical performance, comparing them to conventional ceramic insulation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex>. The measured quantities are leakage current, breakdown strength, dielectric losses, space charge accumulation, and partial discharge inception voltage. While all materials are suitable for power electronics applications, two stand out with superior performance, characterized by lower space charge accumulation, higher dielectric strength, and PDIV levels. The study suggests that these organic materials, despite higher dielectric losses, could be viable alternatives for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1200\mathrm{V}$</tex> applications, pending further investigation into thermal aging stability.

articleTitle: Inductive Loop Operation Versus Loop Antenna for Partial Discharge Detection
abstract: This article delves into the application and efficacy of planar loop sensors for detecting partial discharge (PD) phenomena. The preference for loop sensors in PD detection stems from their simple design, non-destructive testing feature, and contactless characteristics. The paper explores both experimental and finite element modeling (FEM) approaches to evaluate the performance of distinct planar square spiral sensors in PD detection. The primary objective of the study is to compare inductive loops with loop antennas by varying the geometric parameters to achieve each approach. Two single-turn square loop antennas were designed, with a circumference of 30 cm and 75 cm, and compared with four multi-turn square inductive loops with an exterior side of 31.2 mm and varying geometric parameters.
