The figures of merit of all sensors, such as inductance, quality factor, and resonant frequency, are extracted through measurement and simulation to identify the most influential parameter that maximizes the sensing capability toward PD.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Test Results of Glass Transition Pressure and Conductivity of Polypropylene Under Different Pressure Conditions
abstract: A self-made high pressure experimental setup, which is used to test the compressive strain and dielectric properties of polymer materials under different pressure conditions, is described in this paper. The glass transition pressure and resistivity of polypropylene insulation material were studied using this setup. By changing the testing temperature, it was found that the glass transition pressure showed a positive correlation with temperature. At the room temperature, when the pressure increases to about 230Mpa, the material shows a remarkable glass transition characteristic. The glass transition pressure of homo polypropylene and co polypropylene were tested separately, and it was found that the glass transition pressure of homo polypropylene was significantly lower than that of co polypropylene, which was opposite to the comparison of the glass transition temperature of the two. Testing the conductivity of polypropylene at different pressures revealed a significant downward trend with increasing pressure.

articleTitle: Space Charge Characteristics of Epoxy Resin/Carbon Quantum Dots Nanocomposites
abstract: This work deals with the space charge investigation of nanostructured epoxy resin (Sigma Aldrich DER332) filled with Carbon Quantum Dots. Space charge characteristics of the material are obtained by investigating the characteristic curves coming from Thermally Stimulated Depolarization Current measurement. In particular, the analysis of these curves highlights the occurrence of a significant shift in glass transition temperature in the nanocomposite. Furthermore, the incorporation of Carbon Quantum Dots is confirmed by an increase in the inertia in the first step of the performed measurement and by the presence of a Maxwell-Wagner-Sillars peak in the plot of the discharging current. Nonetheless, activation energies of the relaxation processes appearing in TSDC plots do not experience any detectable variation, thus suggesting that the chemical structure of the nanocomposite retains some characteristics of the neat epoxy resin.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a Low-cost Capacitive Non-intrusive Sensor for the Detection, Localization and Identification of Defects in MVAC Cables
abstract: Partial discharges (PDs) monitoring is a common tool for diagnosing electrical systems. An innovative, low-cost sensor for distance detection and positioning of partial PDs has been developed. An ambitious challenge for this PD monitoring system is to predict dielectric breakdowns on a grid and particularly in MVAC cables. The first part of the article demonstrates the proper functioning of this sensor on a test bench. In a second part, monitoring measurements of PD activity issued from artificial defects are presented. PD initiated in submillimetric cavities were collected. Parameters and PD patterns have been interpreted with the aim to correlate with the electrical treeing propagation until breakdown. The final section is dedicated to a concise review of electrical treeing monitoring. Analysis of existing approaches are presented, as well as the interesting opportunities offered by the sensor.

articleTitle: Electronic Transitions in Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene Accounting for Photo-Stimulated Currents
abstract: Biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) is a widely used insulating material in capacitor films. As the demand for improved capacitor performance grows, it's crucial to have a deep understanding of polymer molecular structures and their electronic properties. Therefore, focusing on theoretical modeling, simulations, and experiments is important to uncover the relationship between microscopic phenomena and device effectiveness. In this study, we use a recently developed test bench coupling the Laser Intensity Modulated Method (LIMM) and Photo-Stimulated Discharge (PSD) measurements to investigate charge trapping and detrapping processes in BOPP samples. By analyzing photoinduced currents and absorption spectra, we identified relationships between foreign elements within the polymer chains and charge trapping and detrapping dynamics. Our research indicates that BOPP films typically display two light absorption bands in the UV-visible range. The generation of S1 excitons at around 3.1 eV may suggest the creation of free charges through the Auger effect and luminescence emission. Additionally, higher energy photons (∼6.2 eV) may contribute to the formation of S2 excitons, influenced by chemical additives such as phenolic antioxidants, which can release electrons under the residual field associated with trapped space charge.

articleTitle: Relation Between Chalking of HTV and Decay-Like Aging of FRP in Composite Insulators
abstract: In recent years, the reliability of transmission lines is seriously affected by decay-like aging in composite insulators. Interface discharges and chalking of silicon rubber housing are often found in decay-like aged insulators. However, the relation between HTV chalking and decay-like aging is still unclear. In this paper, an artificial accelerated aging platform based on interface discharge was constructed to reproduce chalking and decay-like aging in composite insulators, and to investigative the effect of HTV chalking on core rod decay-like aging. The experiment provided acidic and high temperature conditions through interface discharge in a high humidity environment, the CT structure, leakage current, and physicochemical properties of core rod are characterized. The experimental results show that the housing filling behavior can exacerbate surface aging of core rods, ATH filling can slow down the aging of core rods during long-term aging. The ability of silicone rubber housing to resist tracking still has a positive effect on reducing core rod decay-like aging. This study provides a laboratory basis for chalking and decay-like aging.

articleTitle: Analyses of RTV Composite Coating under DC Stress for High Voltage Outdoor Insulation
abstract: High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission poses stern threats to insulators due to unidirectional high voltages. Room temperature vulcanized (RTV) silicone rubber (SiR) coatings are highly preferred to cope with flashovers. In this work, RTV-SiR coating co-filled with silica <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\text{Si}{\mathrm{O}_2}})$</tex> and alumina trihydrate (ATH) fillers underwent prolonged accelerated weathering under bipolar direct current (DC) for an extended aging period of 10,000 hours. The results revealed that samples containing nano <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Si}{\mathrm{O}_2}$</tex>, and micron-ATH displayed enhanced hydrophobic recovery, leading to improved suppression of leakage current, whereas ATH-filled composites demonstrated better performance in surface resistivity with improved antiaging. In terms of the polarity impact of DC voltage, samples powered by negative voltage showed relatively less decrease in volume and surface resistivity. Moreover, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of samples filled with nano <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Si}{\mathrm{O}_2}$</tex> exhibited a lower degree of deterioration.

articleTitle: An Improved Algorithm of Cable Fault Diagnosis Considering Signal Attenuation Compensation
abstract: The traveling wave along the long-distance cable system exhibits significant attenuation characteristics in the high-frequency region, resulting in severe peak distortion of positioning curves based on the traditional frequency domain reflection (FDR), especially for the faults which is far from the signal injection end. This phenomenon often leads to misjudgment of cable fault severity. In this paper, the attenuation principle of swept frequency signal along the cable and its influence on the FDR positioning result is analyzed in detail. Based on the traveling wave's attenuation characteristics, to address the above issue, an attenuation compensation function is proposed to improve the FDR algorithm, enabling accurate evaluation of cable's fault severity. Simulation and actual tests on the communication cable and power cable demonstrate that the positioning peaks of the same fault type at the different locations are nearly identical for the optimized FDR positioning curve, with difference less than 3%, which verifies the validation of the improved algorithm.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Behavior of Q(t) Measurement and Noise Effects
abstract: DC power equipment is increasingly being integrated into our society, necessitating reliable diagnostic methods for insulation materials under high DC electric fields. The current integration method (Q(t) measurement) is considered one of the applicable methods for measuring Q(t) data. However, the mathematical and physical analysis of Q(t) measurements is not yet fully developed, resulting in partially analyzed data, especially concerning variance handling. By introducing a circuit model and solving differential equations numerically, this study investigates the causes of variance in the delay properties at the early stages of Q(t). Average Q(t) data for polyimide sample sheets with pseudo-noise in initial conditions were generated, and the numerical changes were evaluated. The findings suggested that variances in delay properties were mainly due to initial offsets in the first and second time derivatives of Q(t), rather than offsets in Q(t) itself. Therefore, it is revealed that the user of Q(t) measurement should be more attentive to the stability and control of inrush current when applying it to actual insulation materials to make diagnoses more reliable.

articleTitle: Breakdown and Partial Discharge in Dry Air under Non-uniform Electric Field for MVDC Applications
abstract: Medium and high voltage gas insulated switchgear (GIS) are key installations in the electrical power transmission and distribution network. The equipment in these substations are insulated with pressurized gas in order to guarantee their proper functioning. This work aims to investigate the performance, in DC, of dry air under non-uniform electric field conditions for medium voltage switchgear applications. Experimental investigations have been carried out to assess the breakdown and the partial discharge inception voltages as function of the electric field non-uniformity and dry air pressures. The experimental work has been compared with numerical study of the breakdown electric field based on streamer criterion using COMSOL Multiphysics numerical software. The results show that the breakdown maximum field decreases as a function of the utilization factor till 0.3, then it stabilizes for weakly non-uniform electric field. The breakdown maximum field is not dependent on the polarity of the DC voltage for utilization factors higher than 0.2. Otherwise, the breakdown maximum field seems to be lower under positive DC voltage for utilization factors under 0.2. Simulation results of the maximum field obtained using the streamer criterion are in good agreement with the experimental partial discharge results.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis of Silicone Rubber in Corrosive Environment Under AC Operation
abstract: Composite insulators have been widely used globally due to their outstanding performance. They suffer from acidic or alkaline pollution in coastal or saline-alkali regions, as well as chemical dust released by industrial and mining activities. These substances settle on silicone rubber housings and become corrosive and conductive after dissolving in water, causing damage to the housings. Therefore, this paper investigates the failure characteristics of silicone rubber in energized corrosive environments, including dielectric properties and X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS). The findings demonstrate that as aging duration increases, the real part of complex permittivity (ε’) and dielectric loss (tan δ) increase. Compared to salt fog, acid fog has a greater effect on the aging of silicone rubber at the same conductivity. The ε’ and tan δ of complex permittivity increase with applied voltage and acid fog conductivity. After aging experiments, the oxygen content on the surface layer of silicone rubber samples increases significantly, while the carbon content and organic components decrease significantly. After the aging treatment, the content of Si(-O)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> decreases significantly, whereas the content of Si(‒O)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> increases and then decreases, whereas Si(‒O)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> exhibits the opposite trend. The research findings can help explore the failure mechanisms of silicone rubber in corrosive environments.

articleTitle: Electric Field Distribution Detection and Surface Insulation Enhancement for GIS/GIL by Flexible Smart Surface Coating Insulators
abstract: Surface defects in epoxy resin insulators are a critical factor leading to the decline in the insulation performance of GIS/GIL equipment. In this article, an innovative coating design utilizing the electroluminescence effect is proposed for the precise identification of surface defects on insulators. The coating demonstrates a linear relationship between electric field strength and luminescence intensity under AC conditions. Through detailed experimental analysis, it was observed that with an increase in AC voltage, the luminescent area on the surface of basin insulators progressively expands, with the luminescence intensity decreasing from the high-voltage conductor towards the grounded shell. In metal particle conditions, variations in luminescence intensity provided a basis for effectively identifying the location of metal particles. Additionally, the coating exhibited a higher dielectric constant, effectively mitigating the adverse effects of metal particles on the insulation performance of basin insulators. The research provides a new method for the detection and evaluation of the surface insulation insulation of epoxy resin insulators.

articleTitle: Core Loss Distribution of Anode Saturable Reactor using J-A Dynamic Hysteresis Model
abstract: The anode saturable reactor (ASR) used in high voltage direct current (HVDC) converter valves generates humongous losses in working condition, which affect the safety of the converter valves. This paper estimates the core loss of ASR based on the J-A dynamic hysteresis model. The parameters of the J-A hysteresis model are optimized by using improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, and the proposed method is verified in predicting the hysteresis losses and non-neglected eddy current and excess losses in cores according to the comparation results between measured and simulated losses in a grain-oriented (GO) silicon steel. By combining the proposed model with the finite-element method (FEM), the simulation model of single core-coils in ASR is constructed, and both the magnetic flux density and electrical stress of each mesh element in turn-on and turn-off transient states are obtained. The consequence shows that the maximum instantaneous loss density can reach up to 54.46 MW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> when the coil current cross through 0 in turn-off state, while the relatively high core losses appear in the inner fillet, ends and vertical yoke near the air gaps, where the maximum losses can reach up to 63.8 W/kg.

articleTitle: Effect of Thermal Aging on Medium Frequency Breakdown of Polyester Films
abstract: This article discusses the effects of thermal stress on polyethylene terephthalate (PET) films focusing on its impact on the capability of the insulation to withstand voltage waveforms with an elevated frequency content. To properly mimic the degradation the material may face during its service life, thin (∼50 μm) PET films were subjected to accelerated thermal aging at 150, 165 and 180 °C. Aging effects (including oxidation) on the chemical structure of PET were investigated by means of Fourier Transform InfraRed spectroscopy. Dielectric spectroscopy was performed on samples to evaluate the dielectric losses at the different aging stages. To simulate the worst-case scenario during operation, high frequencies (up to 30 kHz) were selected and used for the AC breakdown tests, thus assessing the evolution of the PET dielectric strength with aging. Results showed that no direct correspondence between dielectric strength and dissipation factor (tanδ) values is present, suggesting that thermal runaway is not the only factor causing the dielectric breakdown.

articleTitle: Usage of Physics-Informed Neural Network to Extract Physical Parameters From High Voltage Experiments
abstract: Computer simulations based on partial differential equations (PDEs) describing physical phenomena, are widely used for analyzing the performance of high voltage insulation. Such simulation models require access to physical model parameters, which are often hard to obtain. The purpose of the present paper is to explore how Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) tailored for specific PDEs, can be used to extract relevant physical parameters from synthetic data. Electric potential or charge distributions in 1-dimensional coaxial and Cartesian domains were used as training data for PINN models. The following physical parameters were successfully extracted: (i) space charge profiles, (ii) mobilities of ions, and (iii) the radius of the inner electrode in the coaxial geometry. The impact of noisy training data on the accuracy was also studied for the different cases. The main finding is that PINN models can successfully be used to extract model parameters for electrical charge transport problems using synthetic data as input. This approach has large potential to strengthen the research on charge dynamics in gas, liquid, and solid insulation as well as other topics related to high voltage insulation systems.

articleTitle: Research on Semi-Conductive Shielding Materials for High-Voltage Cables Based on Compound Resins
abstract: Ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymer (EVA)-based semi-conductive shielding materials (SCSM) are widely utilized in low/medium-voltage cables. However, the limited thermal stability of EVA prevents their application in high-voltage cables. In this paper, LDPE is introduced to blend with EVA and carbon black (CB) was used as conductive filler to fabricate high thermal stable CB/EVA/LDPE composites for application as high-voltage SCSM. It is demonstrated that the incorporation of LDPE effectively enhances the thermal stability of the CB/EVA/LDPE composites. The first-stage thermal weight loss of the CB/EVA/LDPE composites is decreased to 10.4%, compared to that (14.7%) of the CB/EVA composites. The incorporation of LDPE also leads to the enhancement of the mechanical properties of the CB/EVA/LDPE composites, with a tensile strength of 17.9 MPa and an elongation at break of 285.9%. Moreover, the electrical properties of the CB/EVA/LDPE composites are well maintained, with a volume resistivity of 73.6 Ω·cm. These findings provide theoretical and experimental basis for the development of EVA-based semi-conductive shielding layer for high-voltage cables.

articleTitle: Improved Energy Storage Performance of Biaxially Stretched Polypropylene Films Based on Molecular Semiconductor Grafting
abstract: Previous studies have confirmed that the energy storage performances of modified polypropylene (PP) by chemical grafting has been significantly improved. However, as an indispensable link in the production of capacitor films, the biaxial tensile has a significant effect on the micro structures and macro properties of modified PP materials. In this work, the differences in micro structures between direct hot pressed and biaxial stretched PP composites films with micro addition of grafted molecular semiconductors are studied. Based on situ characterization technology in micro regions of polymers developed in the laboratory, the surface potential and trap distribution characteristics of nanoscale regions in pure and composite materials are compared. The energy storage performances of different samples at 25 and 120 ℃ are tested. It is proved that the biaxial stretching process can be applied to PP composites based on molecular semiconductor grafting, and the stretched films still show a remarkable performance improvement, which has a certain practical application prospect in the industry.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of the Reasons for Partial Coalescence of Uncharged Water Droplet and Layer Under DC Electric Field
abstract: This study is focused on the numerical investigating of forces that affect electrocoalescence process in the droplet-layer system. At a certain electric field strength, the Coulomb forces become sufficient to slow down the process of droplet coalescence with the layer, which leads to the formation of a neck in the upper part of the droplet with subsequent separation of the secondary droplet. The area of the neck formation differs from the location of the initial bridge between droplet and layer, though they get closer with the increase in the electric field strength. The analysis of electrostatic and tension forces acting on the surface of the water phase lead us to deeper understanding of partial coalescence causes, which can further help to suppress this coalescence mode and provide more reliable dehydration of the emulsion.

articleTitle: A Review on Different Deconvolution Techniques on Frequency Domain for a PEA Cell for HVDC Cables
abstract: The processing of space charge signals, obtained through the Pulsed Electro-Acoustic (PEA) method, is crucial for understanding the space charge accumulation mechanisms in dielectric material and the impact these have on the operation of an HVDC cable. In this paper, the authors give a brief description of the entire processing procedure required to avoid making mistakes in the interpretation of the obtained profiles. Specifically, we examine different deconvolution techniques in the frequency domain for analyzing such signals. Deconvolution techniques were implemented in MATLAB environment and used to process a PEA profile obtained from a measurement on a full-size HVDC cable with an applied DC voltage of 100 kV.

articleTitle: A Cable Defect Location and Assessment Method Based on the Hilbert-Enveloped Reflection Coefficient
abstract: Time-frequency domain reflectometry is a sensitive method for locating cable defects. However, common time-frequency domain reflectometry methods cannot assess the severity of the located defects, which may lead to unnecessary cable replacement. Therefore, a cable defect location and assessment method based on the Hilbert-enveloped reflection coefficient is proposed in this paper. The method extracts the attenuation curves of the incident signal through the propagation coefficients to avoid the errors caused by the signal attenuation. In addition, the refraction compensation factor is proposed to avoid the extra errors caused by the reflection and refraction of defect signal. In simulation and experiments, the defect location errors are all less than 1 %, and the assessment errors are less than 6 %. The method is expected to locate cable defects and assess their severity.

articleTitle: Design of a Flexible UHF Antenna for PD Detection in Inverter-Fed Motors
abstract: When performing partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) measurements by using the ultra-high frequency method on insulation systems of inverter-fed motors under repetitive impulsive voltages, the antenna charactaristics and sensor placement should be carefully considered to get high sensitivity. Different antennas have been reported for PDIV tests under impulsive voltages, but the antenna with fixed size would be difficult to install near the test object limited by both the size of the object and the antenna itself. To solve this problem, we present a design of a flexible, narrow-band antenna that can be attached to the surface of a motor stator. The designed antenna has a thickness of 0.16 mm and dimensions of 90*100 mm. Simulation and measurement reveal that as the bending curvature diameter of the antenna varies from 3.1831 mm to 22 cm, the resonance frequency point shifts towards a higher frequency, and its working frequency range is at least from 0.7 to 1.2 GHz. Subsequently, a platform for motor stator insulation PD detection is developed to assess the performance of the antenna. Experimental results indicate that, compared to an Archimedean spiral antenna (ASA), the flexible antenna exhibits hypersensitive, enabling a higher electromagnetic conversion efficiency for the near-field coupled PD under impulsive voltages with 200 ns rise times. The amplitude of the received PD signal distributed in the frequency range from 0.2 to 1.1 GHz is at least 100 times higher than the PD obtained by ASA. Therefore, the signal to noise ratio is increased significantly when performing PD tests at impulses with short rise times resorting to the designed antenna.

articleTitle: Correlating Crystallinity and Electrical Conductivity in Gamma-Irradiated PTFE
abstract: Exposing polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) to irradiation brings about significant alterations in both its crystallinity and conductivity. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the connection, if any, between crystallinity, a structural feature, and electrical conductivity, which represents a macroscopic property. This was accomplished by subjecting PTFE to varying doses of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> -rays, reaching up to 200 kGy. Various physicochemical characterizations were conducted to elucidate the impact of irradiation on dielectric properties. We show that irradiation produces chain scission and oxidized groups at chain ends. The material becomes more crystallizable after irradiation whereas the increase in conductivity would result from transport due to oxidized groups and short chain formation.

articleTitle: Lifetime Investigations on Insulating Materials for High Voltage DC Airborne Applications
abstract: The purpose of the presented study is to evaluate the lifetime of an insulating material for a high DC voltage in an airborne and an off-shore application. In order to accelerate the aging process, a thermal stress at 200°C was applied to coupons made of epoxy material (E). Some samples also undergo combined stresses. For a DC electric field of 3.8kV/mm, no dielectric breakdown was observed after 3 months of test, while for a field of 4.6kV/mm, breakdown of all coupons occurred in less than 30 hours. In order to understand aging mechanisms, several parameters were monitored during the tests. Space charge mapping, using the Pulsed Electro Acoustic (PEA) method, done at 150°C under 4.6kV/mm, showed that hetero-charges were trapped inside the material, leading to a local field enhancement in the material. For the applied field of 3.8kV/mm, the local electric field was below the critical threshold, and no breakdown was initiated. Dielectric spectroscopy was monitored during aging tests in the range of 10mHz-30Hz. A continuous increase of coupons impedance was observed during aging. The increase was even higher in the case of coupons which received the combined thermal and electrical stresses. Charge mapping with PEA showed that most of the charge relaxed after the voltage switch off. Hence it was concluded that the higher impedance increase during time with the cumulated stresses was probably not due to trapped charge inside the material. Instead, the applied DC stress had provoked an additional change of the material properties, compared to the thermal stress alone.

articleTitle: An Optical Measurement Method for Electrostatic Sensing Based on Fabry-Perot Sensing System
abstract: Among the various methods for detecting electrostatic discharge, optical electrostatic sensors have attracted widespread attention due to their numerous advantages, such as high sensitivity and rapid response capabilities. As a type of optical sensor, the performance of fiber-optic F-P electrostatic sensors will be affected the design of the collector. Therefore, a detailed study of the collector design in F-P electrostatic sensors is crucial for enhancing the precision and reliability of electrostatic discharge measurements. In this paper, the sensing capabilities of sensors with equilateral triangular, square, and circular collectors of identical areas under external applied voltage are tested. Simultaneously, models of these three shaped collectors are constructed and subjected to simulation analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that the cavity drive displacement of the sensor with a circular collector exhibits a good linear relationship with the applied voltage. The results also indicate that circular collector, compared to square and equilateral triangular ones, are more suitable for use as sensing modules in sensors. This research provides meaningful insights for the design and optimization of these sensors.

articleTitle: Charge Transport in a Filler-Free Silicone Rubber: Exploring Non-Linear Mechanisms and the “Liquid-like” Anomaly
abstract: The literature diverges about the understanding of DC conduction in elastomeric materials, as silicone rubbers, attributing the conduction whether to a solid or to a liquid one. In this study, three different liquid silicone rubbers (LSR) free of fillers are fabricated from the same bi-component raw material, but with different curing times and component proportions. They were submitted to current-voltage measurements at 40°C, with 1h polarization and depolarization cycles, from 1 to 10 kV. The current-voltage characteristics of a low cured sample presented a sub-ohmic profile. The sample cured and post-cured for a longer time presented an ohmic conduction. The non-stoichiometric material presented also an ohmic conduction, but with a deviation to a sub-ohmic at higher voltages. Moreover, its reversal currents in the depolarization profile were characteristic of blocking activity. Analysis of conduction in rubbers is proposed to explain the liquid-like behavior for elastomers, and the solid-like appearance in certain cases.

articleTitle: Effects of Different Diluents on Dielectric Property of Epoxy Resin Based on Molecular Dynamics
abstract: The purpose of this work is to establish the relationship between the network structure of different diluents and the dielectric properties of the modified epoxy. In this paper, diluents containing butyl and phenyl structures have been chosen as diluents to modify the traditional bisphenol A type epoxy resin networks. The relaxation polarization behavior of various modified samples is investigated under different temperatures, and the inhibition effect of terminal groups of diluents on ß polarization has been revealed. Due to the steric effect of phenyl groups, the polarization of cross-linking points is limited. For the modified cross-linked network containing butyl structure, there is an interaction between steric hindrance and free volume. The effects of different diluents on the network structure have been verified by molecular dynamics.

articleTitle: Effect of LDPE Molecular Structure on the Cross-Linking and Scorching Characteristics of XLPE Material for High-Voltage Cable
abstract: There is conflict between crosslinking and scorch resistance of crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) material for high-voltage cables, and optimizing this relationship through modifications in the molecular structure of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) becomes crucial in the development of high-performance XLPE insulation material. This study utilizes two types of LDPE matrix materials to create crosslinkable polyethylene samples. The LDPE molecular structure is analyzed by gel permeation chromatography (GPC) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). The cross-linking efficiency of XLPE samples is evaluated through gel content and thermal elongation tests, and the scorching characteristic of XLPE materials is assessed using a torque rheometer. The findings show that a higher vinyl content in the LDPE molecular structure contributes to increasing gel content and reducing the thermal elongation of XLPE samples. Additionally, a higher weight average molecular weight (Mw) of LDPE leads to more severe scorching of the XLPE material, which adversely affects the extrusion process. This investigation elucidates the effect of LDPE molecular structure on the cross-linking and scorching characteristics of XLPE insulation, offering valuable guidance for achieving long-distance stable extrusion and high crosslinking degree of XLPE insulation material for high-voltage cables.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of a Transformer-Based Test Platform
abstract: This paper investigates the utilization of esters in power transformers for their cooling and dielectric insulation properties, focusing on their potential to enhance safety and reduce environmental impact. A test platform based on a 100MVA power transformer was developed to analyze the performance of these alternative fluids in an ONAN operation regime. Using Finite Volume Method-based tools and Thermo-Hydraulic Network Models, calculations were conducted to compare the fluid behavior of an ester and a mineral oil within the test platform. The results present thermal and hydraulic data for both types of fluids, highlighting their compatibility with the transformer and adherence to industry standards. The study concludes by demonstrating the feasibility of esters for sustainable power systems and the utility of numerical simulations in predicting fluid dynamics, affirming the effectiveness of the experimental setup.

articleTitle: Research on the Recycling of EP/Al2O3 and its Insulation Performance After Reconstitution
abstract: Epoxy resin/alumina (EP/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) employed in GIL is challenging to degrade and recycle due to its insoluble and infusible properties. This paper uses a chemical recycling method, i.e., alcoholysis, to degrade EP/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> under mild conditions, aiming to improve sustainability and alleviate environmental pressure. Degraded EP (DEP) and recycled Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powders can be reused for the preparation of new epoxy composites, and the catalyst used in the alcoholysis reaction is still reactive. The occurrence of the alcoholysis reaction is verified through nuclear magnetic resonance. Meanwhile, the microscopic morphology of the recycled Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powders is observed by scanning electron microscopy. It is found that both the particle size distribution and micromorphology remain basically unchanged. DEP is utilized instead of 15 wt% bisphenol A diglycidyl ether, and the recycled Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powders are reused to prepare new epoxy composites. The insulating properties of the new EP/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> are investigated and found to be comparable to the original sample in terms of resistivity, AC breakdown strength, and impact flashover voltage. Because the addition of DEP slightly increases the deep trap density and energy level center, the new EP/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> still maintains excellent insulating properties. The increased relative permittivity and dielectric loss in DEP are due to the highly polar ester group and some branched chains in DEP. This paper focuses on the degradation and reuse of EP/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> to offer insights into the recycling process of epoxy composites.

articleTitle: Evaluating Rejuvenation Effects on Water-tree Aged Cables Induced by Electric Field Using PDC Method
abstract: To explore the impact of different injection conditions on the water tree-aged cable rejuvenation effects and rate, including pressure injection and different voltage types injection, we conducted polarization and depolarization current (PDC) tests before and after rejuvenation. Results indicate that applying different external electric fields during the injection significantly enhances the rejuvenation rate, with the positive DC showing the best outcome, followed by AC, and lastly, the negative DC. Finite element analysis demonstrates that a DC field is more favorable for the accumulation of rejuvenation fluid molecules in the water trees. Under a DC positive electric field, both ends of the XLPE molecular chain are negatively charged and are aligned systematically due to the influence of the electric field force, providing a pathway for the migration of rejuvenation fluid molecules and achieving the best rejuvenation effect.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Grafted Molecule Types on Frequency Domain Spectroscopy of Polypropylene Insulation
abstract: Thermoplastic insulation materials represented by polypropylene (PP) have become an important direction for future research on cable insulation materials. To develop high performance PP cable insulation materials, the Havriliak-Negami (H-N) model is used to study the impact of grafted molecule types on frequency domain spectroscopy (FDS) of PP insulation in this paper. Research results demonstrate that PP grafted with the irganox 3052 effectively scavenges free radicals within the material, and increases its oxidation induction time (OIT), thus enhancing the thermal stability of PP. Both the voltage stabilizer DA and the irganox 3052 can increase the barrier height <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{\delta})$</tex> for the thermionic migration in PP. PP-g-3052 exhibits a larger <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">δ</inf> compared to PP-g-DA, enabling better suppression of thermionic migration and consequently reducing the thermionic polarization. Concurrently, the relationship between conductivity activation energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{\sigma})$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\delta}$</tex> is further studied, with consistent changes observed in both. PP-g-3052 possesses the largest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\sigma}$</tex>, exerts the strongest inhibitory effect on carrier migration, and more effectively enhances the insulation properties of PP.

articleTitle: Correlative Calibration for Space Charge Measurement in Cables Using PEA Method
abstract: As one of the key steps in the development of DC cables, calibration methods for space charge measurements have not been sufficiently investigated. The authors have studied the possibility of obtaining a calibration reference signal in the presence of space charge fluctuations, by correlating the PEA signal with frequency components extracted from bias voltage variations with the use of the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) method. In this paper, the space charge in the cable with insulation thickness of 10 mm was measured and calibrated. The results at room and high temperatures (conductor temperature of about 90°C) were compared.

articleTitle: Effect of Functional Grafting on Breakdown Strength and DC Conductivity of Polypropylene Blend Insulation
abstract: Blending polypropylene (PP) with polyolefin elastomer (POE) is a conventional method for improving mechanical characteristics in cable insulation. However, such blends often suffer from diminished electrical properties. To address this challenge, this study investigates the impact of functional grafting on the dielectric properties of PP blend insulation. Through experimental characterization, the synergistic effects of functional grafting and elastomer blending on the dielectric behavior and mechanical properties of PP are analyzed. The introduction of polar groups during the 3052 grafting process in PP generates deep traps, effectively trapping charge carriers and mitigating their migration, thereby reducing DC volume conductivity. Moreover, 3052 grafting significantly hinders space charge accumulation in PP blend insulation, with PP-3 demonstrating the most effective suppression of space charge injection. Additionally, incorporating 3052 into the PP blend insulation notably enhances its DC breakdown strength. Among the samples tested at the same temperature, PP-3 exhibits the highest DC breakdown strength, indicating superior insulating properties.

articleTitle: Effect of Carbon Black Structure on Charge Accumulation at the Interface between Insulation and Shielding for Thermoplastic Polyethylene Cable
abstract: LLDPE and HDPE blended non-crosslinked insulation materials are considered promising as new environmentally friendly cable insulation materials, due to excellent electrical and mechanical properties. It is necessary to simultaneously develop non-crosslinked semi-conductive shielding materials that match LLDPE/HDPE blends. In this paper, thermoplastic LLDPE/HDPE blend insulation materials and LLDPE/CB semi-conductive composite were prepared. The space charge distribution in the insulation layer under different electric field strengths and times was tested using the pulsed electroacoustic method. The influence of CB structure on charge accumulation at the interface was investigated. The results suggest that adding a small amount of small particle CB can effectively reduce the accumulation of space charge and suppress electric field distortion in the insulation under high electric fields. However, adding excessive small CB black can increase the electric field distortion under high electric fields.

articleTitle: Crystallization Regulation of Cross-Linking Polypropylene Film for Capacitors on High-Temperature Dielectric Property
abstract: In this paper, the dielectric properties of polypropylene (PP) films for capacitors are improved based on irradiation cross-linking technique and adding different contents of nucleating agents. At 125 °C, the irradiated cross-linked films doped with 1 wt% cross-linking agent show the breakdown strength of 560.8 kV/mm and the conductivity of 1.12784 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">‐13</sup> S/m. The results show that the cross-linked structure inhibits the thermal movement of the molecular chains, which improves the dielectric properties of PP films at high temperatures. In addition, the introduction of nucleating agents further improves the breakdown strength and reduces the conductivity of cross-linked PP films. At 125 °C, the breakdown strength of the PP film doped with 1 wt% cross-linking agent and 0.05 wt% nucleating agent is 580.5 kV/mm and the conductivity is 1.02 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">‐13</sup> S/m. On the one hand, the interfacial traps between the crystalline and amorphous regions increase, and on the other hand, the cross-linking degree of the PP films is improved, which promotes the effect of cross-linking modification. This paper provides comprehensive guidance for the practical application of PP films at high temperatures.

articleTitle: Thermal Ageing of an Extrudable Fluorinated Polymer for Aerospace Application
abstract: The use of fluorinated polymers is proving increasingly attractive in the context of the energy transition and the move to all-electric propulsion in the aerospace industry. The fluoropolymer investigated in this work is Perfluoroalkoxy (PFA), which is derived from PTFE and retains the same mechanical properties between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-200^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+250^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, although it has a significant advantage over PTFE in that it is compatible with extruded technology. We measured the conduction current of power cables insulated with PFA at various temperatures between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$150^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$260^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and by applying a DC voltage with positive and negative polarity as a function of ageing time. We report that from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and on, an asymmetry phenomenon appears between the transient currents under positive and negative polarity. This asymmetry is accompanied by a disproportionate increase in current levels under negative polarity as we approach the maximum operating temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$260^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. The probable causes of this asymmetry and the increase in current levels under negative polarity relative to positive polarity are discussed. The migration of positive ions, thermal degradation and the release of trapped charges as well as the interface between the PFA electrodes could be the cause of this phenomenon.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Electric Field in a DC Model Cable During Superimposed Impulse Voltage Tests
abstract: Superimposed impulse voltage tests are performed as a part of the qualification of HVDC cable systems. The electro-thermal preconditioning prior to the impulse tests may lead to the accumulation of space charges in cable insulation, which eventually affects the resulting electrical field. Such an impact was evaluated in this work using the bipolar charge transport model with inclusion of ionic charge carriers. The results show that the preconditioning gives rise to the inhomogeneity of the electrical stress, specifically it leads to an electric field enhancement near inner radial position during the impulse tests of opposite polarity and near outer radial position under impulse tests of same polarity. Contribution of cable temperature and the generation and transport of ionic charges were thereafter studied and discussed.

articleTitle: Effect of Antioxidant Grafting on the Dielectric Properties of Polypropylene Insulation
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of melt radical graft modification of the hindered phenolic antioxidant (AO3052) on the insulating dielectric properties of polypropylene (PP). Conductivity and breakdown characteristics of grafted PP with varying antioxidant contents are examined. The results indicate that antioxidant grafting enhances the sensitivity of conductivity to temperature. The DC and aging breakdown strengths of PP grafted with different antioxidant contents are analyzed, and 0.5 wt% antioxidant can improve the DC breakdown strength of PP at 90 °C by 31.3% and improve the aging breakdown strength at 90 °C by 36.1%. Through trap distribution and energy band structure analysis, it is inferred that antioxidant grafting modification introduces additional local energy levels and potential traps in the forbidden bands of PP, thereby inhibiting charge transport.

articleTitle: The Impact of Needle Electrode Curvature Radius on Space Charge Distribution Evolution: A Combined Experiment and Simulation Study
abstract: The insulation of electric power equipment inevitably generates non-uniform electric fields due to internal impurities and irregular electrodes. However, the measurement of space charge distribution under non-uniform electric fields remains insufficient. In this study, based on the previous research of space charge measurement under uneven electric fields, a comprehensive investigation on the space charge distribution in epoxy resin under the influence of varying needle electrode curvature radii was conducted. A dynamic combination of experiment and simulation was employed to measure and reconstruct the space charge distribution, and the impact of needle electrode curvature radius on space charge evolution was analyzed. The results show that the distribution of space charge has similar characteristics under different needle electrode curvature radius, and the peak value of charge density all appears inside the sample and gradually moves to the depth of the sample with time. As the curvature radius decreases, the initial electric field intensity and charge injection increase. The electric field of space charge weakens the electric field of the needle surface, especially with a smaller curvature radius, resulting in a greater decrease in the peak of space charge density over time.

Author Keywords: a combination of experiment and simulation

articleTitle: Enhancing the Piezoelectric Properties of Bacterial Cellulose Films by Incorporation of ZnO Nanoparticles
abstract: Bacterial cellulose (BC) is often used as a functional layer material for piezoelectric sensors due to its degradability. However, its weak piezoelectric properties become a key constraint for its further application. In this paper, BC composites containing zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles were prepared by physical blending method from improving their piezoelectric properties, and the changes of their piezoelectric properties were investigated and analyzed. The results show that the piezoelectric constant of the composite has been increased by about five times to 26 pC/N and maintains a fairly good sensitivity to clearly distinguish different external forces. In addition, the dielectric constant increased slightly, becoming 1.5 times higher at low frequencies. This paper provides a reference for the development of high-quality self-powered sensors, which has a certain reference value for the innovation and development of secondary equipment in power system transmission and distribution lines.

articleTitle: Quasi-2D Finite Volume Modeling of Corona Discharges for Ionic Propulsion: Comparison of Reduced Reaction Schemes
abstract: In this work the effects of different plasma kinetic models on the results of a corona discharge simulation are investigated. The discharge model is based on the time dependent drift-diffusion approximation and uses a quasi-2D finite volume approach. Simulations are carried out considering a wire-to-wire geometry, in which the electrode radii and their distance have been fixed. The electric current, number densities and the electro-hydro-dynamic force yielded by different treatments of the chemical source term in the continuity equation are compared. We find that the employed kinetic model has a significant impact on the computed electro-hydro-dynamic force. This is particularly important to accurately predict the performance of plasma devices for aerospace applications, such as ionic thrusters.

articleTitle: Effect of Halloysite Nanotubes on the Properties of LLDPE/HNT Composites for the Cable Industry
abstract: Polymer composites based on linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) with halloysite nanotubes (HNT) offer great promise for developing low-fire hazard cables due to their proven fire-retardant properties. However, incorporating HNT into a non-polar polymer matrix inevitably changes the composites’ polarity, homogeneity, and thermal properties. Consequently, this can lead to a degradation of the dielectric and mechanical properties. This work describes such changes for LLDPE/HNT composites that differ in the amount of HNT present in the LLDPE matrix. A series of LLDPE/HNT composites with filling levels of 1, 3, and 7 wt% of HNT and pure LLDPE as the reference material were prepared by extrusion. Dielectric properties such as volume resistivity, dielectric strength, complex relative permittivity, and dissipation factor were determined. Tensile tests and cone calorimetry were also carried out to enhance the characterization of the tested materials regarding dielectric properties and other parameters necessary for using the tested materials as cable insulation. Adding HNT to LLDPE up to 7 wt% has no substantial effect on the mechanical parameters. However, due to its molecular polarity, HNT significantly deteriorates the dielectric parameters at 7 wt% of HNT. The results obtained using the cone calorimeter show that adding HNT reduces the value of the maximum heat release rate curve and the burning time. Burning of composites with HNT does not produce more smoke than burning of reference LLDPE.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Recognition of Medium Voltage Switchgear Based on CatBoost Model
abstract: Medium voltage switchgear is a part of the power distribution system. During the operation and maintenance of switchgear, partial discharge (PD) detection is usually an important means of diagnosing insulation defects. Therefore, accurate identification of PD signals under different types of insulation defects is essential. Previous algorithms in the ensemble learning gradient boosting framework have problems, such as overfitting and low recognition accuracy. This paper introduces the use of Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) algorithm, to identify PD signals in switchgear. The algorithm is the improvement of Gradient Boosting Tree (GBT) algorithm with strong generalization ability. Statistical features of PD signals under different insulation defects are used as inputs to train the model. The result shows that the CatBoost algorithm can efficiently identify PD signals, and evaluate the insulation performance of the switchgear.

articleTitle: Lifetime Evaluation of Photovoltaic Insulating Backsheets Based on Elongation at Break Considering the Drop-off Rate
abstract: The excessive use of traditional fossil energy has led to energy crisis and environmental pollution. It is increasingly essential to use photovoltaic power generation technology to prevent energy crisis. As the core component of photovoltaic module, the service life of the insulating backsheet is crucial for the reliability of the modules. However, the backsheet is susceptible to various environmental stresses, which accelerates the aging progress and reduces the service life of the backsheet. Traditional life evaluation models are difficult to accurately quantify the degree of degradation of the backsheets. In this paper, a life evaluation model utilizing elongation at break based on the drop-off rate is developed to investigate the lifetime of backsheets under the influence of temperature and ultraviolet irradiation. This research provides the valuable reference for establishing the life evaluation model of the polymeric backsheets.

articleTitle: Effect of Thermal Aging on the Dielectric Properties of Polypropylene/Elastomer Cable Insulation
abstract: This paper focuses on the effect of thermal aging on the properties of polypropylene (PP) and thermoplastic polyolefin (TPO) blending system cable insulation. The PP/TPO samples are subjected to an accelerated thermal aging test at 135 ℃ for 168, 336, 720, and 1440 hours in an incubator. The Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) test is applied to analyze the changes in functional groups in the PP/TPO insulation. The result of FI-IR indicates that the carbonyl group increases after aging. The Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) shows that the average area of TPO increases. In the initial stage of the PP/TPO insulation, the fragmented spherulites will undergo recrystallization, making the fragmented spherulites perfect, leading to an increase in melting enthalpy and an increase in the resistivity of PP/TPO insulation. In the later stage of the PP/TPO insulation, the molecular chain of PP/TPO insulation is broken seriously, leading to the broken of the spherulites, thus decreasing the resistivity. The break of the chain of the PP/TPO insulation makes the low-density area increase, thus reducing the breakdown strength of PP/TPO insulation. The increasing average area of TPO makes the stress more concentrated in PP/TPO insulation, leading to a decrease in the mechanical characteristics.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Dielectric Behavior of Silicone Gel Under Long-term High Temperature Service
abstract: As a polymer with stable chemical properties and electrical strength, silicone gel is widely used in the packaging of IGBT. With the development of IGBT towards higher power, the reliability of packaging materials has attracted wide attention. In this research, a blast drying oven was used to simulate high-temperature service conditions in accelerated thermal aging tests. Broadband dielectric spectroscopy and power frequency breakdown voltage experimental test platforms were used to characterize the dielectric behavior of silicone gels at different aging stages. Finally, the mechanism was discussed by FTIR test. The experimental results show that ε' does not vary much in the frequency range, while ε” produces a relaxation phenomenon. In considering the influence of service time, the polarization is more pronounced due to the exposure of the shedding of the side chains and the Si-O-Si main chain to the electric field, which leads to an upward trend in both the ε' and ε'’. Similarly, due to the increase of free volume and the increase of microdefect, the power frequency breakdown electric field strength of the sample decreases. This research provides a basis for the performance improvement of silicone gel.

articleTitle: The Role of Defect Aspect Ratio in the Partial Discharge Phenomenology under DC Voltage and Temperature Gradient
abstract: This research is focused on the influence of defect aspect ratio on partial discharge (PD) activity within solid dielectrics subjected to direct current (DC) stress and thermal gradients. Employing finite element method (FEM) simulations by Comsol Multiphysics software, the PD inception conditions under both transient and steady-state voltage conditions was evaluated. The focus centered on investigating the effect of charge injection at the dielectric-cavity interface and the subsequent migration of these charges through the gas medium within the defect. This migration was studied through a laminar flow model considering ionized air movement within the defect, driven by the electric field. Treating the charge motion within the cavity akin to an electric current, an equivalent gas conductivity characteristic of the cavity was derived. The findings show that the shape of the defect profoundly influences the variability of equivalent gas conductivity within the defect during both voltage ramp-up and stable phases.

articleTitle: Cold Behavior of Dielectric Esters
abstract: Natural (NE) and synthetic esters (SE) immersed transformers initially limited to low voltage equipment are becoming more and more diffused in any type of electrical applications (generation, transmission, distribution, industrial) regardless power and voltage. Due to their chemical composition esters exhibit limited performances at low temperatures which must be carefully evaluated in case of application in cold climate countries. Especially in hydraulic generation plant or offshore windfarm, transformers may be taken out-of-service for longer times (days or weeks) and crystallization phenomena may occur. In such cases the measure of pour-point is partially meaningless and “cold and hold” performance must be assessed by testing fluidity after a prolonged standing time at very low temperature.

articleTitle: Enhanced Dielectric Properties of Recycled PLA/BaTiO3 Nanocomposites: Towards Sustainable Capacitor Applications
abstract: Recycled polylactic acid (R-PLA)/BaTiO3 nanocomposite films were successfully prepared using solution blending and hot-pressing methods. The dielectric properties of the R-PLA nanocomposites with different volume fractions of BaTiO3 nanoparticles (nBT) were investigated using dielectric spectroscopy and compared to fresh commercial polylactic acid (C-PLA) nanocomposites. R-PLA nanocomposites exhibited promising dielectric properties with high permittivity and low loss tangent, comparable to those of C-PLA nanocomposites. At 1 kHz, both pure C-PLA and R-PLA exhibited a consistent permittivity value of 4. Additionally, they demonstrated promising permittivity values of 10 when filled with nBT at a volume fraction (fnBT) of 0.20. Interestingly, at 1 kHz, the R-PLA nanocomposite exhibited a lower loss tangent (0.009) compared to the C-PLA (0.013), indicating its potential for improved dielectric performance in capacitor applications and highlighting the viability of plastic waste derived from recycled PLA as a promising alternative in the dielectric fields.

articleTitle: Optimizing Printing Parameters on Dielectric Properties in Additive Manufacturing
abstract: With additive manufacturing, fast, cost-effective, and complex productions are possible to further establish its application in energy technology. A diverse array of parameters, including factors such as infill, component orientation, printing speed and printing temperature, can be intentionally adjusted. The application of experimental design in 3D-printing enables a systematic analysis of this extensive range of printing parameters to comprehend their distinct impacts on print quality. This methodology aids in determining the optimal settings for dielectric properties. Once the test specimen has been produced, the dissipation factor and the relative dielectric constant are determined in a range from 1 Hz to 5 kHz. A D-optimal experimental design is used to optimize the parameters. The parameter infill has a significant influence on the dielectric properties. The dissipation factor and relative permittivity increases. Furthermore, printing time can be reduced without causing a significant deterioration in dielectric properties. The application of design of experiments in the variation of 3D-printing parameters provided precise insights into their effects on the electrical properties.

articleTitle: Scale Change Approach to Assess Thermo-oxidative Degradation in NMN Insulating Paper
abstract: This paper presents the first step of a more global scale change approach, which aims to better understand the failure mechanisms during thermo-oxidative ageing by correlating a set of monitored parameters from a material (micro) to a system/assembly (macro) point of view. This multi-level approach requires modelling the failure mechanisms for individual sub-systems from a large electrical insulating system, such as rotating machines. The object studied in this work is a triplex structure of aramid-fibre paper/polyethylene terephthalate/aramid-fibre paper. AC breakdown of the triplex has been first modelled using a voltage divider principle and then compared with experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Influence of Moisture Absorption on Space Charge Accumulation in Liquid Silicone Rubber Under High DC Electric Field
abstract: Dielectric elastomer (DE) possesses great potential in application for ocean wave energy conversion (WEC) due to favorable stretchability, high energy conversion efficiency, fast electromechanical response and low loss. As a critical component of WEC system, DE materials are inevitably exposed to moisture absorption which may deteriorate the mechanical and electrical properties, further affecting the longterm operation and service life of the system. Moreover, when a high DC voltage is applied, the injection, accumulation and transport of space charge transport will distort the electric field distribution in the dielectric, which is related closely to the breakdown performance. In this paper, liquid silicone rubber (LSR) films, were put in a chamber with high humidity (97%) at 56.5℃ to absorb moisture for different amounts of time. The effect of water absorption on space charge behavior of LSR and post-cured LSR under different applied DC electric fields is discussed using a pulsed electro-acoustic method (PEA) measurement system. The results show that the post-curing process reduces the charge accumulation and modifies the electric field distribution in LSR. The accumulated charge is seen to increase with increasing water uptake, in both LSR and post-cured LSR. The maximum electric field distortion of wet post-cured LSR is lower than wet LSR.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of Non-coalescence Outcomes for Different-sized Conducting Droplets Suspended in a Dielectric Liquid
abstract: The application of a strong electric field to water-in-oil emulsions is frequently used for phase separation owing to an electrical coalescence phenomenon. The present study is aimed to analyze numerically the probability of undesirable outcomes in the case when contacting droplets suspended in oil are of different sizes. Computations are based on the arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) approach. The present study extends available data on non-coalescence outcomes that were obtained for equal-sized droplets and analyzes the scope of applicability of those simplified cases. It is shown that the threshold between complete and partial coalescence of different-sized droplets is nearly equal to that for equal-sized ones with the size of the bigger droplet from the former pair if the radius ratio is between 0.5 and 2. The partial coalescence yields many small droplets in the most cases and, in some cases, results in electrospraying inside the gap between two main droplets.

articleTitle: Cable System Setup for PD Measuring Systems Tests and Analysts Training
abstract: Usually, developers of partial discharge (PD) measuring systems have difficulties to test their new functionalities or the improvements made in the existing ones. Furthermore, when a new PD measuring system is acquired by an electrical company, the subsequent training period for qualified analysts may be particularly complicated. This is because on many occasions, demanding and costly laboratory assemblies or even real installations already in operation are required for the measurements of representative PD activity and background noise. Furthermore, when using laboratory or real installations, the performance of repetitive tests anywhere for comparison purposes is not possible, due to logistics problems and to the stochastic phenomena of the PD generated. In this paper, a solution to solve these difficulties is presented. This solution is based on the development of a novel scale test setup designed to simulate a three-phase cable system. PD activity and noise conditions are simulated in the test setup injecting, in a controlled way, signals using an analog generator. The setup is useful both, for testing PD measuring systems´ functionalities and for training analysts.

articleTitle: Significantly Improving Energy Storage Performance of BOPP Films Based on Surface Polymer Layer
abstract: The lower energy storage density limits the further application of biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films. In this paper, a low-temperature plasma method was used to polymerize polymathic methacrylate with high dielectric constant on the surface of BOPP film in situ. The experimental results show that the PMMA layer with appropriate thickness can improve the direct current (DC) breakdown strength to 774.9 kV/mm, which is 8.4% higher than that of pure BOPP (715.1 kV/mm). The highest discharge energy density also reaches 5.72 J/cm3, accompanied by a charge-discharge efficiency of 91.4%. This paper can provide a new perspective and method for improving the dielectric and energy storage performance of BOPP films.

articleTitle: Effect of Low Temperature on Energy Storage Performance of Polypropylene Film
abstract: In this paper, the dielectric and energy storage properties of biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films at low temperature are reported. The experimental results show that the highest direct current (DC) breakdown strength of BOPP films as high as 906.7 kV/mm is obtained at ‐40 °C, signifying a substantial 23.4% enhancement compared to the performance observed at 20 °C. Furthermore, the maximum discharge energy density attains 7.61 J/cm3, achieving a commendable efficiency level of 90.77%. Carriers are subjected to a degree of freezing at low temperatures, inhibiting injection and migration, which diminishes the conductivity current. In addition, the vitreous molecular chain structure can have higher intermolecular forces to protect the molecular chain from being destroyed. This paper provides a new direction and insight for the development of film capacitors with high energy density and low loss.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Surface Charge Accumulation on Epoxy Insulator in DC-GIS Considering Temperature Gradient
abstract: Surface charges accumulated on the epoxy insulator of direct-current gas-insulated switchgear (DC-GIS) are considered a crucial issue that weakens insulation reliability. The temperature gradient arising from the heating of central conductor has a great impact on the charge accumulation. In this article, an improved numerical simulation considering temperature gradient has been proposed. The dynamic behavior of surface charges was featured by bipolar charge transport model, including charge injection, transport, recombination, trapping and de-trapping. The simulation results showed that as the temperature gradient increased, the peak of negative charge density remained at the grounded electrode-insulator interface, while that of positive charge density shifted to the opposite electrode. A “transport jam” mechanism based on charge mobility was proposed to explain the effect of temperature gradient on charge accumulation patterns. Although in most cases, high temperature gradient will distort the electric field, an appropriate temperature gradient can homogenize the field by influencing the surface charge distribution.

articleTitle: Effect of Electric Field Profile Changes on Partial Discharge Phenomenon in a Loaded HVDC Cable
abstract: This paper deals the effect of electric field distribution on the triggering of partial discharge phenomenon in a loaded HVDC model cable. The electric field profiles have been obtained starting from the measurement of space charge accumulation carried out by means of a novel PEA cell. Measurement results show that the electric field distribution along the radial direction of the cable changes during the application of a DC high voltage stress and thermal gradient. In particular, it has been observed that after 20 minutes of the beginning of the test the maximum value of the electric field moves from the inner to the outer dielectric interface. This increment, occurring in correspondence of the cable radius in which a defect is present, reaches the electric field inception of PD.

articleTitle: Interface Charge Characteristics of Silicone Elastomer/AlN Double Layer Dielectric Used in the Power Module Under DC Voltage
abstract: Silicone elastomer and AlN (Aluminium nitride) is commonly used as insulation structure in high-voltage silicon carbide power electronic devices. Under the strong electric field, there is space charge accumulation at the interface, which affect the electric field distribution and further affect its insulation performance. In this paper, the interface charge characteristics of silicone elastomer and AlN are studied by using Pulsed Electro-Acoustic (PEA) method. The experimental results show that there is space charge accumulation at the interface of silicone elastomer and AlN. A method for calculating the electric field at the interface between metal and dielectric in double-layer dielectric structure is presented. In addition, a calculation method of dielectric interface charge density considering the influence of space charge is proposed.

articleTitle: Enhancing High-Temperature Aeronautic Cables with Extruded Perfluoroalkoxy: Insights from Partial Discharge and Polarization Current Analysis
abstract: Developing high-temperature (HT) cables for aeronautics and aerospace becomes essential due to increased power needs and elevated temperatures. Researchers are exploring extrudable materials, to mitigate internal air voids, thus, reducing the risk of potential partial discharges (PDs). Perfluoroalkoxy (PFA) has been highlighted as a promising material. This study examines two PFA extruded cable designs differing in insulation layers, single and co-extrusion with a semi-conductive (SC) layer, both maintaining identical PFA insulation thickness. The research involves measurements of Partial Discharge Inception Voltage (PDIV) at various temperatures and pressures, in addition to Polarization Current (PC) measurements under a controlled temperature gradient. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of PFA extruded HT cables in improving PDIV and reducing PC in the co-extrusion design with inner SC layer.

articleTitle: Dielectric and Molecular Structure Characteristics of Biaxial Polypropylene under DC/AC Mixed Voltage
abstract: To investigate the dielectric properties and molecular structural properties of biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films under DC/AC mixed voltages, compare the differences between domestic and foreign BOPP films, and promote the localization process of BOPP, this article selects five types of BOPP films from both domestic and foreign countries for dielectric testing and infrared spectroscopy testing. The test results show that the relative permittivity of all samples remains basically unchanged with the increase of DC voltage; the dissipation factor increases in the low frequency range of voltage and decreases in the high frequency range. Under high DC voltage, the dissipation factor of BOPP can be attributed to additives and impurities during the production process. At any DC/AC mixed voltage, the infrared spectra of all BOPP films doesn't change significantly, indicating that the chemical structure of polypropylene molecules has strong stability.

articleTitle: Ageing of Aeronautical Cables Exposed to Partial Discharges: The Effects of Voltage Frequency
abstract: In this work, the behavior of the electrical insulation system of an aeronautical tape wound PTFE power cable in presence of partial discharges (PDs) was investigated in terms of time to failure as a function of the characteristics of an AC applied voltage. The electrical insulation of specimens was submitted to an intense electric field by applying voltage to the conductor, while a grounded metallic braid covered the outer surface of the insulation. An AC mean frequency (14-56 kHz) voltage was set above partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) of the cable. Aging with PDs was carried out at constant voltage amplitude. For each voltage frequency, seven specimens were tested. Time to failure (dielectric breakdown) for each specimen was recorded and different parameters such as surface temperature and dissipated discharge power were measured during the ageing.

articleTitle: Enhanced Dielectric Properties of Polypropylene Film by Multilayered Structural Design for Power Capacitor
abstract: In this paper, multilayered structural design is proposed for improving the dielectric performance of polypropylene (PP) film for power capacitor. The maleic anhydride-grafted polypropylene (MA-g-PP) and tris (4-aminophenyl) amine (TAPA) are selected as additives. The results show that the composite film with PP/TAPA layer close to anode and PP/MA-g-PP layer close to cathode exhibits the best dielectric properties. The leakage conductivity drops by 87.9% at 30 °C and declines by 94.9% at 115 °C. The breakdown strength is improved by 12.9% at 30 °C and enhanced by 19.9% at 115 °C. The simulation results of electrostatic potential and molecular orbital indicate that the MA-g-PP and TAPA could capture free electrons and free holes injected from the electrodes respectively, thereby blocking the charge transport path. The multilayered structural design leads to the carriers accumulating in the outer layers, and the reverse electric field formed reduces the possibility of carriers entering the dielectric through the injection barrier. This method supplies a reference for improving the dielectric properties of PP films, which provides theoretical guidance for surface modification and additive selection.

articleTitle: Fundamental Study for Correction Technique in Space Charge Measurements of Cables under Load-cycle Using Pulsed Electro-Acoustic Method
abstract: This paper discusses a correction technique for space charge measurements in cables under load cycling using the pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method. In general, the functions, such as the system impulse response, required to convert measured waveforms into charge distributions are extracted under the same thermal conditions as the measured waveforms. However, it is not feasible to obtain the system impulse response for all transient temperature conditions under a load cycle temperature condition where the temperature changes from time to time. Therefore, we proposed the method of using the impulse response measured at different temperatures for the conversion. It was found that the root mean square error in the electric field distribution was up to about 3.4% with respect to the average electric field by using our proposed method. This result supports the conclusion that the method proposed in this paper is applicable to the conversion of waveforms into charge distributions under load cycle temperature conditions.
