articleTitle: Evaluating Lifespan of Corona Armor Tape in Form-Wound Rotating Machines
abstract: In form-wound rotating machines, corona armor tape (CAT) is deployed as an outer layer over the coil-insulating materials. However, the CAT is susceptible to degradation caused by ozone, which is generated by partial discharges (PDs). Understanding the CAT's durability in actual operating conditions is crucial, necessitating a precise technique for estimating the CAT's lifespan. This study aims to predict the CAT's lifespan using the Arrhenius law based on chemical reaction kinetics. We focus on the relationship between ozone production and discharge power, and we attempt to predict the CAT's lifespan at any temperature using the Arrhenius plot, with the of PD power serving as a critical parameter. Our findings reveal that the activation energy required for CAT degradation is lower at higher temperatures. Furthermore, the CAT's lifespan at any given temperature is found to exhibit a direct correlation with the power discharged during PD; this underscores the significant impact of discharge power on CAT durability.

articleTitle: Improvement of High-Temperature Energy Storage Performance of PI with Non-planar Structures
abstract: Polyimide (PI) is kind of a commonly used high temperature resistant polymer materials, whose high thermal stability depends on its rigid heterocyclic structures. However, the charge transfer between the diamine and the dianhydride unit is not conducive to dielectric and capacitive properties at high temperatures. In order to destroy the planar conjugated system to a certain extent, three-dimensional structures is introduced into the molecular chain of three different kinds of dianhydride units during the synthesis of PI film materials in this paper, aiming to hinder the carrier movement process, increase the electric and thermal resistance, and finally achieve the improvement of comprehensive capacitive performances. Results show that a proper number of non-planar multi-chain or spiral structures can effectively improve the DC breakdown strength of the films by up to 65.2%. At the same time, due to the improvement of efficiency, the maximum energy storage density of the composite films is approximately doubled at 200 ℃, showing a huge potential in the field of high-temperature energy storage.

articleTitle: Ability of Thermal Method of Measuring Electric Fields at Metal-Polymer and Metal-Semicon Interfaces: An Experimental Study
abstract: Understanding and modelling space charge at interfaces is fundamental as they are weak points of any system including layers with different electrical properties. The Thermal Pulse Method (TPM) may allow micronic resolutions near the thermally excited surface, especially if combined with surface temperature measurements. The present work aims to TPM fallbacks for directly measuring electric fields at interfaces of structures containing metallic, semiconducting, and insulating layers. 50 µm to 160 µm-thick polyethylene samples with and without coated semicon layers are used. They are provided with metallic electrodes deposited either directly on the dielectric or on the semicon layers, to act as bolometers for measuring the surface temperature. A dedicated measurement cell allows measurement, separation and amplification of both space charge and bolometric signals. The experimental set-up is detailed, and results obtained on the different type of samples are discussed. They show that the proposed setup and analysis of space charge and temperature responses measured simultaneously at the interface should allow direct measurement of the electric field at metal/insulator interfaces, and, surprisingly, also at metal/semicon interfaces.

articleTitle: Effect of Antioxidant on Irradiation Resistance of PP Composites for Nuclear Cable Insulation
abstract: This study investigates effect of antioxidants on irradiation resistance of polypropylene (PP) utilized as insulation materials for nuclear cables. Samples comprising isotactic PP (iPP) and Irganox 1010 of 0.1 wt% are irradiated using a Cobalt-60 gamma-ray at the dose range of 0 to 250 kGy. Trap distribution and AC breakdown strength are measured to evaluate the electrical performance with irradiation. The microstructure of the sample is analyzed using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Results reveal that unirradiated samples with Irganox 1010 (P10) exhibit shallower traps, but such samples demonstrate improved irradiation resistance with increasing doses. Compared with PP samples, P10 samples exhibit weakened oxidation, a marginal decrease in melting point, deeper carrier traps, and higher AC breakdown strength after the irradiation. However, the positive effect of Irganox 1010 on PP becomes less distinct with increasing irradiation dose.

articleTitle: Generalizing Numerical Simulation Results for Droplet Electrodeformation Threshold Under Pulsed DC Voltage
abstract: The phenomenon of electocoalescence involves the intensification of the merging of small conductive droplets dispersed in a dielectric liquid. This phenomenon is fundamental to the crucial processes of dehydration and desalting in the oil industry. Recent studies have indicated the potential superiority of pulsed voltage over traditionally used alternating voltages at industrial frequencies and constant voltage. However, the question of the optimal parameters for pulsed voltage remains open. One challenge in determining these optimal parameters is the fact that characteristic frequencies determining droplet behavior depend on droplet size and fluids properties. The objective of this research is to generalize the frequency dependence for a critical characteristic, such as the threshold voltage for droplet rupture. We employ a numerical model based on the Arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian (ALE) method to generate a dataset across a wide range of droplet radii, demonstrating how dimensionless parameters can generalize the results. The study reveals that varying the droplet radius alters characteristic frequencies in a specific pattern, providing insights valuable for determining pulse parameters in experimental planning for coalescence applications.

articleTitle: Space Charge Accumulation and DC Breakdown Strength of Epoxy Nanocomposites
abstract: Introduction of inorganic nanoparticles to epoxy composite material has been demonstrated to have a significant advantage in electrical insulation performance for use in power apparatus. In order to apply nanocomposites to solid insulators in DC power equipment, it is important to evaluate the electrical insulation properties of nanocomposites under DC high voltage. It is well understood that space charges accumulating inside insulating materials can lead to premature failure. In this work, the space charge and DC breakdown of epoxy nanocomposites with nano-BN or TiO2 were investigated. The space charge accumulation can locally increase the effective electric field strength in a region of the insulator and thus leads to a dielectric breakdown. It was previously demonstrated that specific types of nanocomposites can reduce space charge accumulation. The nanocomposites prepared in this study do not suppress space charge accumulation, which could be due to the presence of micrometric-size agglomerates in the nanocomposites prepared in this study. Furthermore, the effect of the agglomerates on space charge accumulation and DC breakdown strength depends on the nanofiller.

articleTitle: Partial Discharges at Boundaries of Oil-Pressboard Immersed in Mixed Insulating Oils
abstract: Liquid and solid insulation work alongside in the transformer to efficiently insulate and cool it. Coadoption and compatibility of both insulations are responsible for the transformer's reliable operation and long life. In recent years, ester oils have become the choice for liquid insulation due to excellent biodegradability, high moisture saturation capability, and good dielectric strength. However, the cost of ester oils is relatively high compared to mineral oil, which lead researchers to come up with mixed insulating oils (MIOs) to balance the cost and performance. It is crucial to study the performance of such insulation as a compatible coexistent with solid insulation. Partial discharge (PD) diagnosis provides an inference into the compatible performance under the presence of the electric field. Therefore, this study focuses on studying the PD at the MIO, pressboard and conductor interface. The experiments are carried out in accordance with IEC 60270 on various mixtures of fresh and oxidative aged MIO soaked pressboards. The blended oil soaked pressboards have higher PD inception voltage than those soaked in base oils. The inception voltage is found to reduce with the aging of the oil. The discharges are observed to a large extent in the negative half cycle.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Waveform Analysis Using Dynamic Mode Decomposition
abstract: The increasing use of electrical power equipment in more demanding conditions has led to a greater need for improved reliability and durability. Consequently, there is growing importance placed on research into the diagnosis of electrical insulation. Partial discharge (PD) measurement has emerged as a valuable technique for this purpose, with ongoing research dedicated to understanding the phenomenon and refining measurement methods. Transient earth voltage (TEV) sensors, designed to detect transient voltage on the earthed metalwork of electrical equipment, offer non-intrusive and simplified approaches for routine inspections. However, the relationship between TEV sensor signals and the characteristics of insulating materials remains unclear. This study investigates the influence of grounding wire and coaxial cable on TEV sensor signals, using fast Fourier transform (FFT) and dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) for analysis. The findings reveal that DMD has superior capability in detecting high-frequency components and provide insights into the impact of grounding wire, coaxial cable, and electromagnetic waves generated by PD on specific frequency bands.

articleTitle: Study of the Impact of a DC Electric Field on Charge Distribution at Solid/liquid Interface by Acoustic Method
abstract: Dielectric liquids, employed primarily for cooling or electrical insulation, play a crucial role in High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) systems. When subjected to an external electric field, the distribution of charges at solid/liquid interfaces (Electrical Double Layer) can potentially lead to failures. This paper specifically investigates the influence of an external DC electric field on EDL, using the Pressure Wave Propagation method.

articleTitle: Research on Partial Discharge and Self-Healing Characteristics for Metallized Film of Capacitors
abstract: In this paper, an experimental system is established to characterize the partial discharge (PD) and self-healing (SF) properties of the metallized film based on the actual structure of metallized film capacitors. Compared with the PD signal waveforms of the polypropylene film, internal discharge, surface discharge and SF discharge signal waveforms of the metallized film were investigated and distinguished. Meanwhile, the phase resolved partial discharge spectrum of the metallized film also reflects a variety of discharge types. Through studying the microscopic morphology of metallized films, SF and surface discharge will cause the loss of metal electrodes on the films. The interaction between them will cause the phenomenon of “margin degradation”, which will accelerate the decrease of capacitance, and lead to the deterioration of capacitor performance until the failure. This paper aims to investigate the PD and SF characteristics of the metallized film and provide a theoretical basis for exploring the capacitance loss mechanism with monitoring the operational status of capacitors.

articleTitle: Hetero and Homocharge in LDPE at Low Electric Fields
abstract: Various studies have shown that in Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE), homocharge (like polarity charge) accumulation is likely in the vicinity of electrodes at low electric fields, whereas heterocharge accumulation (opposite polarity charge) is likely at high electric fields. However, the effect of material morphology on the occurrence of homo/heterocharge is not well established. In this work, LDPE samples from two different types of pellets are prepared using the solvent casting technique. The space charge measurements using the Puled-Electro-Acoustic (PEA) method are carried out at an electric field of 20kV/mm. The space charge measurements show a homocharge formation in one sample and a heterocharge formation in the other. This is intriguing and deserves closer attention. FTIR measurements show no significant differences in the chemical composition of these two samples. DSC measurements indicate a higher degree of crystallinity in the sample exhibiting homocharge. A higher crystallinity lowers the mobility of charge carriers preventing heterocharge formation.

articleTitle: Comparison of Properties of High-Temperature Vulcanized Silicone Rubber Between Natural and Artificial Chalking
abstract: Chalking is one of the most important indicators for assessing the aging degree of high-temperature vulcanized silicone rubber (HTV-SR) for composite insulators. Existing artificial chalking methods are able to effectively simulate the chalking phenomenon, but the equivalence between artificial and natural chalking still remains unclear. In this paper, both naturally and artificially chalking samples are obtained. Then the surface morphology and chemical properties of chalked samples are methodically characterized. Finally, artificial and natural chalking degrees are quantitatively compared and analyzed by linear fitting. Experimental results show that the artificially chalking process has a great influence on the filler precipitation but little change to absorption peaks of chemical bonds. Besides, the content of highly oxygenated Si atoms is increased obviously. It turns out that the degree of artificial chalking in this paper is approximated to the degree of mildly natural chalking (aging for 11 years on the grid). This work presents a detailed comparison of properties of naturally chalking (especially with different aging years) and artificially chalking HTV-SR samples.

articleTitle: Effect of Silica Content and Surface Chemistry on the Dielectric Performance of Silicone Rubber
abstract: Commercial silicone rubbers are typically pre-filled with fumed silica (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). Interestingly, such products might still be considered “unfilled” matrices for further nanodielectric improvements rendering interpretation and repeatability challenging. This study reports on the dielectric performance of entirely unfilled silicone rubbers and their (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-) filled counterparts and compares these systems with the commercial Sylgard 184. It is shown that the critical (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) contents vary significantly with surface chemistry. The DC conductivity and dielectric losses of the bespoke systems display “bathtub” characteristics with optimum fill-grades showcasing performance similar or superior to the commercial product.

articleTitle: Ionic Liquid Grafted Silicone Fillers for High Permittivity Dielectric Elastomers
abstract: A novel, high permittivity soft filler was synthesized through the grafting of an ionic liquid to a silicone chain. The filler exhibited low dielectric losses and a high dielectric breakdown relative to other soft, high permittivity silicone fillers due to improved compatibility with the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) network. The fillers were incorporated within a platinum catalyzed commercial PDMS network (Sylgard 184) which resulted in an elastomer with a relative dielectric permittivity of 7.87 at 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> Hz and a dielectric breakdown strength of 27 V µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Data Acquisition Systems for Dielectric Frequency Response Measurements
abstract: This research focuses on evaluating data acquisition (DAQ) systems for Dielectric Frequency Response (DFR) measurements with the aim of determining the most suitable system for precise dielectric characterization. The performance of a 24-bit simultaneous sampling DAQ card and a 16-bit multiplexing DAQ card is compared with a commercial DFR instrument focusing on critical factors such as resolution, sampling frequency, sampling method, and the potential impact of error compensation. The cards are utilized in an experimental setup capable of performing low-voltage DFR measurements with an accuracy comparable to the commercial instrument. A low-loss ceramic capacitor is used as a test object. The results show that the 24-bit simultaneous sampling card has superior performance aligning well with the commercial DFR instrument.

articleTitle: An Investigation into the Influence of Parylene Surface Modification on the Characteristics of Cellulose Insulating Paper for Eco-Friendly Fire-Retardant Transformers
abstract: The development of a novel ester-based oil-paper insulation system represents a crucial advancement in constructing eco-friendly fire-retardant transformers. However, owing to the inherent weak hydrolytic stability of ester-based insulating oil compared to traditional mineral insulating oil, a mutual promotion of hydrolysis occurs between ester-based oil and insulating paper, thereby accelerating the aging process of the oil-paper insulation system. To enhance the stability of the ester-based oil-paper insulation system, this study employed the chemical vapor deposition method, utilizing Parylene materials to create a novel surface-modified insulating paper. The paper systematically evaluated the hydrophobicity, AC breakdown performance, and thermal stability of the modified insulating paper. Results indicated excellent hydrophobicity, with water droplets forming a static contact angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$72.1^{\circ}$</tex> on the paper surface. Moreover, the AC breakdown performance remained unaffected by Parylene surface modification. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed that the inclusion of Parylene material significantly enhanced the thermal stability of the insulating paper. The activation energy for the new insulating paper was determined to be 84.08 kJ/mol, accompanied by a pre-exponential factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.16 \times 10^6$</tex>, surpassing that of the raw insulating paper at 82.03 kJ/mol with a pre-exponential factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.88 \times 10^6$</tex>. This innovative surface modification strategy using Parylene material offers promising advancements in the performance and stability of ester-based oil-paper insulation systems.

articleTitle: Effect of Graft Distribution on Conductivity and Breakdown Strength of Polypropylene Film for Power Capacitor
abstract: In this paper, the maleic anhydride (MA) is grafted onto the polypropylene (PP) molecular chain by UV irradiation. The distribution of maleic anhydride-grafted polypropylene (MA-g-PP) is controlled to investigate the influence of graft distribution on the dielectric performance. The results indicate that the film with MA-g-PP distributed on both sides exhibits the best electrical properties. The leakage conductivity declines by 72.4% at 30 °C and decreases by 89.9% at 115 °C. The breakdown strength is enhanced by 8.1% at 30 °C and improved by 13.9% at 115 °C. Through the analysis of electrostatic potential and molecular orbital, the MA-g-PP could capture carriers and has stronger attraction on free electrons. The carriers trapped on both sides of the film could form a reverse electric field to suppress charge injection, thereby inhibiting the molecular chain structure degradation. This paper provides theoretical guidance for grafting modification from the perspective of charge transport behavior regulation, which facilitates the promotion of film capacitors.

articleTitle: Insulating Capacity of a Sphere-Plane Electrode Arrangement with Thick Dielectric Coating under Negative Lightning Impulse Voltage Stress in Synthetic Air at High Pressures
abstract: Synthetic air is an environmentally friendly alternative to sulfur hexafluoride in gas-insulated switchgear. Hybrid insulation systems are a possible solution to compensate for the inferior dielectric properties. Thick coatings of several millimeters affect the macroscopic electric field distribution. Thus, the maximum electric field strength in the gas volume can be reduced, resulting in a higher streamer inception voltage. The improvement was investigated theoretically and experimentally. A sphere-plane arrangement with different gap distances (20 mm to 60 mm), coating thicknesses (2 mm to 10 mm) and relative permittivities through different groups of materials (EP, RTV 2 SiR, PU) was investigated. Exclusively negative lightning impulse voltage as the critical polarity was applied. The gas pressure of the synthetic air was varied between 0.1 MPa and 1.0 MPa. FEM simulations of the electric field distribution combined with the streamer criterion applied to the gas gap were used to predict the breakdown voltage of the hybrid insulation system. Comparisons between experimental results and simulations of the streamer inception voltage indicate good agreement. The results of this contribution provide a broad basis for the design of hybrid insulation systems in highly pressurized synthetic air.

articleTitle: Galloping Mechanical Characteristics of Overhead Insulated Lines in 10 kV Distribution Network
abstract: Distribution overhead lines are susceptible to strong winds, ice cover and other detrimental factors. In recent years in China, distribution network overhead line galloping faults have occurred from time to time, which have affected people's normal life and caused great economic losses to the country. In this paper, ANSYS Workbench finite element analysis platform is used to establish a three-dimensional model of 10 kV single-file-pitch elliptical cross-section ice-covered overhead insulated line, analyze the aerodynamic characteristics and galloping mechanical characteristics of the line under different wind load conditions, and obtain the variation rule of the galloping amplitude frequency of the line with the wind speed, wind angle of attack and air flow angle of attack. There is a clear functional relationship between wind speed and wind angle of attack and line aerodynamic characteristics, and a weaker but still significant correlation between air flow angle of attack and line aerodynamic characteristics. The results can provide a reference for the design and erection of overhead insulated lines for 10 kV distribution networks, as well as for the prevention and control of galloping.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Detection Beyond the Frequency Ranges of IEC 60270
abstract: Due to the high background noise encountered during on-site partial discharge (PD) detection of power cables, calibrating PD detection systems at low PD levels becomes challenging, resulting in low sensitivity of PD detection systems. Achieving a 1-nC PD charge within the frequency range recommended by IEC 60270, which is lower than 1 MHz, is often difficult in practice. This paper presents an analysis of PD pulse currents in the frequency domain and proposes an alternative approach for PD detection during on-site testing of power cables. In the proposed method, the center frequency for PD detection is shifted to frequencies exceeding one megahertz, which lies outside the recommended frequency ranges of IEC 60270. Typically, the center frequency falls within the range of 1.5 MHz to 2.5 MHz, with a frequency bandwidth of several hundred kilohertz. By utilizing such frequency ranges, the signal-to-noise ratio of the PD pulse current significantly increases compared to the standard approach. Despite falling outside the standard-recommended frequency ranges, this adjustment allows for calibration using a 50-pC PD charge.

articleTitle: Effects of Water Immersion on Silicone Rubber Surface Before and After Exposure to Precipitating Droplets in AC Electric Field
abstract: This work is devoted to studying the aging of high-voltage silicone rubber insulation in the presence of salt fog. The impact of the fog is simulated by spraying a multitude of discrete droplets that settle on the silicone sample surface and roll down over it. Due to the occurrence of partial discharges between the droplets, the hydrophobic rubber becomes hydrophilic. The work examines how preliminary and subsequent water immersion of the samples affects the time of hydrophobicity loss and the water-repellent properties of the samples. Preliminary immersion can decrease the duration required for hydrophobic materials to lose their water-repellent properties. Subsequent water soaking tends to impede the drainage of water from an inclined sample.

articleTitle: Conductivity and Breakdown Strength of Polybutene and Its Copolymer Insulation Varying with Crystal Form
abstract: The article primarily focuses on the impact of crystal form transformation on the breakdown and DC conductivity mechanisms of isotactic polybutene (iPB) and polybutene-block-propylene copolymer (PBA) materials. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was employed to analyze changes in crystallinity and melting peak under different crystal forms. The crystal form transformation of polybutene was studied by X-ray diffraction (XRD). The breakdown strength of polybutene was tested at various temperatures (30, 50, 70, and 90 °C), and the temperature-dependent conductivity characteristics were analyzed using the space charge limited current model (SCLC) and hopping conduction model. The results indicate that crystal form transformation and copolymer modification significantly enhance the insulation performance of polybutene. On one hand, they notably increase the breakdown strength of polybutene at 30 °C and 50 °C, with a slight increase at higher temperatures. On the other hand, fitting results reveal that Ohmic conductivity dominates at low electric fields, while both crystal forms of polybutene can be well described by hopping conduction and SCLC as the electric field increases. The crystal form transformation and copolymer modification broaden the range of Ohmic conduction in polybutene, thereby improving its conductivity characteristics.

articleTitle: Insight into 525 kV HVDC Cable System Performance Through Peeling Characterizations
abstract: This contribution presents methodology for 525 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{kV}$</tex> HVDC extruded cable characterization by means of novel electrical health and ageing assessment methodologies, enabling high statistical certainty in electrical results thanks to the manufacturing of cable peeling test objects. The peeling tests furthermore allow quantifying the electrical properties of virgin and 40-years aged specimens (achieved by means of a prequalification (PQ) test), to improve understanding on the remaining life and electric characteristics of the aged specimens. First, an investigation is performed on space charge accumulation in fresh, PQ aged, thermally aged and electro-thermally aged peeling specimens. Second, conductivity is mapped in fresh peelings as well as their equivalent PQ-aged counterparts, the latter including radial statistics. The results indicated that while some evolution of these electrical parameters can be identified, the aging evolution observed in the PQ test is minimal compared to the more severe aging protocols.

articleTitle: A Modular Fractional-order Circuit Model for Broadband Impedance Characterization of Polymeric Insulation Systems
abstract: Power assets driven by semiconductor devices are developing towards high-voltage (HV), miniaturization, and high-power density, which are posing serious threats, e.g., electrothermal stresses on insulation systems as the weakest points. Therefore, modeling impedance characteristics of insulation systems is a crucial step to support the insulation design and reliability analysis of HV power assets. This paper proposes a modular broadband impedance characteristic modeling approach for insulation systems, which can apply to multifrequency applications. The proposed new impedance circuit model fully considers the intrinsic conductance behavior and relaxation mechanisms of insulation systems over broadband frequencies. Meanwhile, the fractional calculus theory is introduced to assist in modeling the frequencydependent dielectric response characteristics for nonideal insulation systems. The new circuit model is based on in-depth physical insights and is modular and user-friendly. It enables a better representation of the broadband impedance characteristics of insulation systems.

articleTitle: Phase Dependence of Surface Charge Accumulated on Epoxy Insulator in C4F7N/CO2 under AC voltage
abstract: The application of binary gas mixtures consisting of heptafluorobutyronitrile (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>N) and carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) in AC GIS is currently attracting much attention. The charge accumulation on epoxy insulators is a crucial problem restricting the safety of gas-insulated equipment, and whether the charging behavior is phase-dependent hasn't been fully understood yet. In this study, the charge distribution characteristics on a down-scaled disc epoxy insulator surface in C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>N/CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mixtures under AC voltage were investigated, and the influence of the truncated phase and duration of AC voltage on surface charge accumulation were analyzed. The results showed that the area of the negative charge speckle first increased and then decreased over time. However, the phase angle was found to have a negligible impact on the surface charge distribution characteristics of the insulator.

articleTitle: Conductivity and Permittivity of CNT-Epoxy Nanocomposites with Filler Concentrations in the Neighborhood of Percolation Threshold
abstract: This study aims to investigate the effect of the incorporation of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) on the electrical conductivity and permittivity of nanocomposites near the percolation threshold. The study is performed by tuning the concentration of CNT nanoparticles. This modifies the interparticle distance that governs the charge transfer mechanism between nanotubes. The percolation threshold of a composite is defined as the filler concentration at which the formation of a continuous conductive pathway through the matrix is initiated, at this critical concentration, the composite transitions from an insulating to a conducting material. The percolation threshold of a MWCNT -filled epoxy composite is determined, and the conductivity and permittivity of the composites with filler concentrations in the vicinity of the threshold are investigated.

articleTitle: Unveiling Internal Partial Discharges in Wiring and Cable Systems with Novel Testing Method
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) is a pivotal concern in the design of reliable wiring and cable systems for aeronautical application. Today, standardized PD tests for cables strongly rely on experimental setups and the quality of sample preparation, lacking the ability to distinguish between external and internal PD events. In the light of these challenges, this paper presents a novel testing device designed to characterize internal PD in wires and power cables under various environmental conditions for aeronautic. The method involves immersing a portion of the specimen in Gallium liquid metal to establish a counter electrode while managing triple points at the Gallium/sample interface by introducing dielectric liquid on top. Results indicate notable variations in Partial Discharge Inception Voltage (PDIV) values based on testing method, with the proposed technique consistently yielding lower PDIV values and exclusively assessing internal PD, unlike other traditional methods.

articleTitle: Effects of Bending Stress on the Propagation of Abnormally Shaped Electrical Trees in PP
abstract: This study investigates the impact of bending stress on the electrical tree characteristics of polypropylene (PP) cable insulation. Pure PP and impact polypropylene copolymer (IPC) are selected as the base materials. Electrical tree growth experiments were conducted at various bending curvature radii. The findings indicate that bending stress accelerates the growth of electrical trees, leading to insulation breakdown of iPP within 5 minutes at a curvature radius of 10 mm. Additionally, bending stress significantly alters the electrical tree morphology. Under extreme bending, iPP tends to form a single-trunk morphology, whereas IPC, with the introduction of elastic chain segments, enhances the dispersion of electrical trees, mitigating the inclination to develop along a linear trajectory. Consequently, IPC insulation exhibits promising potential for cables operating under bending conditions.

articleTitle: Investigating Effects of Composite Dielectric Material Components and Temperature on Breakdown Strength
abstract: Breakdown measurements under applied AC voltage stress at a constant temperature are presented for pure epoxy, epoxy containing mica tape and epoxy containing glass mat tape. These form the individual components of the composite insulation system as used in the main dipole bending magnets at the ISIS neutron and muon source. Results are presented as Weibull plots from which characteristic breakdown fields (scale), and shape parameters are calculated. Subsequently the measurements are repeated over temperature on epoxy samples containing mica. A slight decrease in breakdown strength occurred when glass fibre mat was included, whereas the presence of mica caused a significant increase. The difference in breakdown strength between the different sample types are discussed in terms of the theories of electrical breakdown, and ultimately were related to the tensile strength of the corresponding materials.

articleTitle: Effect of Atmospheric Air Pressure and Electrode Curvature on Air Breakdown Voltage & Surface Flashover of Solid Dielectric with Same Clearance & Creepage Distances
abstract: This paper presents measurements of Surface Partial Discharge Inception Voltage (SPDIV) and Flashover (FOV) Voltage on needle/plan and rod/plane configurations with thin polyimide film Kapton representing 5mm of creepage distance for different air pressure (90 mbar to 1002 mbar). In addition, using the same electrode configurations, Breakdown (BDO) Voltage of air is measured without insulation, and with the same distance between electrodes (clearance distance) for the same air pressure conditions. This study is a contribution for the understanding of the effect of the presence of solid dielectric between electrodes on surface dielectric strength under aeronautical air pressure constraint.

articleTitle: Breakdown Strength Study of Barium Titanate Ceramics for Power Electronics Applications
abstract: The present study is related to the compactness issues of power electronic modules and the integration of functions within their assemblies. It focuses on the dielectric properties of titanate-based ceramic material shaped by Spark Plasma Sintering. With such a process, barium titanate dense ceramic demonstrates high relative permittivity with low dielectric losses, presenting a particular interest for being an embedded decoupling capacitor. The aim of this work is to characterize the influence of different parameters, such as ceramic pellets’ thickness, densification, and permittivity on their breakdown strength under DC voltage stress.

articleTitle: Study on Accelerated Deterioration and Early Failure Mechanism of Silicone Elastomers Under Nanosecond Pulsed Electric Field
abstract: The pulsed electric field caused by the operating conditions of high-voltage and high-power semiconductor devices will exacerbate the insulation deterioration of silicone elastomers for packaging. This paper will comprehensively study the degradation mechanisms of silicone elastomers under nanosecond pulse electric fields from both macroscopic and microscopic levels. Macroscopically, the study conducts research on bubble discharge under nanosecond pulse electric fields through Comsol simulation. Microscopically, on one hand, the paper investigates the behavior of charge-induced molecular vibrations under nanosecond pulse electric fields; on the other hand, it calculates the dynamic behavior of charges by constructing a molecular dynamics model. The research finds that, macroscopically, nanosecond pulse electric fields lead to charge separation which causes field distortion and triggers bubble discharge, and as the rate of change increases, the discharge current intensifies, the production of ozone increases, and the resultant damage to material insulation is more severe. Microscopically, on one hand, the study reveals that at the edges of nanosecond pulses, charges cannot respond to the rapidly changing electric fields, experiencing greater resultant forces that excite molecular vibrations, which intensify with the increase in the rate of change of the pulse electric field. On the other hand, it is found that the relaxation time of space charges exhibits an exponential increase with the depth of traps, and when the relaxation time matches the frequency of the pulse electric field, electrons enter into resonance, leading to an intensified detrapping. This research will provide a theoretical foundation for improving the insulation performance of encapsulating materials.

articleTitle: Electric Field Mapping by Electro-Optical Probes in Known Geometries Under High Voltage
abstract: This paper reports the use of electro-optical (EO) probes in mapping electric field in known high voltage (HV) geometries (plane-plane and sphere-sphere). The measurements are performed autonomously with the use of a robotic arm and the development of an automatic data acquisition unit. The measured electric field profiles were then compared with finite element analysis (FEA) models calculated in COMSOL software and showed a good agreement with COMSOL. This work is part of the de-risking of non-contact electric field measurements for identifying defects on live cap and pin insulator strings on HV towers.

articleTitle: Mechanoluminescence of Anhydride and Imidazole Cured Epoxies Under the Combined Effect of Thermal and Cyclic Mechanical Stresses
abstract: The luminescence of two crosslinked BA/FDGE epoxy resins under cyclic mechanical and thermal stresses has been studied. Spectra under thermal or combined thermal and mechanical stresses show the same patterns with a maximum around 550 nm indicating that the same molecular groups are responsible for the luminescence under both stresses. The luminescence also shows a delay with the applied stress decreasing with temperature. This study could help elucidate the mechanisms at the origin of mechanoluminescence and thermo-mechanical degradation in epoxy polymers.

articleTitle: Effect of Different Coating Materials on Partial Discharge Characteristics and Electrical Tree of Printed Circuit Board
abstract: Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) are commonly used in power devices. With the development of power electronic technology, the performance of PCBs cannot meet the demand for high switching rates and high-power devices. Some cases of PCB insulation failure are often discovered in power devices. Among them, deterioration in the PCB layer is a very common problem. However, the process of deterioration cannot be observed because of the opacity of PCB. Based on the double-layer PCB, different insulation materials are used to study how the surface insulation material affects PCB degradation. In this paper, the electric tree growth and partial discharge characteristics of different epoxide materials combined with copper-clad laminate were compared and analyzed, and the difference in insulation characteristics was analyzed by pulse sequence analysis (PSA) and phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) pattern. It is found that the discharge characteristics of different materials can be qualitatively judged by the shape of the dV (voltage differences) plot and the distribution of dV. The changes of partial discharge inception voltage can correspond to apparent charge, thus reflecting the insulation properties of materials.

articleTitle: Dielectric Breakdown of Alumina: Effect of Mechanical and Electrical Prestress
abstract: This work studies the influence of the mechanical and electrical constraint on the dielectric and mechanical breakdown of alumina ceramics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{A}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex>. In this study the dielectric and mechanical breakdown of alumina with different thickness has been characterized and compared with the results obtained with the electromechanical setup. It can be observed that the mechanical prestress of 50% of the mechanical breakdown value, applied to the samples reduces the dielectric breakdown field of the sample of 12 %. A similar behavior is observed for the electrical prestress, for 70% of the dielectric breakdown field on the mechanical breakdown strength, resulting a reduction of 30% of the mechanical breakdown strength.

articleTitle: Effect of Insulation Thickness on Space Charge and Electric Field Distribution in ± 500 kV HVDC Extruded Cables
abstract: This study concentrates on the effect of insulation thickness on space charge and electric field distribution in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 500 \text{kV}$</tex> HVDC extruded cables. The modified bipolar carrier transport model (bipolar electronic-ionic carrier transport, BEICT) was used to emulate the dynamic evolution of space charge and electric field inside the insulation at temperature gradient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Delta \mathrm{T})$</tex>. The results show that the rise of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta \mathrm{T}$</tex> intensified the homo-electronic charge injection on the internal side of insulating layer as well as dissociation of impurities, leading to massive hetero-ionic charges accumulating on the external side. The electric fields at the internal and external sides of insulating layer were thus weakened and strengthened, respectively. The increase in insulation thickness resulted in a higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta \mathrm{T}$</tex> along the insulating radial direction, exacerbating the electric field non-uniformity degree. Regarding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 500\text{kV}$</tex> HVDC cable, 26 mm is a more appropriate choice, which not only ensures the safe operation, but also maximizes the insulation utilization.

articleTitle: A Study Towards Machine Learning Prediction of Thermal Conductivity of Polymers Based on Molecular Dynamics
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing demand for further enhancement of thermal conductivity in dielectric polymers used in electrical equipment and electronic devices. While machine learning-based property predictions have been explored for polymer molecular design, existing models often suffer from low interpretability and require extensive computations or experimental efforts. In this study, we predicted the thermal conductivity of both crystalline and amorphous polymers by incorporating information from the unit cell structure of crystals and molecular dynamics force field parameters as descriptors. We achieved improved prediction accuracy for thermal conductivity of amorphous polymers.

articleTitle: Research on Charge Variation of Discharges in Pure Nitrogen and its Mixture with Sulfur Hexafluoride
abstract: Nitrogen and its mixtures with sulfur hexafluoride are receiving more attention as insulation gases. In this paper, the surface charge variation of the discharges in pure Nitrogen and its mixture with sulfur hexafluoride was measured by the Pockels effect. The experiment result shows that, in a lower gas pressure, the surface charge channel will propagate further and the branches are less likely to occur. The surface charge channels in the mixture hardly extend outwards which may be due to the electronegative of sulfur hexafluoride.

articleTitle: Space Charge and Conduction Character of PP/POE Composites Under High Temperature
abstract: The mechanical properties of polypropylene (PP) can be effectively improved by adding elastomers to meet the requirements of cable manufacture. However, the insulation property of PP/elastomer composites will be weakened. The temperature can greatly influence the space charge accumulation in DC condition. And then the electric field distribution and breakdown voltage can be significantly influenced by temperature. This paper studied the electrical properties of PP and elastomer composites at high temperature. The results show that the conduction current densities and the conductivity of the PP and PP/POE composites increase with the temperature rises. The increase at 60 °C is significantly higher than at 40 °C, and the increase of the composites material is much higher than that of PP. The space charge of the PP is stable at high temperature, the amount of space charge accumulation of composites increases with the increase of temperature, and the amount of space charge increases sharply at high temperature. The POE phase begins to soften between 40-60 °C, the molecular chain changes, leading to the decrease of insulation performance at high temperature.

articleTitle: Identification of Installation Defects on MV Cable Systems Through on Field PD Measurements Performed with the Aid of NPF Voltage Source
abstract: This study explores partial discharge (PD) phenomena observed during Near-Power-Frequency (NPF) voltage source tests conducted on 35 kV medium voltage (MV) cable circuits. The research aims to understand how test voltage impacts the occurrence of PDs in the presence of defects on the semiconductor layer of MV terminals. Furthermore, the study utilizes simulations to evaluate the distribution of the electric field across the semiconducting layer and its relationship with the initiation of partial discharge phenomena.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of BNNS/NFC Modified Three-Layer Insulating Paper
abstract: Extra-high voltage bushing faces severe heat dissipation demand during operation, which puts forward higher requirements on the thermal conductivity, mechanical and electrical properties of insulating paper. In this paper, the laminated design method is combined with nanomaterial body doping modification technology to design BNNS/NFC modified sandwich structure insulating paper. The doping of BNNS significantly improves the thermal conductivity of the insulating paper, and the thermal conductivity coefficient is increased by up to 15.82%. The sandwich structure and the nano-fillers also have obvious effects on improving the mechanical and electrical properties of the insulating paper, and the tensile strength of the modified paper is increased by up to 20.4%, the AC breakdown field strength is increased by 26.58%.

articleTitle: New Markers Based on HF Signals for Series DC Arc Detection
abstract: The current approach towards the More-Electrical and All-Electrical Aircraft (MEA and AEA, respectively) is pulling the new designs of electric power systems to higher rated voltages. This is giving new concerns related to ionization phenomena, and, among then, the DC series arc has revealed hazards in the short-term operation in aircraft. This ionization phenomenon is difficult to detect and there are no commercial devices are still available for this purpose. In addition to the appropriate sensor, conditioning and processing techniques, it is needed to extract from the system, accurate information to detect the arc. This paper point to new markers from HF signals measured by inductive devices.

articleTitle: A Micro-Identification Method of Composite Insulation Sheds Aging based on IC-FHA-YOLOv8 and SEM Images
abstract: The aging discrimination method of composite insulators has always been the focus of research in the electric power field. This paper obtained the SEM data set (CIS-SEM data set) by collecting 550 composite insulator samples in operation in a coastal area in China. By analyzing SEM images, this paper determined the aging characteristics of the SiR surface of composite insulators at different aging stages. Then, based on different aging characterizations, this paper divided the aging degree of composite insulators into 6 levels from the micro-level. This paper improved the basic YOLOv8 and added the improved CBAM to achieve better determination of dense targets. For small object detection, we proposed a four-head ASFF prediction head, which can be replaced according to the characteristics of the data set. The results show that the detection accuracy (mAP) of the IC-FHA-YOLOv8 algorithm on the CIS-SEM data set can reach 98.6%. The new algorithm can achieve higher detection accuracy at the expense of less detection speed, which can also well balance the accuracy and speed of the algorithm. It is of great significance to identify the aging of composite insulators from the micro-level.

articleTitle: Insulation State Assessment of Press-Pack IGBTs Based on Electric and Temperature Field Simulation
abstract: IGBT devices are used throughout the entire process of integrating renewable energy generation into the grid, AC/DC transmission, and grid establishment, serving as foundational components supporting the development of smart grids. However, during prolonged operation, issues such as encapsulation insulation may arise in IGBT devices. Therefore, it is necessary to investigate the electric field and temperature distribution within the internal packaging insulation structure of press-pack IGBTs. Whether the IGBT is in the off-state or on-state processes under electrostatic field conditions, simulation results from steady-state calculations indicate that the highest electric field primarily occurs at the junction of the polyamide (PI) passivation layer/air gap/aluminum plating. Additionally, under continuous current conditions, the temperature of the chip's active region is significantly higher than that of the two end electrodes, with the highest temperature occurring near the PI passivation layer. The increase in temperature-induced thermal expansion causes changes in parameters such as roughness between materials, leading to an increase in contact thermal resistance, further raising the temperature. Both high temperature and high electric field may potentially cause failure in PI, which serves as the packaging insulation material. In the long run, this can pose a threat to the chip's packaging insulation and accelerate the device's aging process.

articleTitle: Polymer Composition and Film Morphology Affecting Polypropylene Electret Charge Stability
abstract: Electret charge stability has been examined by thermally stimulated surface potential decay for corona charged polypropylene films. Pressed and extruded samples have been analyzed with their initial morphology and after annealing at 120°C for 15 min. Notwithstanding the typically low amounts of additives used by polymer manufacturers, already distinct differences in charge stability have been observed for polymer compositions with different anti-oxidant packages. Charging with positive corona has provided the most stable electret films for all analyzed sample compositions. Next to the additive related peculiarities, a major discrepancy on electret stability has been noticed between extruded and pressed films. It is found that pressed films have a better electret stability in respect to the extruded films. Annealing has improved the electret stability, but doesn't affect all samples equally. Biggest gains in electret stability have been obtained by annealing quench cooled extruded films, even though the improvements are both composition and polarity dependent.

articleTitle: The Trap and Dielectric Characteristics of Polyimide Nanofiber Membranes at Different Temperatures
abstract: Polyimide nanofiber membranes, as a high-performance insulation material, have garnered considerable attention and hold promising application prospects. In this study, polyimide nanofiber membranes were prepared by electrospinning process, and their surface potential decay, traps, and dielectric properties were investigated under temperature conditions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25 \ {}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, 50 \ {}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, 75 \ {}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex>, and 90 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\circ}{\mathbf{C}}$</tex> utilizing an isothermal surface potential decay test system and a wideband dielectric spectroscopy test system. The results indicate that as the temperature rises, the traps energy levels escalate, the density of shallow traps diminishes, and the density of deep traps shows an overall increasing trend. Elevated temperature extends the average free path of electron motion, intensifying electron capture and emission. Furthermore, the rise in temperature induces thermal depolarization, leading to a reduction in the dielectric constant and dielectric loss of the polyimide nanofiber membranes. This study holds important theoretical value and engineering significance for advancing the application of polyimide nanofiber membranes.

articleTitle: Effect of Pressure on the Electrical Treeing and Discharge Characteristics of Epoxy Resin
abstract: The move towards more electric aircraft (MEA) is driven by the need to tackle the increasing level of greenhouse gas emissions in the aviation sector. MEAs operate at low-pressure, high-altitude environment, where the increase in operating voltage will make the insulation system more susceptible to defects. Electrical treeing and the partial discharge (PD) associated with it, is one of the pre-cursors leading to untimely failure of solid dielectrics. This work investigates the influence of air at 0.2 bar and 1 bar on the propagation of electrical trees and the PD activity in an epoxy resin needle-plane sample under 6 kV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMS</inf>. It was found that a pressure of 0.2 bar usually inhibits the tree propagation when compared to 1 bar. The permeation process of a test sample under 0.2 bar air led to short branches of tree growth along the chamfer edge of the needle tip.

articleTitle: Studying the Novel Interaction of Carbon Dots with Aged Mineral Oil Through Photoluminescence Emission
abstract: Carbon dots have covered a wide range of applications recently since they are biocompatible, non-toxic, and created in a low-cost hydrothermal process. Their size affects their photoluminescence properties which are determined by the specified conditions in the synthesis process. Photoluminescence spectroscopy is far less used than ultraviolet visible spectroscopy in the literature concerning condition assessment of power transformer insulating oil. This paper focuses on the development of a compatible optical sensor from carbon dots to assess the condition of aged mineral oil. The aged oil simulates the naturally occurring accelerated oxidation in an in-service power transformer according to ASTM D1934. During this, the novel interaction between the novel synthesized carbon dots and the mineral oil whether fresh or aged will be highlighted. Dielectric dissipation factor is obtained in the lab and correlated with the optical emission spectra of the novel optical sensor. Judging the oil condition is done by referencing the in-service limits of dielectric dissipation factor for mineral oil in power transformer specified in IEEE Std C57.106-2015. A novel optical sensor is developed from carbon dots capable of indicating dielectric dissipation factor and aging of the mineral oil under conditions that simulate real operation.

articleTitle: Study on Space Charge Accumulation Allowance for DC Cables Using Bipolar Transport Calculation
abstract: Charge injection and accumulation in DC cables have a possibility to enhance the local electric field especially when impulse voltage with reversed polarity is applied. Allowance level of charge accumulation was assessed based on the safety margin included in this polarity reversal testing. The bipolar transport model was utilised to obtain a realistic charge distribution under a temperature gradient condition. The field enhancement due to the space charge accumulation was evaluated by comparing the calculation results obtained for ohmic and Schottky injections. It was found that the allowance of additional charge should be evaluated at the inner conductor, where the charges injected by the Schottky effect were stacked to enhance the local field under the voltage reversal. This paper also assessed how far we can grasp the space accumulation allowance to clarify the remaining issues.

articleTitle: Simulation and Mechanism Study of Cavity Discharge Under Pulsed Electric Field
abstract: The high voltage devices are easy to produce tiny cavities and discharge under pulsed electric field, which aggravate the deterioration of material insulation. In order to explore the specific mechanism and influencing factors in the process, this paper builds a two-dimensional plasma simulation model of cylindrical medium wrapped spherical cavity under nanosecond pulsed electric field and analyzes the spatiotemporal evolution process of discharge through the changes of electron density, positive ion density, surface charge density and electric field intensity. Besides, the rule of the effect of discharge products and pulse frequency on cavity discharge are studied. The simulation results show that the cavity discharge mainly occurs at the front and tail of the pulse. The discharge current will rise rapidly after the cavity breakdown. When surface charges accumulate to a certain extent, the opposite electric field will cause the gas voltage to decrease and finally the discharge ends near the pulse flat area. When the pulse voltage is applied, the number of ozone molecules continues to increase. The generation rate is faster at the front and tail time, which is more corrosive to dielectric materials. When the pulse frequency is increased, the gas is more likely to discharge at a lower voltage and the peak discharge current decreases. The number of ozone molecules increases within a certain period of time. This paper provides a certain reference for improving the insulation properties of materials.

articleTitle: Impact of Semi-Conductive Layers on the DC Conductivity of XLPE MVAC Cables
abstract: The increasing demand for electrical energy poses new challenges on the existing transmission and distribution grid. To overcome these challenges, the DC transmission in the MV grid will play an important role in future. To achieve a cost-effective solution, research is focusing on the use of MVAC cable systems for MVDC. MVDC cables with extruded insulation exhibit phenomena such as the accumulation of space charges in the insulation bulk. Furthermore, space charges accumulate at interfaces. Since the semi-conductive layers in cables represent such interfaces and the interaction with the insulation could be crucial for reliable operation, leakage current measurements are carried out on XLPE plate samples with and without an extruded semi-conductive layer. The material was taken from an MVAC cable. The apparent DC conductivity is measured in a temperature range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}-90^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex> and for an electric stress up to 20 kV/mm.

articleTitle: A Novel Evaluation Method of the Effect of Space Charge in Insulating Materials to IGBTs Blocking Voltage
abstract: We propose a novel evaluation method for the effect of space charge in passivation materials to blocking voltage of high voltage power devices like IGBT and diode devices. In the method, an electrode called Guard Probe (GP) is placed above the edge termination area of high voltage power chip. Dependence of the collector current on collector-emitter voltage ( <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{I}_{\text{ce}}-\mathbf{V}_{\text{ce}}$</tex> curve) is measured repeatedly with increasing the voltage applied to the GP electrode step-by-step. The GP electrode simulates the space charges which are the major cause of long-term instability of high voltage devices. The GP voltage when an indication of avalanche breakdown, that is a sudden increase of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{I}_{\text{ce}}$</tex>, appeared in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{I}_{\text{ce}}-\mathbf{V}_{\text{ce}}$</tex> curve just below the rated voltage, is defined as “the GP voltage at avalanche breakdown”. A good correlation between the GP voltage at avalanche breakdown and long-term instability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{I}_{\text{ce}}$</tex> was observed for several IGBT and diode devices with different edge termination structures and passivation materials. Therefore, the GP voltage at avalanche breakdown can be used as an index of ruggedness of high voltage power devices against external electric field perturbation by space charges in passivation and encapsulation materials.

articleTitle: Dielectric Spectra of Polyurethane Casting Resins for Electrical Engineering Applications
abstract: Polyurethane-based casting compounds are crucial in electrical engineering. Despite their long history of use, research and optimization of their applications remain important. This study compares two different polyurethane-based materials suitable for high-voltage electrical applications, focusing on their dielectric properties. The experiment involved measuring volume resistivity, loss factor, and permittivity, as well as conducting a broadband dielectric spectroscopy analysis. The chemical composition of the tested materials was further characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and hardness measurements were also conducted. The first tested material serves as the reference in this experiment, being commonly used. The second material was included in the experiment as a potential replacement for the first material because it exhibited significantly higher bulk resistivity and optimal polarization behaviour during the first analyses.

articleTitle: Simulation of Partial Discharge from a Railway Pantograph
abstract: This paper considers partial discharges from a railway pantograph. Experimental results are compared with corresponding Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulation models. A three-dimensional model is used to confirm the location and magnitude of peak electric fields within the pantograph identified by the experimental results. Following this, discharges from the tips of the current carriers, which were identified as the peak field points, are simulated using a two-dimensional drift diffusion axisymmetric model. The magnitudes of apparent charge and their occurrence within the cycle obtained through simulation are found to be in agreement with the experimental data. Possible future work could include investigation of the influence of environmental factors on partial discharges and the impact of ionisation coefficient on the results.

articleTitle: Effect of Semiconductive Layer on Space Charge Accumulation of Polypropylene Blends for DC Cable Insulation
abstract: This paper reports on the effect of different semi-conductive shielding layers on the space charge accumulation behavior of insulation layer in polypropylene (PP) HVDC cable. Four kinds of semi-conductive shielding materials were prepared with different content of CB (20, 25, 30, 35 wt%) in ethylene butyl acrylate copolymer (EBA) resin matrix. PP/propylene-based-elastomer (PP/PBE) blends were selected as the insulation layer. The space charge accumulation behavior of polypropylene blends was measured by pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method under an electric field of 50 kV/mm. The average charge density and electric field distribution in PP/PBE blends were estimated. The results showed that the average charge density of PP/PBE blends decreased first and then increased with the increase of the content of CB, and reached the minimum value when CB content was 25 wt%. At the same time, the electric field distortion also reached the minimum. Therefore, this semiconductive layer has the best inhibition effect of space charge in PP/PBE blends. This work has referencing significance for improving the insulation performance of PP based cable.

articleTitle: Effect of Cracks on the Dielectric Breakdown of Polymers and Ceramics
abstract: The influence of an insulating crack on the dielectric breakdown of polymers and ceramics is evaluated by finite element modeling. Measured dielectric breakdown and relative permittivity for epoxy resin and alumina specimens were used as inputs for the numerical model. An insulating crack was modelled in the center of the material, with its longitudinal direction aligned parallel and perpendicular to the electric field direction. The intensity of the electric field increases up to 17 times, confined within the crack when the crack was perpendicular to the field. The presence of a crack parallel to the field does not cause large disturbances on the electrical field distribution. The measured dielectric breakdown for both materials were similar to those obtained by the model with the crack in perpendicular direction.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties Comparison: Enamelled-Extruded Wires vs. Conventional Wires
abstract: The principal aim of this work is to compare some electrical properties characterized experimentally on samples of enamelled wires developed from two kinds of coating insulation processes. It consists of an evaluation of the dielectric strength, Partial Discharge Inception Voltage (PDIV), and voltage endurance accordingly to IEC standards. Enamelled-extruded wires are evaluated, its insulation comprises an enamel primer on PAI, a second enamel coat of PAI-silica composite produced through the sol-gel process, and a topcoat on PPS resin. The same properties had been characterized on conventional enamelled wire samples (PEI and PAI) for comparison. The breakdown voltage measurements are carried out under 3kV (50Hz), and the lifetime data of twisted pairs samples are collected. The analysis of those results employs the Weibull distribution. The PDIV of these wires is measured, the results obtained show some advantages of the enamelled-extruded wires being 781 V (conventional wire PDIV = 668 V). The lifetime under 3kV (50Hz) has demonstrated an advantage for this type of wire, with α=1616 minutes compared to α=529 minutes for conventional wires. The dielectric strength is very similar between both kind of wires, with α=104.5 V/µm for the enamelled-extruded and α= 109.4 V/µm for the conventional wire. This study shows the increased electrical properties of enamelled-extruded wires compared to conventional ones. This advantage is significant regarding the electrical endurance under high voltage. This kind of insulation has the potential properties to be employed in winding applications and is also an eco-friendly solution compared to the conventional wires.

articleTitle: Aging Characteristics of Silicone Rubber Composite Insulators Based on Space Charge Behavior
abstract: Silicone rubber composite insulators are widely used in high-voltage transmission lines, but they face serious aging problems during long-term operation. In this paper, the unaged and aged silicone rubber composite insulator samples are taken as the research object. The space charge detection is carried out in the range from 0.6 to 30 kV/mm, and the aging characteristics of this insulating material are analyzed by charge density, accumulation rate and maximum electric field distortion rate. The results show that the charge accumulation threshold field decreases after aging. For both unaged and aged samples, the rate of charge accumulation is divided into three stages, from slow accumulation to fast accumulation, and finally back to slow change. At the first inflection point of charge accumulation rate, the corresponding field intensity reduces significantly in the aged sample. Besides, the maximum electric field distortion rate of the aging sample increases at each tested electric field. And the position of the maximum distortion point migrates from the middle of the sample to the lower surface.

articleTitle: Monitoring Aging of Natural Ester Insulating Fluid using Supercritical Fluid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (SFC-MS)
abstract: Petroleum-based mineral oils have been used in transformers to provide cooling and insulation. However, there are increasing concerns over the persistence and impact of petroleum-based oils on the environment due to their resistance to biodegradation. Natural ester-based oils are considered to be sustainable alternatives, as they are biodegradable and possess improved fire safety properties compared to mineral oils. Here, supercritical fluid chromatography-mass spectrometry (SFC-MS) is used to study the chemical composition of natural ester oils and their behavior when subjected to aging experiments. Under the applied aging conditions detectable amounts of hydrolysis products (free fatty acids and DAGs) are evident in the aged samples. Furthermore, SFC-MS can also be used to simultaneously monitor the presence of other oil components, such as antioxidants.

articleTitle: Interfacial Insulation Degradation Characteristics Between Epoxy Resin and Silicone Rubber Under Different Interface Pressures
abstract: In this paper, an equivalent experimental platform for interfacial insulation degradation testing with controllable pressure is established. The growth process of discharge tracking, and the characteristics of partial discharge and dielectric breakdown under different interface pressures are explored. The results indicate that compared to high pressure of 0.3 MPa, the inception voltage under 0.05 MPa is reduced by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30{\rm{\% }}$</tex> and the growth rate of tracking is increased by 5 times. With the reduction of interface pressure, interfacial breakdown strength is decreased and the characteristics of partial discharge transition from internal discharge to a coexistence of surface and internal discharges. Besides, under lower pressure, the discharge tracking mainly occurs on the surface of silicone rubber, while under higher pressure, it shifts to epoxy resin. This research provides a theoretical basis for the insulation state evaluation of dry-type cable termination for gas insulated switchgear (GIS) under different interface pressures.

articleTitle: Effects of Icing and Galloping on the Insulation Performance of 10 kV Overhead Insulated Conductor
abstract: Icing and galloping caused by extreme weather may lead to the damage and conductor breakage of 10 kV overhead insulated conductors. In this paper, the forces on the insulation layer of overhead insulated conductors in the process of galloping are investigated by ANSYS Workbench finite element analysis under different icing thicknesses and wind speeds. And the distribution of the electric field on the surface of the conductors and around the conductors is investigated by COMSOL simulation software. As the intensity of conductor galloping increases, it correspondingly escalates the damage to its insulation layer, resulting in the formation of cracks and the infiltration of moisture. This can cause conductor breakage. When the conductor is covered with icicle-type icing, the maximum electric field strength around it is three times of that under normal conditions, and the field strength below the center of the conductor also increases.

articleTitle: A Study of Ageing and Gelling in Natural Ester Oils
abstract: Two natural ester-based transformer fluids derived from soybean oil and rapeseed oil were compared to their edible equivalents. Oxidative ageing was performed in the presence of Kraft paper at 130 °C and some samples contained copper. It was found that both edible oils, particularly soybean oil, showed increased acidity and viscosity after ageing in the presence of copper. Further tests showed that both butyl hydroxytoluene (BHT), which is a common inhibitor for mineral oil but is moderately toxic, and Irganox 1010, which is non-toxic, successfully mitigated the adverse effects of oxidation in edible soybean oil. The study highlights some of the detrimental effects of oxidation in natural ester oils and shows that Irganox 1010 provides a non-toxic alternative to BHT for stabilizing ester oils.

articleTitle: Breakdown Characteristics and Electrical Life Evaluation of 500 kV EHVAC Cable Insulation at Different Temperatures
abstract: This study investigates the effect of operating temperature on the breakdown strength and aging life parameter of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulation for 500 kV extra-high voltage alternating current (EHVAC) cables. The test samples were cut from a properly degassed real 500 kV XLPE cable. The continuous-rising voltage breakdown tests and step-up voltage breakdown tests were conducted at 30 °C, 50 °C, 70 °C, and 90 °C, respectively. The results show that, the AC breakdown strength decreases with increasing operating temperature regardless of the thickness of XLPE samples. When the temperature is 70 °C or below, increasing the thickness of samples effectively slows down the decreasing trend of the breakdown strength. However, at 90 °C, increasing the sample thickness cannot resist the decrease in AC breakdown strength. By analyzing the aging life curves of the XLPE samples at different temperatures, it is found that the aging life parameters of the XLPE samples at 30 °C and 90 °C are 18 and 14, respectively. It is perceived from testing results that even after continuous operation for 40 years, the tested XLPE material can possess AC breakdown strengths of 44.6 MV/m and 28.3 MV/m at 30 °C and 90°C, respectively. This study provides a reference basis for the design of insulation thickness and the electrical life assessment of 500 kV EHVAC cables during the long-term operation.

articleTitle: Electrical Tree Resistance Enhancement of Polypropylene Based on Heterogeneous Structure Modulation
abstract: This paper focuses on the Electrical tree resistance enhancement of polypropylene based on heterogeneous structure modulation. The heterogeneous mesoscopic structure is modulated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> -nucleating agent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha-\text{NA})$</tex>, and its effects on the partial discharge and electrical tree properties are investigated using a combination of experimental and simulation methods. The results show that the difference in the dielectric properties from the crystal to amorphous regions, triggered by the diversity in molecular chain arrangement and density, led to localized strong electric field distortion and further induced the growth of electric tree along the amorphous region at the boundary of the spherical crystals. The addition of a-NA refined the spherical crystal size and raised the spherical crystal density. The electric field distortion, induced by excessive size and loosely stacked spherical crystals, were suppressed to some extent, and the strength and frequency of partial discharges are thus weakened. The electrical tree resistance and breakdown strength of the material were consequently markedly enhanced.

articleTitle: Study of Injection and Retention of Charges in Silica-Based Nanocomposite Dielectrics: Impact of Size of Silver Nanoparticles
abstract: It is well-known that dielectric materials store charges when they are subjected to an electric field. Recently, nanocomposite materials were identified as promising candidates to tune this effect. This study focuses on silica-based nanocomposites containing a single plane of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) embedded at 5 nm under the surface. More particularly, the influence of AgNPs size on charges injection and retention is investigated. The electrical charges are injected locally by using an Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) tip and the related surface potential profile is probed by Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM). The results show that proper selection of the size of AgNPs allows a fine control of the charges dynamics.

articleTitle: Thermal Fault Assessment of High-voltage Cable Based on Evolved Gas Analysis
abstract: Existing techniques for assessing the condition of high-voltage cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cables continue to encounter challenges, particularly in terms of sensitivity and reliability when diagnosing thermal faults. In response to these challenges, this study introduces a method for diagnosing thermal faults based on the analysis of evolved gases emitted from cables. Initially, both low and high-temperature thermal faults occurring in the water-blocking buffer layer, XLPE insulation, and semiconductive layer materials of high-voltage XLPE cables were considered. Through thermogravimetric-mass spectrometry (TG-MS) experiments, the characteristic gas generation processes associated with these thermal fault types were simulated, and their patterns were scrutinized.
