By summarizing the characteristic gas generation properties corresponding to various types of faults, assessment criteria for determining the thermal fault status of high-voltage cables were developed. These criteria utilize parameters such as the ratio of CO to CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> content, the presence of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, C2H4, and C2H2 generation, as well as the ratio of H2 to C2H2 content.

articleTitle: Effects of Climatic Aging on the Performance of EPDM Used in Power Cable Insulation
abstract: This work is intended to contribute to better understanding towards the weathering degradation of the properties of ethylene-propylene-diene-monomer (EPDM), a polymer used as insulation in medium voltage electrical cables. The samples were exposed to natural weathering in the city of Tizi-Ouzou, in northern Algeria, over a period of approximately 5.5 months. The samples were monitored using a variety of electrical and mechanical characterization methods, including measurements of bulk resistivity, dielectric strength, dielectric constant, dielectric loss factor, tensile strength, and elongation at break. Material color change, surface stiffening and increased surface cracking are the major macroscopic effects of weathering degradation. Electrical and mechanical test results show that after this period of weathering, only the resistivity and elongation at break were significantly affected. The other physical properties of the polymer were only slightly altered, suggesting the need for a longer accelerated aging period. Some of the characteristics that are measured are markers of aging that could be used in the future to predict the service life of an insulator.

articleTitle: Radiation Aging Effect on Electrical Properties of Superconductive Magnet Wires
abstract: This paper focuses on the effect of high dose radiation on the electric insulation of superconducting wires used in particle accelerator magnets. The analysis focuses on the evolution of the electrical properties, due to radiation doses, of the poly-vinyl acetate (PVA) insulation of these wires, particularly complex permittivity. This aims at verifying the suitability of the dielectric spectroscopy technique as a nondestructive approach for the aging assessment of these wires, usually placed in inaccessible areas. This is achieved by comparing results coming from complex permittivity with oxidation buildup obtained through Fourier Transform Infra-Red (FTIR) spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Effect of Continuous Polarity Reversals at Different Temperatures on the Space Charge Characteristics of XLPE
abstract: In DC transmission systems, both high temperature and polarity reversal voltage can influence the transport of space charges, leading to insulation failure in severe cases. Consequently, this study primarily investigates the space charge distribution and transient electric field distortion of XLPE when subjected to four consecutive polarity reversals at temperatures ranging from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. The effects of temperature and polarity reversal on the transport of space charges are examined. The results indicate that temperature influences the migration rate of charge carriers and the injection/extraction rate at electrodes. With increasing temperature, the depth of charge distribution expands from 60 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}$</tex> to 200 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}$</tex>. Due to the influence of electrode materials on charge injection, the concentration of injected electron holes is higher during positive polarity voltage. A sharp increase in electric field distortion rate occurs during the transition from negative to positive voltage. At <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$</tex>, an observable increase in Heteropolar charges within the specimen is evident with an increase in the number of polarity reversals, while at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$</tex>, an increase in both depth and density of charge accumulation within the specimen is observed with an increase in the number of polarity reversals.

articleTitle: Condition Assessment of Insulation Systems Through Electric Field Mapping Using Electro-Optic Sensors
abstract: The performance of outdoor insulators directly affects the reliability of power supply. However, their insulation performance is highly dependent on the environmental factors such as pollution. Evaluating the extent of pollution on insulators is essential for maintaining high power quality standards. This study explores a novel approach to assess the severity of pollution and its impact on insulation integrity of composite insulators, utilizing Electro-Optic (EO) sensor technology for electric field mapping. Given the challenges associated with collecting and analyzing such data during power line inspections, this research seeks to evaluate the feasibility of EO sensor-based diagnostics for preventive maintenance. The objective is to identify and map variations in electric field associated with pollution-induced insulation degradation. Furthermore, this study investigates the distribution of two components of the electric field under different contamination scenarios, taking into account the position of the sensor and the applied voltage. The results demonstrate a significant influence of the pollution deposition on the measured electric field values, highlighting the efficiency of the EO sensor in accurately assessing insulation condition. These findings provide valuable insights for implementing targeted maintenance strategies, ultimately enhancing the longevity and reliability of high-voltage equipment and fortifying resilience within the energy sector.

articleTitle: Transient Current and Space Charge in Gamma Irradiated PTFE: Discussion on Heterocharge Formation
abstract: Heterocharges in gamma irradiated polymers are often observed but their origin and dynamic are not fully understood. The main objective of our work is to explore heterocharges behavior in gamma irradiated polytetrafluoroethylene under DC field, in correlation with transient current, by using exactly the same protocol for space charge and current measurements. Furthermore, the reversal of applied voltage is expected to be a good tool to explore heterocharges in this case. The heterocharge build-up seems associated with a region near the film surface with lower electrical conductivity. The heterogeneity could arise from strong surface oxidation of the PTFE layer promoted by gamma irradiation.

articleTitle: A Noncalibration Partial Discharge Magnitude Measurement Method Based on an Embedded Bushing Sensor
abstract: Partial Discharge (PD) magnitude is an important parameter for assessing switchgear insulating performance. The conventional measurement method needs a standard calibration source to calibrate PD detection sensors such as HFCT and TEV. This is a complex process and requires the switchgear to be shut down. Consequently, this paper proposes a noncalibration PD magnitude detection method based on the embedded bushing sensor of the switchgear. This sensor is based on capacitive voltage dividers existing in most bushings, used to indicate the presence of voltage in a cabinet. The test shows that this method provides similar results to the traditional sensor, and complies with the IEC60270 standard.

articleTitle: On the Dielectric Relaxation Characteristics of Epoxy Resins Under Different Aging Conditions
abstract: In this paper, thermal aging treatment of epoxy resins is carried out at 180 °C under different times, and the changes in the dielectric spectrum are analyzed using Havriliak-Negami (HN) model. The experimental results show that dielectric constant and dielectric loss of epoxy resins show a tendency of decreasing firstly, and then increasing with the increase of aging time. In the early stage of aging (0-168 h), the relaxation strength of α-relaxation and β-relaxation increases, and the relaxation time slightly decreases, due to the post-curing and molecular rearrangement of the epoxy resin, which results in the increase of cross-linking density and Tg. While in the late stage of aging, the oxidative decomposition takes a dominant role and leads to severe molecular chain destruction and free volume increase, which in turn causes an increase in the α-relaxation strength and a decrease in the relaxation time. In addition, thermal aging further enhances the dipole polarization, leading to an increase in the β relaxation strength, while the relaxation peak shifts to the high-frequency direction. Thermal aging has a significant impact on the dielectric polarization and relaxation properties of epoxy resins by altering their cross-linked structure.

articleTitle: Fundamental Analysis of Interfacial Signal in Double-Layer with Different Permittivity Using PEA Method
abstract: This paper deals with the interfacial signal in the double-layer. In the insulating systems in power electric devices, multi-layered insulation structures are usually used. For example, a joint of a power transmission cable has a double-layer of a cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) and a rubber material, and a high voltage is applied to the doble layer. In such case, precise analysis of interfacial charge is required because accumulated charge at the interface has a critical impact on the overall stress distribution. The space charge distribution was measured in the double-layer using the PEA method, and the PEA signal generated at the interface was investigated. After voltage is applied to the specimen, initially the DC and pulse electric fields are shared depending on the dielectric constant of each material. Acoustic waves are observed at the interface due to the difference in electric fields of the pulses. To investigate the interfacial signal, the charge distribution in the double-layer was calculated based on the charge distribution measured in the single-layer and compared with the measured signal. The calculated results and measured signals were very similar. Information about this phenomenon can help with signal processing and lead to a more precise interpretation of the space charge distribution in the double-layer.

articleTitle: Research on Transient Voltage Characteristics of EHV Cable Considering Corrugated Sheath
abstract: Electromagnetic transient characteristics in EHV cable systems are essential for the calculation of overvoltage and the design of insulation co-ordination. In this paper, an improved transient model of EHV cable with a structure of corrugated sheath is proposed to calculate parameters of wave propagation. In this method, the corrugated sheath is equivalent with a smooth structure based on the geometric mean radius and length, to obtain the accurate impedance and admittance of complex cross-section cable. Then, a transient test on a 500 kV EHV cable circuit is carried out to verify the accuracy of the proposed model for the transient voltage. Compared with the frequency-dependent phase model in PSCAD, the calculation accuracy of the modified model is improved by more than 5% with a relative error of 4%. This increase in calculation accuracy is caused by the errors of corrugated sheath thickness and surface area in the PSCAD model. Therefore, it is necessary to consider the influence of the corrugated sheath when calculating the transient wave propagation and designing the protection strategies of the EHV cable.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Modelling of the Dielectric Response of PA6-BaTiO3 Nanocomposites with Different Levels of Absorbed Moisture
abstract: The effect of moisture content and different levels of Barium Titanate (BTO) filler in Polyamide (PA6) on the dielectric response is investigated through an equivalent circuit with Dissado-Hill circuit elements. The dielectric measurements were conducted under dry condition and 75% relative humidity at an above glass transition temperature of 80°C. The dielectric response has been decomposed into alpha and beta relaxation processes, a quasi-dc (QDC) process, dc conductance and high frequency independent permittivity (Ɛ ͚). It was found that the characteristic frequency and magnitude of each process are strongly moisture dependent but the addition of BTO only has minor effects compared to that of the moisture.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Dielectric Analysis of Promising Lead-Free DabcoH+A− Ferroelectric Materials for Energy Applications
abstract: Low Frequency Dispersion (LFD) is a common feature of dielectric materials that was identified in the late 1970s. It is linked to the many body interactions of dipoles and charges in dielectric materials and informs on the conduction mechanisms of materials at low frequency, especially in ionic materials. DabcoHClO4 is an ionic lead-free ferroelectric material showing relatively high remnant polarization among organic materials and is built around linear hydrogen links, making it a good candidate for flexible electronics, especially mixed with polymers. Dielectric spectroscopy characterization is performed on dabcoHClO4 pellets to measure dielectric constant and losses, ac conductivity dielectric modulus and impedance above and below the Curie temperature. The low frequency behavior reveals the presence of LFD and gives new insights to understand the conduction mechanisms of this family of hybrid molecular ionic materials.

articleTitle: Holistic Reliability Analysis Strategy for High-Voltage Polymeric Cable Assets based on Field-Dependent Dynamic Mechanisms
abstract: The holistic and non-destructive insulation reliability assessment of high-voltage (HV) cable assets is continuously paid more attention to supporting the resilience, safety, reliability, and availability of power systems. Clear dynamic physical mechanisms of HV cable assets will be visualized using broadband dielectric spectroscopy (BDS). Therefore, this paper aims to present some crucial observations from the high-field BDS of HV polymeric cable assets with composite structures. The influence of two types of voltage excitations (continuous and cyclic) on high-field BDS is analyzed for HV polymeric cable assets with various aging states. It can be found that the BDS memory effect and saturation effect induced by high field are prominent, with a focus on fresh and aged HV cable assets. Finally, the condition-based maintenance strategy and reliability assessment approach based on high-field dynamic mechanisms are provided as an engineering reference for HV polymeric cable assets. The relevant crucial findings can provide a theoretical basis and guidance for the reliability assessment of HV polymeric cable assets.

articleTitle: Characterization of Polymeric Components of a Cable for Applications in a Radiation Environment
abstract: In this study, a cable featuring extruded polyethylene insulation and designed for CERN fast-pulsed magnet systems is assessed. The evaluation focuses on radiation resistance, with cable samples subjected to accelerated ageing using gamma radiation. Comprehensive measurements, including partial discharge, tan delta, dielectric spectroscopy, tensile tests, and oxidation induction time tests, have been conducted to analyze the ageing of the polymeric components due to radiation.

articleTitle: Trapping Activated Tautomerism of Acetophenone in Polyethylene
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) is an excellent electrical insulator, and is common in high voltage cable applications, where it is chemically cross linked to improve thermal stability, leaving cross linking residues in the material. Acetophenone is one such residue, which is often studied due to its tendency to trap mobile electrons. In the present work the keto-enol tautomerization of acetophenone in the gas phase is studied using quantum chemistry methods. Activation energies, free energy change and Eyring rate constants are calculated for both reaction directions, for both neutral and ionized acetophenone. Ionization is shown to lower the activation energies of tautomerization, and the energetically favored enol to keto reaction has particularly high reaction rates for ionized molecules. Activation energies are similar to electron trapping energies of acetophenone in PE, and we postulate a trapping activated tautomerization mechanism, and discuss how the various modes of trapping, de-trapping and recombination for keto and enol acetophenone may establish a balance keto and enol tautomers over time.

articleTitle: Substitution of Solid Encapsulation Materials by Dielectric Fluid in Power Modules: Potentialities and Challenges
abstract: In conventional power modules, the solid insulating material (epoxy, silicone gel) that covers the top of the devices, does not efficiently contribute to the heat extraction. Moreover, thermal conducting paths are formed by heterogeneous layers for electric insulation, causing inevitably high thermal resistance. As an alternative, the direct cooling of the devices using dielectric liquids in forced convection can pave the road toward a new class of high performance power modules. The aim of this paper is to evaluate the potentialities of using flowing dielectric liquids as encapsulating material in order to ensure the direct cooling of the devices as well as the electric insulation. The thermal interest of the solution is validated using thermal-hydraulic simulations while the dielectric properties of various liquids are evaluated experimentally over a wide temperature range. Results show that by selecting package structure allowing a high exchange area between the top device interconnection and the dielectric fluid, a reduction by more than 40% of the junction to fluid thermal resistance can be achieved. Moreover, based on the combination of the variation of the dielectric properties of liquids in motion issued from the literature and the measured dielectric properties (relative permittivity, electrical conductivity, breakdown voltage) of the dielectric fluids, the three evaluated candidates show their ability to insure a good insulation at temperature up to 175 °C for high voltage applications.

articleTitle: Pulsed Electrical Aging Tests of Insulation Systems and Components for Support of HV Power Supplies Design
abstract: Insulation of HV Power Supplies (HVPS) is exposed to a wide spectrum of voltage stresses, ranging from dc to pulsed voltages. The latter subject insulation to transients at amplitudes up to hundreds of kV at pulsed repetition rate (PRR) from fractions of Hz up to several kHz. It is argued that pulsed testing is appropriate for both pulsed and dc HVPS as limited by electrical aging. The ultimate goal is establishing design guidelines for adequate life for varied field configurations. Testing means comprise wide-band HVPSs and voltage dividers capable of voltage generation and measurement up to 210 kV. Life prediction is based on inverse power law with data mostly obtained in step-stress tests. Devices Under Test (DUT) varied from silicone potting samples with different field nonuniformity, to components, to complex insulation systems. For the first, an attempt is made to construct aging curves for equal life as a function of the field nonuniformity coefficient varied from ∼4 to ∼40 corresponding to rounded and needle electrodes, respectively. An exponent n=12 derived from step-stress tests was used in the curves’ generation. Capacitance loss and life of Polypropylene HV capacitors into billions of 10 kV-15 kV pulses is described. Lastly, aging and breakdown of transformer main insulation is studied with pulsed voltages up to 200 kV at PRR up to 60 Hz. One of the failure mechanisms was ascribed to partial discharges in the winding layer insulation. Although limited to electrical aging, pulsed testing can provide better guidance to design than both, or either, short-term and/or dc tests.

articleTitle: Enhanced Partial Discharge Evaluation Through Integrated RF and IEC Measurements
abstract: In light of growing regulatory concerns regarding the environmental impact of SF6, it is crucial to develop diagnostic procedures that can identify defects in systems utilising alternative gases for insulation. This study examines the application of carbon dioxide and technical air (N2/O2, 79%/21%) in high-voltage applications. Partial discharge assessment is a well-established technique for condition monitoring, commonly employing conventional (IEC 60270) and radio frequency techniques. Simultaneously measuring partial discharge using both radio frequency and electrical detection methods might yield valuable insights into the shape of the fundamental current pulse, which would otherwise be unattainable by merely relying on one methodology. This paper describes the integration of radio frequency and conventional measurements to evaluate the partial discharge properties of technical air and carbon dioxide gas insulating medium. Distinctive patterns become evident when plotting the energy of the radiated pulse versus apparent charge for a particular defect source. These patterns may appear as either curved or clustered data. The integration of the two measurements offers the opportunity to leverage the respective advantages of each approach while mitigating certain limitations that arise when relying solely on one method of measurement.

articleTitle: Thermal Characterization and Time-dependent-dielectric Breakdown Study of Polyimide Thin Film Capacitors
abstract: Polyimides have recently raised a huge interest as versatile dielectrics for galvanic isolation devices. In this study, we explored calorimetry and thermogravimetric properties of two commercial polyimides with different curing ranges. The electrical characterization with time-dependent-dielectric-breakdown tests at several voltages and frequencies provided lifetime behavior and completed materials comparison.

articleTitle: Average Streamer Channel Field Strength in Pressurized Synthetic Air at Lightning Impulse Voltage Stress
abstract: To design gas insulated switchgear filled with pressurized synthetic air, it is important to understand the discharge behavior. The streamer expansion is limited by the average streamer channel field strength. The polarity dependent behavior of the average streamer channel field strength in pressurized synthetic air at lightning impulse voltage stress was investigated in this study. To achieve this, streamers in a strongly nonuniform field created by a needle placed in a uniform and weakly nonuniform background field were optically recorded by a streak camera. This approach was novel compared to previous studies. The results for the average streamer channel field strength were similar at different degrees of homogeneity of the background field. The positive streamer channel field strength with 0.5 kV/mm is independent of the streamer length and increases as a function of pressure to the power of 1.5. The negative streamer channel field strength scales inversely proportional to the streamer length and increases linearly with pressure. For streamer expansions longer than 40 mm, the negative channel field strength is comparable to literature values at 0.1 MPa with 1.0 kV/mm.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Inception and Extinction Voltages in Motor Coils for Aerospace Electric Propulsion
abstract: The evaluation of partial discharges (PDs) in insulated coils for aerospace electric propulsion operating with AC 50 Hz and high-frequency voltages is addressed in this work. Existing investigations lack representativeness both in terms of sample type and voltage conditions. The study compares detection thresholds for PD inception and extinction voltages using various detectors and analyzes the sensitivity of conventional coupling capacitor and electromagnetic measurement techniques. The results indicate that the PD cabinet with an integrated coupling capacitor provides the most accurate measurement for AC voltages. The HFCT is more sensitive to charge threshold changes than TEM and UHF antennas. The use of a shot bath for grounding reduces PDIV compared to an electrolyte arrangement. Rectangular voltage frequency has no influence on PDIV, but increasing rise times lead to higher PDIVs.

articleTitle: Breakdown Process Modeling of Tri-post Insulator Subjected to Electrical and Mechanical Loadings in HVAC-GIL
abstract: In this study, a simulation model is established to study the breakdown evolutions of the tri-post insulator under the combined effects of electrical and mechanical stresses. External forces of different values and in different directions are applied to the insulator in addition to an AC voltage of 1100 kV. Results show that after applying electrical stress and straight tension along the insulator post, the tensile stress and the corresponding strain energy density are concentrated around the tips of the lateral branches, thus promoting their expansion, and even causing a transverse fracture under the condition of 100 kN. In the case of a small straight compression below 25 kN, the breakdown process can be restrained. But when it comes to 75 kN, the breakdown process is promoted again, and a shear fracture can be caused above 100 kN. The outcomes of this study are hoped to help understand and predict the breakdown behaviors of dielectric materials.

articleTitle: Electrical Tree Growth Characteristics of Epoxy Resin under Combined Effects of Low Temperature and Mechanical Stress
abstract: Due to the uneven thermal expansion, thermal stress will be generated at the epoxy bushing in GIS cable termination at low temperature, which may be the main reason for insulation failures. However, researches on the degradation process of epoxy under low temperature superimposed thermal stress is scarce. Therefore, this paper aims to investigate the effects of combined low temperature and mechanical stress on the electrical tree characteristics of epoxy. The platform with controllable temperature and mechanical stress is built to test the electrical tree characteristics from the range of room temperature to ‐40 °C and 0 to 30 MPa. The partial discharge, the growth rate and the cumulative damage characteristics of electrical tree are analyzed. It is found that, at low temperature, the toughness of the epoxy resin decreases, and the thermal stress will greatly reduce the surface energy for crack expansion, resulting in the electrical tree shows a feature of filamentary electromechanical breakdown. The deterioration process of epoxy shows a rapid expansion like crack, and the time to breakdown is greatly reduced. Making the electrical tree presents filamentary electro-mechanical breakdown, eventually leading to the breakdown failure of cable termination.

articleTitle: Structuring HVDC Cable Joints Using Smoothly Field Grading Materials
abstract: The design of accessories is critical for insuring the reliability of HVDC accessories even more as ever high voltages are targeted. Different technologies are available today that do not necessarily involve the interposition of a field grading layer between the cable insulation and the joint body. In this work, we explore the solution of setting a two-layers joint body with the idea of keeping the same polymer and using fillers to impart non-linearity to the conductivity. We show that significant reduction of field maxima can be reached with this design. The so constructed fictive material appears feasible considering literature data. Whether full objects can be produced is another question.

articleTitle: Flashover Improvement of AC-DC Mixed Voltages on HVDC-GIS Spacer with Functionally Graded Materials
abstract: In HVDC systems with bipolar high voltage, the gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) may experience mixed voltages of AC and DC. To enhance the insulation capability of the basin spacer, this study presents a collaborative optimization approach for AC and DC electric fields utilizing the multi-dimensional functionally-graded material (MFGM). A novel spacer was developed by integrating materials with volume graded permittivity (ε-FGM) and surface nonlinear conductivity (SNCM), followed by conducting electric field simulation and flashover voltage testing under various AC, DC, and AC-DC mixed voltages. When exposed to DC voltage, the central region of the convex surface of the MFGM spacer tends to accumulate homopolar surface charges. In contrast, heteropolar surface charges tend to accumulate in the surrounding area. As a result, this accumulation leads to a 25% reduction in electric field strength at the HV triple junction point and an increase in flashover voltage by 14.5% compared to traditional spacers. Under the AC voltage, the electric field distortion of the MFGM spacer is decreased by 21% and the flashover voltage is raised by about 18%. Under the AC-DC mixed voltage, the flashover voltage of the MFGM spacer is raised about 12.7%. The MFGM spacer demonstrates satisfactory performance in electric field relaxation for both steady-state and transient-state, indicating its potential application in HVDC-GIS.

articleTitle: Effect of Dissociation-Recombination Processes in a Dielectric Dispersion Medium on the Coalescence and Non-Coalescence of Conducting Droplets Suspended in it
abstract: An electrical coalescence of conducting droplets is the basis for electrostatic oil cleaning, when tiny water droplets are removed from the dispersion (continuous) medium. However, most studies on the topic treat oil as a perfect dielectric or, at least, disregard dissociation-recombination charged layers near the water-oil interface without appropriate substantiation. The effect of finite (i.e., non-zero) electrical conductivity of oil and dissociation-recombination phenomena in it on the electrical coalescence processes is considered in the present investigation. Two important cases are examined, where oppositely charged ions have equal and different mobilities. In the first case, the threshold electric field strength value, the average electric field strength in the interelectrode space when coalescence of droplets is replaced with non-coalescence, shows a weak decrease compared to the case of dielectric oil. In the latter case, the collision between droplets becomes unlikely due to their translation motion in the same direction and the emergence of electrohydrodynamic jet in the opposite direction behind the droplets.

articleTitle: Electrical Tree Characteristics of Glass Fiber/Epoxy Composites Under Repetitive Impulse Voltage
abstract: Insulation rod made of fiber-reinforced epoxy resins composites, is a key component in Gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) equipment. During operation, insulated rods are often subjected to operational overvoltage. In this paper, electrical tree growth characteristics are investigated of two types of glass fiber/epoxy composites with different fiber laying directions, using positive and negative impulse voltages to simulate operational overvoltage. The results show that the fiber has a better hindering effect on the electrical tree. Electrical tree grows rapidly along the fiber/epoxy interface. With a negative pulse, the electrical tree is more likely to cross the fiber barrier and move toward the periphery or the ground electrode.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Adjustment Algorithm for Electrothermal Simulation of Surge Arrester
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive adjustment algorithm to solve transient nonlinear finite element models for arresters with coupled temperature and electro-quasistatic fields quickly and accurately. Due to slow temperature changes, it can be considered that the electrical quasi-static field is in a stable state within ΔTsteady. Hence, there is no need for transient solutions of the quasi-static field at every moment. We determine ΔTsteady which is dynamically changing based on the change rate of conductivity of ZnO varistor. The results indicate that as the injected energy increases, power losses might exceed the heat flow dissipation due to the negative temperature coefficient of resistivity of the ZnO varistor, leading to arrester thermal runaway.

articleTitle: Constant Voltage Breakdown Measurement of Lapped Insulation Under Cryogenic Conditions
abstract: A method for assessing constant (dc) voltage breakdown in lapped insulation under cryogenic conditions is presented, focusing on Kraft paper, Kapton and PPLP. Breakdown estimation under cryogenic environment can be greatly improved in terms of confidence and test duration by using a moving breakdown point along the sample. Experiments carried out in liquid nitrogen and gaseous helium at about 77 K show that Kapton offers the best breakdown electric field and that the improvement of PPLP is not so important compared to simple Kraft paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of Space Charge and Current Characteristics of AL/LDPE Interface
abstract: The linear relationship between the square root of the electric field strength and the logarithm of the injection current indicates that the injection process of the AL/LDPE interface conforms to the Poole-Frenkel effect. The linear relationship of depolarization stage still exists, but the slope and intercept are different. This may indicate that the depolarization phase is not simply injection, but also contains components of charge extraction.

articleTitle: Typical Defect Study of HVAC Power Cable Through Distortion Analysis of Grounding Current
abstract: As the service life increases, the latent defects of power cables gradually become apparent, threatening the normal operation of cable lines. This study simulates two typical defects of power cables under laboratory conditions, the thermal aging and the insulation scratch. The grounding current signals of cable specimens are collected under three defect levels. The Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), which is improved by the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, and the Lorentz chaotic synchronous system are both adopted to analyze the grounding current distortion from different dimensions. A correlation has been established between the harmonic characteristics of grounding currents, the graphical features of distortion, and the typical cable defects. The results indicate that the grounding current of thermally aged cables primarily consists of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3^{\text{rd}}, 9^{\text{th}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$13^{\text{th}}$</tex> harmonics, and the dynamic error scatter plot takes the form of a flat ellipse. In contrast, the harmonic content of insulation-scratched cables is generally lower, and the dynamic error scatter plot contains two elliptical lines tangent at the top. This study will provide guidance and reference for the condition assessment and defect determination of power cables.

articleTitle: Separation and Recognition of Partial Discharge Signals from Multiple Sources Using Encoder-Decoder based Neural Network
abstract: Partial Discharge (PD) detection is important method to diagnose electric power equipment and find hidden dangers in it. There may exist multiple PD sources in the equipment, which could seriously affect the accuracy of subsequent analysis. To separate the multi-source signal, clustering method and BSS method were applied. However, these methods have limitations such as requiring multiple sensors and not being usable in pulse overlapped case. In this paper, we introduced Conv-TasNet, which was trained to decompose the mixed signals and reconstruct the original signal. This method requires single sensor and can be available for overlapped case. We have obtained two types of partial discharge signals in laboratory and mixed them to simulate a multi-source PD signal. The signals were generated to simulate the case of overlapped and non-overlapped pulses, respectively. The mixed signals entered Encoder-Decoder based Neural Network and was separated into single-source signal. The separation accuracy of multi-PD signals was evaluated by SI-SNR and these values were 25.22dB and 15.67dB, respectively. Furthermore, the defect types of separated signals were identified using CNN model. The accuracy of classification was almost 100%. These result shows that our proposed method can sufficiently separate multi-source PD signals.

articleTitle: Thermal Aging Characteristics of Epoxy Resin: Chemical Structure and Dielectric Property
abstract: Epoxy resin, widely used as an insulating material in electrical power equipment, may face the risk of degradation in its insulating performance when exposed to high temperatures over extended periods. In this paper, epoxy resin samples were prepared and subjected to an accelerated thermal aging test at 180 °C for up to 1440 hours. The physicochemical and dielectric properties were tested at various thermal conditions. The experimental results indicate that the oxidation of hydrogen at the α-position of tertiary carbons in secondary alcohols and esters to form carbonyl groups is the primary reaction during the thermal aging process of epoxy resins, accompanied by the rearrangement of molecular structures due to reactive free radicals. In the early stages, molecular rearrangement and post-curing reactions are predominant, leading to a slight enhancement of dielectric properties. As aging progresses, the oxidation and scission of molecular chains intensify, alongside a decrease in crosslink density and a reduction in the level and density of deep traps. Furthermore, high-temperature aging is associated with the formation of low-density regions, increasing the number of internal defects, which significantly deteriorates the dielectric properties, with an 137% increase in conductivity and a corresponding 18.14% decrease in breakdown strength. This study provides valuable value insights for the assessment of the aging condition of epoxy resins.

articleTitle: Influence of Different Step Time and Step Voltage on the Calculation of Endurance Coefficient in Polypropylene AC Step-Stress Tests
abstract: Polypropylene is considered to be one of the new power cable insulation materials due to its excellent insulating and thermal properties, and numerous of studies on its insulating properties have been published recently. The endurance coefficient plays a vital important role in assessing the performance of polypropylene insulation under long-term electrical stress ageing and the step-stress method is usually adopted to calculate the endurance coefficient of insulation. Nowadays, step stress tests are mainly implemented by changing the step voltage and the method has a large time consumption at longer step times. In this paper, the AC breakdown field strength of polypropylene is obtained by AC breakdown test to provide a reference for step stress test. The polypropylene endurance coefficient is calculated by different methods of varying the step time and the step voltage. It is found that the method of varying the step voltage could also calculate the endurance coefficient of polypropylene and the result is similar to that obtained by varying the step time. At the same time, it is also found that the large step voltage may cause the sample breakdown during the pressurization process, resulting in data distortion, so the step voltage should be selected reasonably when choose the method of changing the step voltage.

articleTitle: Aging Assessment of 220 kV Submarine Cables Based on Ultra-Low Frequency Dielectric Loss
abstract: In this paper, the dielectric loss of submarine cables and their XLPE slices at different thermal aging degree is investigated under ultra-low frequency (ULF) voltage. Two 220 kV short submarine cable samples with a length of 2 meters are prepared, and XLPE slices are prepared by cutting the insulation of the submarine cable. The temperature and time of thermal aging are varied during the experimental process to study the trend of the dielectric loss of the submarine cable insulation, and the results of the dielectric loss of the 220 kV submarine cable and their XLPE slices are compared and analyzed. The results show that the dielectric loss of both samples at ultra-low frequency voltage increases with the aging time. The tendency of the dielectric loss to increase is more significant at higher voltage amplitudes or lower test frequencies. Under the same thermal aging stage, the dielectric loss trends of short submarine cables and their XLPE slices show consistency. Therefore, the changing trend of dielectric loss could be used to characterize the thermal aging degree of submarine cable insulation,

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Next Generation Ester Based Dielectric for Single-Phase Precision Immersion Cooling
abstract: Dielectric coolant research and development is crucial for the global deployment of immersion cooling (IC). The call for safe and truly sustainable dielectric coolants has become prominent over the last years. To answer this demand, a novel non-hazardous and bio-based dielectric ester coolant, i.e. L759, was developed. This coolant combines a low viscosity and high flash point with a precisely controlled material compatibility for single-phase (1P) IC applications. The coolant has been extensively tested in a precision immersion cooled Ku:L2 V1 chassis during more than eight months. The thermal and power performance, material compatibility (i.e. the interactions between the coolant and the hardware) and the long(er)-term coolant stability were thoroughly investigated and discussed. No server malfunctioning (thermal, power) was observed. No major compatibility issues were encountered. In addition, the ester did not degrade upon testing. Ester technology shows great potential in operating 1P IC systems.

articleTitle: Effect of Graft Modification on Electrical Tree Growth in PP/POE Composite Insulation Cables
abstract: This paper focuses on the electrical tree growth characteristics of graft-modified polypropylene (PP) composite polyolefin elastomer (POE) insulation under the combined action of direct current and impulse voltages. The results show that the graft-modified specimens have shorter electrical tree lengths and smaller cumulative damage areas. At high temperatures, the cumulative damage area does not increase significantly, and the DC breakdown strength remains 75% of the original, which has excellent high-temperature stability. The results show that the hindered phenolic compounds grafted on PP/POE can not only inhibit the breakage of PP molecular chain and extension of the amorphous area by scavenging free radicals generated at high temperatures, but also make the mixing of PP and POE more homogeneous and reduce the physical defects of composite insulating materials, which prevents the occurrence of partial discharges, and thus inhibits the growth of electric dendrites.

articleTitle: Polarity Reversal Effect on Space Charge Characteristics of Double Layer of Natural Ester Oil-Impregnated Paper with Different Moisture Contents
abstract: This study investigates the impact of polarity reversal on space charge characteristics in oil-impregnated paper insulation used for HVDC converter transformers, specifically examining the influence of remaining charges on the oil-paper insulation system. Findings show that at moisture levels below 2.0wt.%, mineral oil impregnated paper is more susceptible to polarity reversal than natural ester oil impregnated paper. The hydrophilic nature of natural ester oil mitigates the effects, providing a potential advantage in transformer performance. In contrast, under extremely wet conditions (5.0wt.% moisture), high moisture levels demonstrate the impact of polarity reversal less influential for both mineral oil-paper and natural ester oil-paper.

articleTitle: High Frequency Dielectric Properties and Losses in Partial Discharge Resistant Rotating Machine Insulation
abstract: The complex permittivity of glass-fiber and polyimide backed mica tape for winding insulation in rotating machines have been investigated using a dielectric spectrometer. A frequency ranging from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">‐2</sup> Hz to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Hz and a temperature ranging from 20 °C to 150 °C was applied to both pristine samples and samples aged for one week at 150 °C and 200 °C, respectively. The real part of permittivity, real part of conductivity and loss factor increased for decreasing frequencies and increasing temperatures. For both tape materials, a significant decrease was seen after one week at high temperature, but for the polyimide tape the change was less significant at 150 °C. This temperature is below the thermal class of the insulation. The observed decrease in the real part of permittivity, and hence decreased loss factor is possibly due to a continuing curing of the resin in the insulation system.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of the Dynamic of Electrons Implanted in a Polymeric Material
abstract: This paper focuses on studying the effect induced by the dynamics of radiation charges on the behavior of the electric field within an irradiated polymeric material. Utilizing a simulation model based on the numerical resolution of transport equations, the evolution of implanted charges under various DC electric fields is examined over time. The main analyzed parameter is the depth of the implanted charges within the material. The results obtained demonstrate that when the implanted charges are deeply positioned, they lead to an intensification of the local electric field over a wide area within the material. Moreover, their dynamic response to an applied electric field causes an additional intensification of the local field by approximately 25%. Furthermore, these charges tend to accumulate increasingly as they penetrate deeper into the bulk of the material.

articleTitle: The Evolution of Space Charge and Electric Field in HVDC Cable under Polarity Reversal Voltage Superimposed with Temperature Gradient
abstract: The evolution of space charge and electric field under polarity reversal voltage superimposed with temperature gradient (ΔT) in the insulation of HVDC cable are studied. The results show that the maximum electric field (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>) appears near the inner shielding layer during polarity reversal. As the ΔT rises, the E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> during polarity reversal aggravates gradually. Extending the voltage reversal period enhances the accumulation of negative charges during the process, thereby mitigating the E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> after the polarity reversal. During voltage polarity reversal, the variation trend of net charges on the inner side aligns with that of electrons. Hence, the electron transport behaviors near the inner shielding layer constitute an important factor influencing electric field distortion.

articleTitle: A Novel Piezoelectric Paper-Based Flexible Nanogenerator Composed of Rochelle Salt Nanoparticles and Bacterial Cellulose
abstract: In this paper, Rochelle salt (RS) nanoparticles were doped into bacterial cellulose (BC) films, and BC/RS composite films with different RS mass fractions were prepared by physical blending. The effects of typical ferroelectric material additives on the dielectric and piezoelectric properties of BC were studied. A renewable flexible piezoelectric material with excellent properties was prepared. The dielectric and piezoelectric properties of the composite films with different RS ratios were tested in the laboratory. The results show that the introduction of the RS phase in RS/BC composite films has little effect on the original chemical structure of the materials. The sensitivity of the materials remained high while the piezoelectric constants of the materials were substantially enhanced, and the response curves were nearly linear in the face of different magnitudes of external forces. In addition, the introduction of the RS phase also improves the dielectric constant of the materials, thus optimizing its dielectric properties. The novel renewable flexible piezoelectric materials prepared in this paper contribute to the application of miniature piezoelectric nanogenerators in power systems.

articleTitle: Influence of Harmonic Distortion on the Breakdown Voltage of a Composite Material for the Use in Dry Type Transformers
abstract: In this contribution, an investigation about the influence of voltage harmonics on the breakdown voltage of a composite material intended for the use of dry-type transformers produced under the filament winding technology is discussed. A dielectric strength measurement was performed on samples of a composite applying voltage with different waveforms With the intention of recreating the structural disposition of the material, which originates as a result of the manufacturing process by rolling filaments, which are previously impregnated on a resin bath, on a rotating mandrel, a special arrangement has been used for the manufacture of the test objects, consisting of plates with fiberglass bundles under mechanical tension in an epoxy resin matrix. Test samples were exposed to six different voltage waveforms, differing in their total harmonic distortion (THD). The test voltage is generated through a programmable source and a high voltage test transformer. The performed measurements show differences on the RMS value of the breakdown voltage of the material according to the total harmonic distortion. A comparison between the values based on the RMS values and the peak values is given.

articleTitle: Research on Transformer Oil Condition Diagnosis Technology Based on Multi-Frequency Ultrasonic Detection
abstract: Oil-paper insulation is an important form of insulation in transformers. Under external stresses such as discharge and overheating, transformer oil may gradually deteriorate, leading to changes in its physical and chemical properties. In this paper, a multi-frequency diagnosis system for transformer oil insulation status is designed based on multi-frequency ultrasonic detection technology, with the frequency range of ultrasonic waves between 200-1000 kHz. The diagnosis of transformer oil status is achieved by comparing the attenuation spectra of multi-frequency ultrasonic signals received by the receiving sensor and transmitted by the transmitting sensor. To analyze the characteristics of the attenuation spectra of multi-frequency ultrasonic signals of transformer oil with different degrees of aging, a comprehensive experimental platform is established. This platform combines the pulse current method and the dissolved gas analysis method to study the ultrasonic attenuation spectra characteristics of transformer oil in the initiation, development, and pre-breakdown stages of discharge. It provides experimental basis for subsequent theoretical analysis and diagnosis of transformer oil insulation status.

articleTitle: Effect of Radial Space Charge Distribution on Electric Field Distribution in HVDC XLPE Cables
abstract: High voltage DC (HVDC) cables accumulate space charge and distort the internal electric field distribution during operation. In this paper, the insulation layer of 400kV HVDC cables is taken as the research object. The space charge distribution characteristics of XLPE specimens with different radial positions are studied. The insulation layer is uniformly sliced into thin sheets and divided into three parts: inner, middle and outer. The space charge distribution of XLPE specimens at different radial positions is measured at 30 to 70°C and ±10 to ±30kV/mm electric field strength. The measurement results are taken into the simulation model to calculate the electric field distribution. The results show that the space charge of the inner and outer layers varies significantly with temperature and electric field. The space charge of the middle layer specimen changes with hysteresis. The electric field simulation results show that the electric field intensity is larger at the inner insulation position when no load is applied, and larger at the outer insulation position when full load is applied.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of the Electric Field in HVDC GIL with Application of Surface Conductivity Gradient Material
abstract: Gas insulated systems are utilized in narrow spaces and possess advantages in reliability, low loss and power capacity. HVDC gas insulated lines (GIL) are a suitable transmission technology for electrical energy. However, under DC condition space charge accumulation occurs and may lead to enhanced electric field stress within the GIL. The interface between solid and gaseous insulation is especially sensitive for electric fields and charge accumulation. Therefore, surface functionally graded material (SFGM) is applied as a field control technique to decrease the electric field. Thus, different SFGM approaches are investigated in this work by numerical simulation to optimize the electric field distribution within HVDC GIL.

articleTitle: Lifetime Estimation of Epoxy Cast Insulation under Medium-frequency Square Voltage with Ramp Breakdown Tests
abstract: The medium-frequency (MF) square voltage stress generated by power modules challenges the integrity of epoxy resin cast insulation in MF transformers (MFT). This study aims at a lifetime prediction by ramp stress tests with MF square voltages in the absence of partial discharges. Weibull-inverse power model was employed for the breakdown voltages (BDVs) with modulated voltage ramp rates. The obtained inverse power terms are 11.04 and 14.29 for 1 kHz and 10 kHz unipolar voltages, indicating a high-field per pulse aging mechanism. The non-monotone trend of BDVs with different voltage ramp rates for 10 kHz voltage were found and discussed.

articleTitle: Effect of Microstructure and Stretching Ratio on Dielectric Properties of Polypropylene Films for HVDC Capacitors
abstract: In this paper, polypropylene (PP) pellets with different isotacticity were prepared, and PP films were obtained by different stretching ratios. The crystallization characteristics of different films were studied and the dielectric properties at various temperatures were analyzed. Further, the influence of microstructure parameter and stretching ratio on the dielectric performance of PP films was explored. The result shows that the PP film with isotacticity of 99.6% and stretching ratio of 4 × 4 has the highest breakdown strength and the lowest conductivity. The improvement of isotacticity can enhance the crystallinity and improve the loose structure of the molecular chain in the amorphous region, thus inhibiting the migration of charge carriers. In addition, a reasonable stretching ratio can elevate the orientation degree of molecular chain to form an orderly crystalline morphology, thereby improving the crystallinity. This research provides experimental and theoretical support for the enhancement of electrical performance of PP films.

articleTitle: Improved Dielectric Performance of Silicone Rubber Filled with Graphene under Gradient Magnetic Field
abstract: In this paper, graphene nanoparticles are doped into silicone rubber (SiR) to research the electrical tree characteristics under a gradient magnetic field. The results indicate that SiR doped with graphene nanoparticles can improve its insulating performance under a magnetic field. The probability of electrical tree initiation in samples decreases with different nanoparticle contents. When the doping content is low, the growth process of the electrical tree is effectively inhibited. Moreover, after adding graphene nanoparticles, the breakdown time of the samples is also extended. The sample with a content of 0.003wt% has the best performance. However, when the doping content exceeds this value, the performance improvement effect is weakened. The growth of the electrical tree in SiR can be limited because the injected charge is captured by graphene nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Measurement of Space Charge Distribution and Partial Discharge by PEA Method
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency of inverter-driven motors, it is required to prevent partial discharge, and it has been pointed out that PDIV may be lowered during operation due to the space charge that accumulates in the insulation material used to coat the windings. However, there have been few experimental attempts to demonstrate this effect. Therefore, in this study, the effect of space charge accumulation in insulating materials on PD characteristics was verified by the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) metho. As a result, it was clarified that the space charge accumulation influences PDIV degradation.

articleTitle: Simulation of Space Charge in HVDC Cable under DC Superimposed Operating Impulse Voltage
abstract: This research examines the space charge properties of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulation for HVDC cables under DC superimposed operating impulse voltage. A bipolar charge transport (BCT) model considering impurity dissociation is developed to simulate the evolution of the electric field and charge distribution in XLPE under DC superimposed impulse voltages of different polarities. The results show that there is an obvious polarity effect on the space charge characteristics within the cable insulation when subjected to impulse voltage. Specifically, the application of a homopolar impulse voltage leads to an overall intensification of the electric field within the insulation, facilitating the injection and migration of homopolar charges and culminating in enhanced charge accumulation. Conversely, the application of an opposite polarity impulse voltage triggers a complex electric field reversal process (positive-negative-positive). The reversed electric field will lead to the extraction and recombination of the originally accumulated homopolar charge at the electrodes, resulting in a decrease in the amount of accumulated charge. The space charge characteristics under the superimposed heteropolar impulse voltage become insignificant due to the repeated alternation of the electric field within the insulation.

articleTitle: Study of Intermediate States of Ge-Rich GeSbTe Phase Change Memories by Impedance Spectroscopy
abstract: We propose a first investigation of intermediate resistance states of Ge-rich GST (GGST) PCMs by impedance spectroscopy. We highlight that all states present resistive and capacitive components. When switching the memory from the RESET to the SET state the resistance decreases continuously from a low resistance state to a high resistance state while we observe the opposite behavior for the capacitance values. Based on these results, we propose to redefine a state by considering not only the resistance but also the capacitance of the device.

articleTitle: A Ternary Co-polyimide for High-temperature Capacitive Energy Storage
abstract: The development of modern power electronic systems places increasing demands on polymer dielectrics for continuous operation under extreme conditions of high temperature and high electric field. However, the insulating and thermal stability of current polymer dielectrics are often contradictory and mutually exclusive. Herein, we report a ternary co-polyimide that introduces both a highly rigid main-chains and saturated alicyclic side-chains. The former ensures the stability of the copolymer at elevated temperatures and reduces intrachain charge transfer due to its isopropyl structural units with large dihedral angles. The latter increases the molecular chain spacing and decreases interchain charge transfer due to its bulky alicyclic side groups. The resultant copolymer shows decent discharge energy density with 90% charge-discharge efficiency at 200 °C (6.1 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) and 250 °C (3.1 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>), far exceeding those of conventional dielectric polymers and polymer composites. Here a completely new dimension is offered for the molecular design of polymers, giving rise to well-balanced thermal and dielectric properties, and ultimately the desired capacitive energy storage performance at high temperatures. The molecular design strategy in this work regulates the charge transfer process based on the intrinsic structure of the polymer and provides a new perspective for the future development of advanced high-temperature polymer dielectrics.

articleTitle: Effect of Stress Relaxation on Insulating Properties of Dielectric Elastomers with Different Pre-strain Ratios
abstract: Dielectric elastomer (DE) has been considered as ideal artificial muscles due to its intrinsic softness and flexibility, large reversible deformation, high specific energy density as well as light quality. However, low modulus and large elastic deformation bring about electromechanical instability (EMI), resulting limited electrical breakdown strength. Pre-strain can efficiently eliminate EMI and improve DE's breakdown strength. Theoretically, stress relaxation will make the effect decline with the time subsequently. In this paper, we have investigated the influence of pre-strain ratio and time to DE's insulating properties. After stress relaxation, the electrical breakdown strength of dielectric elastomers does not constantly decay, and its variation is consistent with that of Young's modulus and dependent on the pre-strain ratios.

articleTitle: Electrical Characteristics and Surface Topography of Elastomeric Nanocomposites Based on Multi-walled Carbon Nanotubes and Poly(Dimethylsiloxane)
abstract: This work presents the influence of the weight fraction of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) in the poly(dimethylsiloxane) matrix on electrical insulating and morphological properties of the composite films. Atomic force microscopy surface topography maps showed good dispersion of MWCNTs within the polymer matrix without aggregates on the surface. Using of broadband dielectric spectroscopy measurements, it was found out that the percolation threshold of composite films lies in the MWCNTs concentration range of 0.5 - 1.5 wt. % in polymer matrix. For nanocomposites above to the percolation threshold, the impedance response showed a shift from conductive to dielectric-like behavior as frequency is increased. This global impedance response is attributed to the presence of conductive particles distributed in an insulating polymer matrix acting as a complex network of local resistors and capacitors.

articleTitle: Effect of Low Molecular Weight Part of LDPE on DC Conductivity of XLPE
abstract: Crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) is commonly used as high voltage direct current (HVDC) cable insulation material, which is obtained by crosslinking low-density polyethylene (LDPE). Its electrical and mechanical properties will be influenced by LDPE. In addition, the electric field distribution within DC cable insulation depends on the material's conductivity. Therefore, this paper focuses on the relationship between XLPE conductivity and the low-molecular-weight part of LDPE. Though controlling the extraction temperature, the low-molecular-weight part was removed to different extents, which can be supported by the decreasing trends of methyl, carbonyl, and vinyl. The research on the change in material structure showed that with the removal of the low-molecular-weight part, the crosslinking degree of XLPE slightly increased, the crystallinity of LDPE increased while that of XLPE remained essentially unchanged, mainly due to the inhibition of crosslinking on crystallization. Analysis of conductivity revealed that the removal of the low molecular weight part led to a decrease in DC conductivity and an increase in activation energy. This can be attribute to the reduced carrier concentration and enhanced crosslinking network. Based on the relationship between the low-molecular-weight part and XLPE conductivity, this paper provides a perspective on the control of base resin for the development of XLPE.

articleTitle: About Plasma-Polymer Interaction and Treeing Progression
abstract: Partial discharges are one of the main aging mechanisms of electrical components. Some specific types of partial discharges, such as surface discharges and treeing, involve the interaction of a plasma with a polymeric surface. Our aim is to build a multi-scale model that describes the ageing of dielectric materials exposed to these types of partial discharges and can, possibly, shed new light on the treeing progression.

articleTitle: Partial Discharges Detection Using an Electromagnetic Antenna: a New Approach Based on Polyimide-Epoxy Samples
abstract: The development of reliable electrical machines must consider the ageing phenomena of winding insulation system. When subjected to PWM-like voltages, the winding insulation degradation may be accelerated through partial discharges (PD). The use of wide band gap power electronics components implies to consider these degradations even for low-voltage applications. To assess the electrical insulation health state of the winding, PD detection can be performed. The aim of this study is to investigate the PD inception in polyimide-epoxy samples designed with an enclosed cavity. A detection system based on an electric field antenna combined with a spectrum analyzer is developed for this purpose. An impulse winding tester and a Silicon Carbide-based power generator are both used to carry out this PD study. Switching frequencies up to 80 kHz are analyzed in terms of PD inception voltage.

articleTitle: Charge Transport Model Considering the Presence of Ions in an XLPE Containing By-Products
abstract: Chemical residues, generally resulting from material preparation, exist in the volume of polymer insulations and impact their dielectric properties. This is particularly the case in XLPE, where by-products from cross-linking and antioxidants exist. In the presence of an electric field, these chemical species can dissociate or ionize, giving rise to ionic charges. Like electronic charges, ions contribute to conduction and to space charge accumulation in the insulation under DC stress. However, it is difficult experimentally to distinguish the role of electronic and ionic species. In this paper, we simulate the impact of the presence of ions by modeling their generation and transport in an XLPE containing dissociable by-products. Ionic phenomena are combined with electronic ones in a bipolar charge transport model, assuming that ionic charges result from dissociation of neutral species in the insulation volume. The model is described, and simulation results are presented and discussed as regards the impact of the presence of ionic species on space charge and current.

articleTitle: Different Oxygen Diffusion Patterns in XLPE Under Thermal Oxidative Aging
abstract: The thermal oxidative aging of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) significantly impacts the long-term stability of high-voltage cables. However, understanding the oxygen diffusion behavior in XLPE under various aging conditions remains unclear. This study aims to explore the distribution of oxygen along the thickness direction of aged XLPE sheet samples. Experimental results show that after aging, the fracture elongation and tensile strength of severely aged samples drop to less than half of their initial values, indicating chemical changes in XLPE nearing the end of its lifespan. FTIR tests reveal a linear increase in the carbonyl index of aged samples over time. Microscopic infrared testing of fractured surfaces reveals significant differences in oxygen diffusion between XLPE aged in a high elastic state and in a molten state. In the molten state, the carbonyl index exhibits high values at the surface and low values in the middle throughout the aging stage. Initially, XLPE in the high elastic state shows a similar pattern, but in the late stage of aging, an abnormal distribution emerges, with high carbonyl index values in the middle and low values on the surface. This study highlights significant differences in oxygen diffusion patterns of XLPE with certain thicknesses during aging under different phase states. These findings provide an experimental basis for improving cable life assessment models in the industry.

articleTitle: A Novel Electric Field Stress Optimization Method for High-voltage IGBT Module Based on AC Dielectrophoresis
abstract: High-voltage IGBT modules are the critical components of new power systems. However, since the IGBT is subjected to unipolar square wave voltage for a long time, it is very easy for space charge accumulation to occur at the triple point, which will cause electric field distortion and eventually insulation damage. In this paper, the nonlinear conductive materials with adjustable nonlinear coefficients and switch-field stress were constructed based on AC dielectrophoresis for homogenizing the electric field. Firstly, a spatio-temporal evolution model considering “electric field stress-time-temperature” was constructed based on the classical Debye model and the carrier hopping conductivity model. Further, the dielectrophoresis process parameters corresponding to the optimal electric field distributions at 30°C, 60°C, and 90°C were calculated by simulation. Finally, the effectiveness of the above method in suppressing the local electric field distortion of IGBT was verified by partial discharge test, which can significantly improve partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) by 31.5%.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Inception Voltage of Pigtail Samples with Type II Insulation and Sinusoidal vs Switched Voltage
abstract: Partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) under sinusoidal voltage and switched voltage with dV/dt of 20 V/ns have been investigated for pigtail samples with type II insulation consisting of Litz wire as conductor and mica-Kapton tape as groundwall insulation. Voltage was increased in steps of 100 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">peak</inf> with duration of 60 s for both sinusoidal and switched voltage with switching frequency of 45 Hz until PDs were observed. No significant difference in the PDIV for sinusoidal and switched voltage was found. Further, sinusoidal voltage was applied until breakdown. No correlation between breakdown voltage and PDIV was found, but very large PDs (∼ 100 nC) consequently initiated 4-5 kV below breakdown voltage. Dissection of the tested pigtails showed multiple voids in the wedge between Litz wire strands and the inner insulation layer, suspected to cause the main portion of the PDs. Such voids with only a thin varnish covering the electrode surfaces would get less significant space charge build-up. Therefore, a low field enhancement from space charges is expected during the fast voltage change of switched voltage.

articleTitle: Influence of Thermal Conductivity of Multi-scale Particles Epoxy Composites on High-Frequency Electrical Insulation Property
abstract: Epoxy, with excellent electrical insulation properties, processing performance, and low price, is commonly used for transformers (110kV and below) and power electronic transformers (high-frequency transformers) as the primary insulating material. Since the thermal conductivity of epoxy resins is only 0.2 W/(m·K), the electrical insulation properties decline significantly at high frequency. Preparing epoxy composites with high thermal conductivity and excellent electrical insulation at high frequencies is a great challenge for industrial production. It is considered that SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (9 eV), BN (5.9 eV), and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (7.2-8.8 eV) are thermally conductive particles with good electrical insulation properties. The materials filled with different micron-scale particles have higher thermal conductivity than the nanofilled materials. In this study, 5 μm SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, 25 μm BN, and 40 μm Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> were used as fillers, and the filler ratios were calculated according to the Dinger-Funk model, focusing on the effects of the variation of filler content on thermal conductivity and electrical insulation properties. The thermal conductivity of the epoxy composites improved with the increase of filler content up to 1.003 W/(m·K), while the AC breakdown field strength gradually decreased. However, the breakdown time at 20 kHz, 35 kV/mm bipolar square wave appeared to increase and then decrease with the increase of content. Therefore, the optimum content of fillers allows the preparation of efficient epoxy composites as insulating materials for power electronic transformers. This study provides ideas for designing thermally conductive composites operating at high frequency and high voltage fields.

articleTitle: Response of Polypropylene and its Nanocomposite with Synthetic Nanoclay under Electric Field and Temperature
abstract: It is a known fact that polypropylene is an important engineering material that is also used in electrical systems as a dielectric. The objective of this study is to evaluate the time-to-failure behavior of nanocomposite polypropylene and compare it against the plain polypropylene as a function of thermal and electric fields. The polypropylene used in this investigation is isotactic polypropylene, while its nanocomposite is 2% nanometric synthetic clay doped polypropylene. At each target temperature level, the samples are subjected to sinusoidal electric fields of 3 levels, namely 40 kV/mm, 50 kV/mm and 60 kV/mm. Based on the findings in this study, the plain polypropylene samples have higher time-to-failure than the nanocomposite polypropylene. It seems that having 2% nanometric synthetic clay in polypropylene does not show enhancement in time-to-failure.

articleTitle: Behavior of Water and Ions Within Polyethylene: Insights from Molecular Dynamics Simulations
abstract: Understanding the molecular-level behavior of water and ions is crucial for comprehending the degradation phenomena in polymeric materials. This study employs molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the behavior of water, sodium ions (Na+), and sulfate ions (SO42-) within alkane molecules (C120H242). Our approach involved constructing various computational models to simulate the dynamics of water and ions under electric fields, particularly on their behavior within spaces confined by C120H242. The findings reveal significant insights: in free water, electric fields significantly influence the diffusion constants of Na+ and SO42-. A notable observation is the reduced mobility resulting from increased attraction between Na+ and SO42 in the absence of water. In confined spaces, diffusion becomes more pronounced when ion movement aligns with the direction of electric field, and a lower concentration of ions correlates with higher diffusion constants. Moreover, under intense electric fields, ions and water molecules are observed to penetrate C120H242, thereby maintaining an ordered arrangement.

articleTitle: Effect of Coating Conductivity on Surface Charge Accumulation with Metal Particle on DC Conical Insulator
abstract: This paper focuses on the surface charge accumulation on conical insulators in DC gas-insulated switchgear (GIS). Down-sized insulators applied with high-, low- and nonlinear-conductivity coatings were selected as test samples with a metal particle attached to the central conductor. After being charged by ±15 kV DC voltage for 1 hour, the charge distributions on the concave and convex surfaces of the insulator were displayed. The results showed that the effect of coating conductivity on surface charge accumulation was related to the polarity of applied voltage and surface characteristics of the insulator. A charge spot appeared near the metal particle, on the convex surface, a hetero-charge spot tended to be formed while on the convex surface, the polarity of the charge spot was reversed.

articleTitle: Electric Field Distribution and Evolution in ±500 kV Submarine Cable Factory Joint under Steady and Transient Voltages
abstract: This article focuses on the evolution of the electric field in HVDC submarine cable factory joints (FJ) under steady voltage (DC voltage) and transient voltage (switching overvoltage and polarity reversal voltage). A charge transport model is established based on the geometric model of FJ. Under DC voltage, the accumulated space charges near the insulation interface weaken the interface electric field, and the maximum electric field (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{max}$</tex>) occurs in the return insulation. When the DC voltage is superimposed with the opposite polarity switching impulse voltage, the electric field at the interface increases abruptly to 45.4 kV/mm. The polarity reversal voltage also causes the interface field to reach 39.5 kV/mm. Under the transient voltage, the maximum value of tangential electric field (Et) at the interface appears on the inner side of the insulation. When the DC voltage is superimposed with the opposite polarity switching impulse voltage, the maximum Et at the interface is 14.8 kV/mm, which is 155.2 % higher than that under the DC voltage.

articleTitle: Space Charge Distribution Measurements of Thin-Film Insulating Materials with Slow Sound Velocity using a High-Resolution PEA System
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) associated with higher voltages in inverter-driven motors has become a problem; one of the reduction causes of PD-inception voltage is said to be the space charge that accumulates in the winding coating material, especially at high temperatures, and it is necessary to investigate this accumulation characteristic. However, the typical thickness of the coating material of the windings used in electric vehicles is about 30 μm, making it difficult to measure the space charge distribution with the usual PEA (pulse electrostatic stress) method, which has a positional resolution of about 10 μm.
