In the present study, a thin P(VDF-TrFE) piezoelectric sensor was formed directly onto a ground electrode deposited on both sides of sapphire glass, which is said to have good acoustic propagation characteristics, by the spin coating method, and used to obtain a position resolution of about 2.5 μm at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$80^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. The resolution was successfully improved significantly.

articleTitle: Effect of Metal Deactivator on Breakdown and Energy Storage Properties of Polypropylene Modified by Deashing Method for Film Capacitors
abstract: In this paper, a novel deashing solution of metal deactivator/anhydrous ethanol is prepared to reduce the ash content and improve the breakdown and energy storage performances of polypropylene (PP). Meanwhile, the deashing method is optimized by adjusting the type and content of metal deactivator. The breakdown and energy storage properties of the deashed samples were tested. The results show that under the optimal concentration, the breakdown strengths of the samples deashed by different kinds of solution are improved by 29.5∼34.8% and the maximum discharge energy densities increase by 11.7∼35.6%. In addition, the total ash contents of the deashed samples decrease by 20.7∼72.1%. The chelation reaction between the metal deactivator and ash promotes the migration of ash to the deashing solution, which not only significantly reduces the ash content of PP, but also reduces the shallow trap density. Therefore, the carrier transport process is inhibited, and the breakdown and energy storage properties are significantly improved.

articleTitle: A Charge Microscopy for High Temperature Use with a Polymer Acoustic Coupler
abstract: In the insulation technology, complex systems including heterogeneous interfaces are often handled, and it is desirable to measure the electric field distortion and its dynamic change due to space charge spreading in two or three dimensions. A well-known scanning device for this purpose was proposed by Maeno et al. based on the pulsed electro-acoustic method. To detect acoustic signals generated by electric charges, a metallic acoustic coupler, which also serves as an electrode, coupled to the water medium. An aspherical acoustic lens was used to compensate for large aberrations. The presenter fabricated an acoustic coupler made of a polymer whose sound velocity is close to that of water to reduce aberration problems. The high thermal resistance of the polymer acoustic coupler was utilized to enable measurement at temperatures exceeding 100°C.

articleTitle: Correlation Method to Explore Corona Discharge Dynamics Under DC Harmonic Voltages
abstract: Employing correlation analysis, this investigation applied two non-destructive coupling sensors measuring the corona discharge characteristics in air compressed to 6 Bar. The study aimed to understand how harmonic contents, especially those resulting from commutation and overlap angles, affect harmonic voltage distortions. To achieve precise diagnostics of the ripple effect in discharge inception, this work utilized both an ultra-high frequency antenna and a current transformer. Through simultaneous measurement in real-time and data cluster stacking, the results indicated that the harmonic voltages on the DC side arise from its frequency components. The correlation plots demonstrated diverse responses of discharge distribution when adjusting the commutation control settings. It is proposed that correlation results might offer insights into quantifying the ripple voltage influence on the corona discharge distribution pattern, and also assess the correlation between the commutation overlap control strategies and the behavior of discharge pulses.

articleTitle: Hindered Phenolic Compound Grafting Modification and Space Charge Investigation of PP Cable Insulation
abstract: This paper explores the impact of grafting molecule types on the physicochemical and insulation properties of polypropylene (PP) cables. Two molecules without hindered phenolic groups are selected as comparative samples. Three types of grafted polypropylene insulation samples are prepared, and the electrical conductivity, space charge characteristics, and direct current breakdown characteristics of polypropylene under direct voltage are studied. The results indicate that hindered phenolic compounds can significantly mitigate the conductivity of polypropylene at elevated temperatures compared to the other two grafted small molecules. In space charge experiments, the grafted modified materials exhibit reduced quantities of space charge, leading to higher breakdown field strengths. This indicates that hindered phenolic compounds can increase trap density, reduce the number of hot electrons, avoid molecular chain damage, and thus extend the insulation life of PP.

articleTitle: Comparison of High Temperature Dielectric Properties Between Epoxy Resins with Alicyclic and Bisphenol A
abstract: The purpose of this study is to elucidate the dielectric properties of alicyclic epoxy resins at elevated temperatures. Compared to common bisphenol A epoxy resins, alicyclic epoxy resins have a higher glass transition temperature and lower viscosity in the liquid state. Therefore, alicyclic epoxy resins are expected to exhibit good dielectric properties in high temperature environments. In this paper, we compare the dielectric properties of alicyclic epoxy resins and bisphenol A epoxy resins from room temperature to high temperature.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Piezoelectric Ceramic Nanofibers for Flexible Transducers and Advanced Applications
abstract: Polymeric piezoelectric materials have attracted enormous success in the field of wearable electronics due to their high flexibility and good mechanical stability. Nonetheless, these materials exhibit a low piezoelectric response if compared to ceramics. This study is focused on the development of a flexible and highly sensitive piezoelectric sensor made with ceramic lead zirconate titanate (PZT) nanofibers. Results show an exceptionally high sensitivity of 30 mV/N and a piezoelectric strain coefficient d33 of 39 pC/N for the fabricated PZT sensor.

articleTitle: Epoxy-glass-mica Layered Composites with Nanoparticle Fillers Incorporated by Air-brush Technique
abstract: Three-component electrical insulating composites (epoxy-glass-mica systems) represent key electrical insulating materials for high-voltage applications, which are produced in a very wide range of variants and still represent materials suitable for further innovations and improvements. The improvement of these composites can be achieved by incorporating different types of nanofillers as a fourth component of the composite, as is the subject of presented research. As well as the selection of a suitable nanofiller and its level of filling, the proper dispersion of nanoparticles in the volume of the polymer is crucial in terms of the resulting composite properties. For this reason, this paper discusses the usage of the air-brush technique for a uniform deposition of nanoparticles. Epoxy-glass-mica prepregs and fillers based on boron nitride, aluminium oxide, and halloysite nanotubes were used for preparation of the layered composites. Comparison of the dielectric analyses results for the reference composite and the composites with fillers incorporated by the air-brush technique revealed that certain differences in volume resistivity, dissipation factor, and parameters related to the occurrence of partial discharges have been achieved.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Thermal Aging Characteristics between Silicone Rubber and Epoxy Resin for Dry-Type Transformer
abstract: Epoxy resin (EP) and silicone rubber (SIR) are commonly used insulating materials in dry-type transformers. In this paper, the electrical, mechanical, and thermal stability properties of SIR and EP are compared under thermal aging conditions at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{180}^ \circ }\mathrm{C}$</tex>. The results indicate that the SIR has a higher activation energy, less long-term performance degradation, and better stability at high temperatures compared to EP. Additionally, while EP has greater tensile strength and lower elongation at break, SIR shows less decline in mechanical performance after aging, suggesting a longer service life. When considering SIR as a possible replacement for EP, it is important to pay attention to its aging performance over the expected service life to ensure sufficient insulating properties and mechanical strength. These findings provide important reference for the selection of insulating materials for dry-type power equipment.

articleTitle: Initiation and Growth Characteristics of Electrical Trees at Ultra-Low Frequency Voltage
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of ultra-low frequency (ULF) voltage amplitude and frequency on the initiation and growth characteristics of electrical trees in cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulation. The needle electrode was inserted into the XLPE cable insulation to prepare the needle plate electrode sample, which was used to initiate the electrical tree. The microscopic observation system was used to record the growth process of electrical trees. At the same time, the influences of ultra-low frequency voltage and power frequency voltage on the initiation voltage of electric tree were compared and analyzed. The results show that the initiation voltage of electrical trees decreases with the increase of voltage frequency. The growth rate and fractal dimension of the electrical tree increase with higher voltage amplitude or frequency.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Degradation of Five Esters and the Effect of the Cellulose on Their Properties
abstract: The need to replace mineral oils used in the cooling and insulation of transformers has led to the development of various alternatives. The most promising options include synthetic and natural esters of various origins. However, based on the available information and the studies conducted under different conditions, it is not possible to determine if the long-term behaviour and properties of all esters are the same. This work analyses the five main commercial esters (sunflower, rapeseed, soybean, palm and synthetic) and their degradation when combined with kraft and thermally upgraded papers. The insulating materials were aged along with copper at 130 °C in sealed glass vials. The performance of the fluids was studied through the measurement of moisture content, acidity, interfacial tension, and dielectric dissipation factor. Moreover, the ageing of the cellulosic materials was monitored by the reduction of the polymerisation degree. The results showed that there are significant differences between esters of different origins. Furthermore, the properties of the esters were affected by the paper they were combined with.

articleTitle: New Advancements in Measuring the Distribution of Electric Charges within Liquids using PEA
abstract: The Electrical Double Layer (EDL) is a physic of charge generation and distribution that appears as soon as a liquid gets in contact with a solid surface. Through not fully understood physicochemical reactions, the solid and liquid molecules react with each other by an ionization process generating electrical charges that are distributed into two layers of opposite polarity, one in the solid and the other one in the liquid. Various theoretical approaches have been developed to understand and predict charge behavior at the interface. Nevertheless, experimental validation using tools is a considerable challenge due to technical issues associated with measuring the relatively low magnitude of the involved charges. The primary goal of this study is to experimentally determine the charge distribution at solid/liquid interfaces, employing an innovative adaptation of the Electro Acoustic Pulse method (PEA-L). The PEA-L measurement instrumentation will be presented, and the response at the aluminum/ethanol interface will be analyzed.

articleTitle: Detection and Diagnosis of High Voltage Cable Water-Blocking Buffer Layer Defect based on Frequency Domain Reflection Method
abstract: This article investigates the detection and diagnosis of defects in the water-blocking buffer layer of high-voltage cables using frequency domain reflectometry (FDR). Firstly, considering the possibility of the buffer layer affecting the distributed parameters of the cable, a parameter model for the distributed capacitance and distributed conductance of high-voltage cables is derived from electrostatic field theory. Then, based on the surface morphology characteristics of the buffer layer, the state of the buffer layer is classified into dry, moisture, corrosion, and ablation. The volume resistivity and relative permittivity of the buffer layer in different states are tested using sheet samples, and the influence of these states on the distributed conductance and distributed capacitance of high-voltage cables is further analyzed, obtaining the mechanism of how buffer layer defects affect the characteristic impedance of high-voltage cables. Finally, by constructing an experimental platform for detecting buffer layer defects in high-voltage cables in the laboratory, it is confirmed that the FDR method can effectively detect and diagnose defects in the buffer layer of high-voltage cables.

articleTitle: Erosion of Polymers by Partial Discharge at Atmospheric Pressure
abstract: The erosion of electrical systems due to partial discharges (PD) is an essential subject for various industries (automotive, railway, aerospace, etc.) with the transition to electric energy. In this study, we investigated the erosion of Kapton over a short period while also measuring the energy of PDs. This allowed us to study the relationship between PD energy and erosion rate. The experimental setup consisted of five cells powered by five independent voltage sources. We also discussed the method of measuring energy. Erosion is measured using a profilometer. The experimental results show a good correlation between energy measurement and erosion rate, suggesting that the partial discharge energy is a promising erosion indicator. Furthermore, the influence of frequency and exposure time on erosion behaviour is examined.

articleTitle: Graded Surface Modification of Electric Vehicles Motor Insulating Material by using Plasma to Tailor Surface Charges
abstract: Insulation challenges in power frequency converters arise from electric stresses on motor winding slots and overhang junctions, leading to erosion of stress-grading insulation due to partial discharge and heat. Additionally, nonuniform electric field distribution and thermal transients at the slot-coil interface pose challenges. This study focuses on modifying the surface of polyimide-based composite varnishing to achieve uniform electric field distribution. A novel fluorescence-enhanced hexamethyldisiloxane atmospheric pressure plasma jet is used to modify the surface, enhancing surface conductivity and converting deep traps into shallow traps. Samples treated with plasma demonstrate accelerated dissipation of accumulated charges, signifying enhanced electrical properties. This improvement can help to improve other electrical characteristics like flashover and breakdown strength. Furthermore, the integration of graphene oxide enhances thermal properties, facilitating the efficient dissipation of heat generated during electric motor operation.

articleTitle: Developing Novel Self Healable Capacitor Materials with Improved Thermostability
abstract: The current work reports the chemical modification of polyolefins in presence of a free radical initiator via reactive extrusion. The crosslinked network is formed upon radical coupling during processing which is substantiated by viscoelastic measurements. The network formed consists of a polyethylene gel with free polypropylene with improved dielectric properties. The designed material is stable at elevated temperatures with an inherent self-healability which renders it a potential candidate as capacitor in power electronics.

articleTitle: Research on Characteristics of Typical Partial Discharge Pattern in GIS Based on SiPM
abstract: Inevitable defects often occur in the process of GIS manufacturing, transportation and assembly, which will affect the operation of the power grid. In this paper, an array optical sensor is designed based on a Silicon photomultiplier tube (SiPM) to detect partial discharge in GIS, and a measurement platform and defect model are built to simulate partial discharge in GIS according to the conditions required by the optical measurement method. Corona discharge, creepage discharge, internal discharge and discharge between metallic parts on floating potential are measured by SiPM array, and the influence of sensor distances of 10 cm, 15 cm and 20 cm on the sensitivity is investigated. According to the obtained data, the phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) spectra of four discharge types are obtained. Then, the PD feature spectra, such as phase-maximum discharge quantity, phase-average discharge quantity, and discharge frequency-discharge quantity, are analyzed, from which statistical characteristics, including skewness, kurtosis, discharge factor, phase asymmetry, and correlation coefficient, are extracted. The results indicate a negative correlation between the sensor's sensitivity and the distance between discharge sources. Different discharge types can be effectively classified by comparing phase-discharge quantity spectra and statistical characteristics.

articleTitle: Effect of Mechanical Stress on Dielectric Properties of Epoxy Resin
abstract: This study examines the dielectrics properties of epoxy resin under mechanical stresses ranging from -10 to +10 MPa commonly encountered in gas insulated transmission lines (GIL) and gas insulated switchgears (GIS) systems. With the tensile stress increases, the permittivity of the epoxy resin decreases and the conductivity, trap energy level and accumulated charge increase. The opposite is true for the compressive stress case. Notably, mechanical stress has a more significant influence on conductivity than on relative permittivity. Consequently, the electric field distribution of epoxy insulators under DC is significantly more affected by externally applied mechanical stresses than under AC or overvoltage conditions. These findings emphasize the importance of considering the effect of externally applied stresses on the dielectric properties of insulators when designing them.

articleTitle: A Study of Negative Differential Mobility in Low-Density Polyethylene Based on Kinetic Monte Carlo Analysis with Percolation
abstract: The mobility of low-density polyethylene exhibits a negative electric field dependence in the high electric field region. The negative electric field dependence can be approximated using a Gaussian disorder model which is used to analyze organic materials. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are performed to investigate the mechanism behind the negative differential mobility. The calculation shows that the negative electric field dependence of the mobility becomes stronger when the number of hopping sites in the material decreases.

articleTitle: “Make it Stick” –Influence of Hydrophobicity of Nano Silica Functionalization on Dispersion and Breakdown Performance in BOPP Nanocomposites
abstract: This paper aims to evaluate commercial silica nanoparticles with surface functionalization of different hydrophobicity for BOPP capacitor films using a small-scale production process requiring only a few grams of particles. Therefore, capacitor grade PP and 0.5 wt.% of fumed silica were compounded in a laboratory mixer, hot pressed into plugs and biaxially oriented on a laboratory stretching device. Three commercial particle systems with comparable specific surface area but different surface functionalization (methacrylate silane (MAS), octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane (OMCTS) or dimethyldichlorosilane (DDS)) as well as unfunctionalized silica were investigated. Optical microscopy and scanning electron microscopy showed that dispersion improved greatly with higher hydrophobicity. Interestingly, short-term dielectric strength for OMCTS functionalization was 37 V/µm higher than for the PP reference and 34 V/µm higher than for DDS, although both consisted of the same chemical groups. Long-term voltage endurance was improved for the polar MAS functionalization despite the short-term performance being governed by agglomerates. Therefore, a combination of hydrophobic and hydrophilic groups seems promising.

articleTitle: All-Inorganic Electrical Insulation Systems for High-Power Density Electrical Machines
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of ‘All-Inorganic Electrical Insulation (EI) System’ to enable the next generation of high-power-density electrical machines (EMs) that can operate at extreme conditions, namely high voltages (V) up to 1 kV DC and high temperatures (T) up to 500°C. The feasibility was explored for this concept using experiments and simulations by investigating the inorganic materials adapted to design high-T and high-V EMs. Candidate materials are (i) developed for magnet wire insulation and (ii) selected for a slot filler. In particular, employing physical vapor deposition (PVD), aluminum nitride (AlN) ceramic thin-film coatings were developed on Cu conductors. The experimental results demonstrate very high dielectric breakdown field strength (1 kV/micron for > 90 nm coatings) and thermal conductivity (290 W/m·K at room T (RT), 160 W/m·K at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{T} = 300\ ^\circ \mathrm{C}$</tex>), surpassing existing thin-film insulating materials. Thermal simulations using MotorCAD software compare conventional organic insulation of magnet wires with the AlN coatings. The AlN insulation alone potentially reduces operating T by 6 °C, enhancing EM efficiency. Combining AlN coatings with a selected high thermal conductivity slot filler at 500 °C enables fivefold heat dissipation, boosting potential power density by 50%. These findings demonstrate the potential of all-inorganic EI systems to deliver a step change in high-T EM design for aerospace, traction, and nuclear applications.

articleTitle: Green Developments in Gaseous Insulation Systems
abstract: Climate change, pollution, and limited material resources are some of the most pressing global problems that need to be urgently addressed and will entail a fundamental change in the way modern societies operate. Our community of dielectric and electrical insulation experts has accepted to tackle these challenges and is increasingly working on finding solutions. This Eric O. Forster Memorial Lecture aims to give an introduction into the challenges that we are facing with respect to developing green(er) gaseous insulation systems and to give an overview on current trends in research and development, as well as on achievements of the past decade. The lecture closes by discussing the assessment of green technology and making societal questions explicit that need to be debated in parallel to the technical developments.

articleTitle: Fron Cover
Foreword
